### §204 — investigation + real proof: multi-level string-concatenation and Class<?> parameter propagation to a MongoDB collection name is NOT traced back to the endpoint (user-reported, found directly in real code)

**User's report (paraphrased from their own words)**: a method defines/builds a string, passes it
into a child method, which appends to it and passes it to a third method, which passes it to a
fourth — 3+ levels deep — and only the bottom method uses the fully-built value as a MongoDB
collection name in a real DB call; the analyzer does not capture this. Same complaint for passing a
`.class` literal down a similar chain and deriving the collection name from it at the bottom.

**Step 1 — how collection-name resolution actually works today**, read end to end:
`CollectionResolver.collectCollections` (`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/
CollectionResolver.java`) and `MongoMethodDetector.detect` (same package). Both operate **strictly
per-method, per-call-site** — there is no cross-method data-flow/constant-propagation pass at all.
Concretely:
- A call's collection-name argument is resolved from `InvocationRef.stringArgs()`, which
  `BytecodeClassParser` populates only from `LDC`-loaded literals (or a same-class `GETSTATIC`
  constant resolved inline) seen immediately before the call in the *same* method body
  (`BytecodeClassParser.java` lines ~336–349, ~426–433).
- If the argument is instead an `ALOAD` of a parameter/local (not a literal), the parser records it
  as a `DynamicArgSource` with `kind` = `PARAM` / `LOCAL_VAR` / `FIELD` / `STATIC_FIELD` and just the
  **bare variable name** (lines ~355–380, ~417–450) — it never looks at what the *caller* actually
  passed into that parameter.
- `CollectionResolver.mergeDynamicResult`/`tryResolveDynamicViaEnumConstants` only ever resolves a
  `STATIC_FIELD`-kind dynamic ref, and only via a single-hop lookup into
  `ctx.fieldConstantsMap`/`ctx.enumConstantsMap` (a compile-time constant on some *other* class) —
  never a `PARAM` or `LOCAL_VAR` kind, and never anything requiring walking up the call chain.
- String **concatenation** is resolved only in the single narrow case of `literalOnlySlotValue`
  (`BytecodeClassParser.java` ~358–367): a local slot that was `ASTORE`d from a literal `LDC`
  **exactly once**, with no other store — i.e. `String x = "LIT";` reused later. A `StringBuilder`/
  `+`-concatenation result (`prefix + region`) is never folded back to a literal; it is just another
  non-literal local, captured (if at all) as a bare `LOCAL_VAR` dynamic ref.
- The one and only piece of code that tags a **caller's** call-site value onto a **callee** node is
  `CollectionResolver.tagCallSiteCollection`, and it is hard-restricted to the `BulkWriteCollector`
  `addInsert`/`addUpdate`/`addDelete` pattern specifically (checked in `CallTreeBuilder.buildCallTree`
  right where children are attached) — nothing else gets this treatment.

**Conclusion before writing any test**: the analyzer's tracing goes exactly **one call site deep,
with only a single-assignment-literal or same-class-constant resolution inside that one method** —
it does not follow a parameter back through even one caller, let alone three. Both of the user's
patterns should reproduce as a gap.

**Step 2 — built real, compiled, multi-level test code** (not stubbed `ClassInfo`/`MethodInfo` —
actual `javac`-compiled `.class` files run through the real `BytecodeClassParser` + `CallTreeBuilder`
+ `CollectionResolver`, matching the harness pattern used by other proof passes this session, e.g.
`FieldStoredMethodReferenceGapTest`). Source (scratch, not committed) under
`/private/tmp/claude-502/.../scratchpad/section203/`:

**Pattern A — `srcA/com/example/patterna/`** (4 classes, 4 levels):
- `OrderController.getOrders(@PathVariable String region)` (`@RestController`, `@GetMapping("/orders/{region}")`)
  builds `String prefix = "orders_";` and calls `orderService.fetchOrders(prefix, region)`.
- `OrderService.fetchOrders(String prefix, String region)` calls
  `regionAppender.append(prefix, region)`.
- `RegionAppender.append(String prefix, String region)` **concatenates**
  `String built = prefix + region;` (→ `"orders_east"` at runtime) and calls
  `childRepo.execute(built)`.
- `OrderRepositoryChild.execute(String fullyBuiltCollectionName)` calls
  `mongoTemplate.find(new Query(), Object.class, fullyBuiltCollectionName)` — the real DB call the
  detector recognizes (`MongoMethodDetector.TEMPLATE_METHODS` contains `"find"`,
  `TEMPLATE_OWNERS` contains `"MongoTemplate"`).

**Pattern B — `srcB/com/example/patternb/`** (4 classes, 3 levels of `Class<?>` propagation):
- `InvoiceController.getInvoices()` (`@RestController`, `@GetMapping("/invoices")`) calls
  `invoiceService.fetchInvoices(InvoiceEntity.class)` — passing a `.class` literal, not a string.
  `InvoiceEntity` is deliberately **not** `@Document`-annotated (that path is already handled
  elsewhere; this reproduces the reflection/naming-convention case the user described).
- `InvoiceService.fetchInvoices(Class<?> entityClass)` calls `repoChild.execute(entityClass)`.
- `InvoiceRepoChild.execute(Class<?> entityClass)` derives the collection name via
  `deriveCollectionName` (`"InvoiceEntity"` → strip `"Entity"` → lowercase + `"s"` → `"invoices"`),
  then calls `mongoTemplate.find(new Query(), entityClass, collectionName)`.

`org.springframework.data.mongodb.core.MongoTemplate`/`.query.Query` were not on the module's test
classpath (only `spring-boot-starter-web`, not `spring-boot-starter-data-mongodb`), so minimal stub
classes with the identical FQNs were compiled first and put on the `javac` classpath — this is
sufficient and faithful because the analyzer's detectors only ever read the owner-class name string
out of the bytecode; they never load or reflect on the real Spring Data Mongo classes.

**Step 3 — ran the real analyzer**, via a new JUnit test,
`jar-analyzer-core/src/test/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/Section203MultiLevelPropagationProofTest.java`
(a throwaway proof/demo harness, not a permanent regression test, left in place as a reproducible
artifact): loads every real compiled `.class` file from a directory through the real
`BytecodeClassParser.parseClass(byte[])`, indexes them through the real
`CallTreeBuilder.indexClass`, finds the first indexed endpoint, and calls the real
`CallTreeBuilder.buildCallTree` on it, printing every node's `collectionsAccessed`,
`collectionSources`, `dynamicCollectionRefs`, and `hasDbInteraction`.

Two harness fixes were needed to get the real pipeline running standalone (neither touches
production code): (1) `ResolutionContext.jarArtifactMap` defaults to the null-hostile `Map.of()`,
which NPEs on `getOrDefault(null, …)` for classes with `sourceJar == null` (main-jar classes) — the
test swaps in a plain `HashMap` after `createContext()`; (2) `DomainConfigLoader` needs its
`applyDefaults()` fallback invoked via reflection (same pattern already used by
`MongoTaggingTest`/`EndpointTaggingTest`) since no `domain-config.json` is on the unit-test
classpath.

Compiled twice — once with plain `javac` (no `-g`, no local-variable debug table — a real, common
production-jar shape) and once with `javac -g` (full debug info, the more favorable case for the
analyzer since it can actually name the variables) — to make sure the finding wasn't an artifact of
missing debug info.

**Step 4 — real captured output.** Without `-g` (no variable names available at all):
```
=== §203 PATTERN A PROOF OUTPUT START ===
com.example.patterna.OrderController#getOrders hasDbInteraction=false collectionsAccessed=[] ...
  com.example.patterna.OrderService#fetchOrders hasDbInteraction=false collectionsAccessed=[] ...
    com.example.patterna.RegionAppender#append hasDbInteraction=false collectionsAccessed=[] ...
      com.example.patterna.OrderRepositoryChild#execute hasDbInteraction=true collectionsAccessed=[] collectionSources={} dynamicCollectionRefs=[]
=== §203 PATTERN A PROOF OUTPUT END ===
```
`hasDbInteraction=true` is correctly set on the leaf (the `mongoTemplate.find(...)` call itself is
detected), but `collectionsAccessed` is **completely empty** — not even a placeholder — anywhere in
the tree, and there is no `dynamicCollectionRefs` entry either, because without a local-variable
table the parser cannot even name the `ALOAD`d parameter (`resolveLocalVarName` returns `null`, see
`BytecodeClassParser.java` ~369–377). This is the realistic worst case for many real production
JARs.

With `-g` (full debug info — the *best* case for the analyzer):
```
=== §203 PATTERN A PROOF OUTPUT START ===
com.example.patterna.OrderController#getOrders hasDbInteraction=false collectionsAccessed=[] ...
  com.example.patterna.OrderService#fetchOrders hasDbInteraction=false collectionsAccessed=[] ...
    com.example.patterna.RegionAppender#append hasDbInteraction=false collectionsAccessed=[] ...
      com.example.patterna.OrderRepositoryChild#execute hasDbInteraction=true collectionsAccessed=[] collectionSources={} dynamicCollectionRefs=[{variableName=fullyBuiltCollectionName, varKind=PARAM, pattern=MONGO_TEMPLATE_DYNAMIC, source=MONGO_TEMPLATE, operationType=READ}]
=== §203 PATTERN A PROOF OUTPUT END ===

=== §203 PATTERN B PROOF OUTPUT START ===
com.example.patternb.InvoiceController#getInvoices hasDbInteraction=false collectionsAccessed=[] ...
  com.example.patternb.InvoiceService#fetchInvoices hasDbInteraction=false collectionsAccessed=[] ...
    com.example.patternb.InvoiceRepoChild#execute hasDbInteraction=true collectionsAccessed=[] collectionSources={} dynamicCollectionRefs=[{variableName=collectionName, varKind=LOCAL_VAR, pattern=MONGO_TEMPLATE_DYNAMIC, source=MONGO_TEMPLATE, operationType=READ}]
      com.example.patternb.InvoiceRepoChild#deriveCollectionName hasDbInteraction=false collectionsAccessed=[] ...
=== §203 PATTERN B PROOF OUTPUT END ===
```
Even in this best case, `collectionsAccessed` is **empty at every single node in both trees** — the
real endpoint report (`aggregatedCollections`, the field `EndpointReportBuilder`/the UI reads) would
show **zero collections** for `GET /orders/{region}` and `GET /invoices`, even though both endpoints
demonstrably perform a real, resolvable-at-runtime MongoDB `find()` (`"orders_east"` and `"invoices"`
respectively). All the analyzer surfaces is a bare, un-derived variable name
(`fullyBuiltCollectionName` / `collectionName`) with no indication of what it actually evaluates to
or that it was built from a 3–4-level call chain. Pattern B's `Class<?>` propagation additionally
never even reaches `deriveCollectionName`'s own logic — the detector has no way to know
`mongoTemplate.find`'s 2nd/3rd args came from a `Class<?>` parameter that was itself derived from
another `Class<?>` parameter two levels up; it only sees a `LOCAL_VAR` named `collectionName` at the
call site itself.

**Confirmed: both of the user's real-world findings are genuine, reproducible gaps.** Scope: any
endpoint whose collection name is resolved via **string concatenation across ≥2 method calls**, or
via a **`Class<?>` value threaded through ≥2 method calls** before being turned into a collection
name, will have that DB access either **completely missing** (no debug info) or **present only as an
unresolved bare variable name with zero collection value** (with debug info) in
`aggregatedCollections`/the endpoint report — never the correct resolved name. This is a strictly
narrower, more specific case than §200's field/registry-stored-method-reference gap (which is about
*how a call is reached at all*); this one is about *what value a definitely-reached DB call actually
receives*.

**No fix implemented**, per this task's proof-only scope. A **small, safe fix is plausible but not
attempted**: extend `CollectionResolver.tagCallSiteCollection`'s existing "resolve at the caller's
call site" mechanism (currently hard-restricted to `BulkWriteCollector.addInsert/addUpdate/addDelete`)
to the general case — when a callee node's own `dynamicCollectionRefs` contains a `PARAM`-kind entry,
look at what literal (or single concatenation of literals) the *caller's* corresponding argument
expression actually was at the call site that produced this child, one hop at a time, recursively
up to some small bounded depth (e.g. 3–4, matching the user's report). This is a real, contained
extension of an existing mechanism, not a new subsystem — but it does touch `CallTreeBuilder.java`
(where children are built and tagged) and was explicitly out of scope to implement without stopping
to report back first, per this task's instructions.

**Files added** (not committed, no git in this repo):
`jar-analyzer-core/src/test/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/Section203MultiLevelPropagationProofTest.java`.
Scratch source/compiled classes under `/private/tmp/claude-502/.../scratchpad/section203/` (outside
the repo, both non-`-g` and `-g` compiled variants). Did **not** modify `BytecodeClassParser.java`,
`CallTreeBuilder.java`, `CallGraphIndex.java`, or any other production file. Did not touch
`plsql-parser/*`, `DependencyCrawler.java`,
`EntityProceduresReader`/`EntityTablesReader`/`EntityJoinsReader`, `callGraphViz.js`, or `scope.js`.

**Status: DONE — investigated exactly how far collection-name tracing goes today (one call site,
single-assignment-literal or same-class-constant only, no cross-method data flow at all except the
narrow `BulkWriteCollector` call-site tag), built and ran real multi-level test code for both
user-reported patterns through the real analyzer pipeline, and captured real output proving both are
genuine gaps: the resolved collection name is never recovered, and even the best case (full debug
info) only yields a bare unresolved variable name with an empty `collectionsAccessed`/
`aggregatedCollections`. A small, contained fix approach is identified and recommended, not
implemented.**

## 109. `CALL-*` — collection/DB-attribution call-chain tracing gaps (from §200/§203/§204)

New ID prefix, added to the legend in "How to read a task": **`CALL-*`** — JAR-analyzer call-tree /
collection-resolution tracing (`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/
CollectionResolver.java`, `MongoMethodDetector.java`, `CallTreeBuilder.java`, `CallGraphIndex.java`,
`BytecodeClassParser.java`). None of `DB-*`/`ING-*`/`MID-*`/`UI-*`/`ANA-*`/`INF-*` fit: those are all
scoped to the mongo-storage-mode migration (`SCALE-ARCHITECTURE-PLAN.md`/`MONGO-MODULE-PLAN.md`/
`RELATIONAL-MODEL-PLAN.md`); this work is entirely inside the JAR bytecode analyzer's own
call-tree/collection-attribution engine, a different subsystem with no existing task rows.

**Why these tasks exist**: §200 (investigation), §203 (real compiled-JAR proof of the field-stored
method-reference gap), and §204 (real compiled-JAR proof of the multi-level string-concatenation and
`Class<?>`-propagation gaps) all independently confirmed real, reproducible cases where a genuine
MongoDB DB access is silently missing from `EndpointInfo.getAggregatedCollections()` — the exact field
the endpoint report and UI read — because collection-name/call-chain resolution in this analyzer is
strictly **one call site deep**, with the single existing exception being
`CollectionResolver.tagCallSiteCollection`, hardcoded to the `BulkWriteCollector.addInsert/addUpdate/
addDelete` pattern only (`CollectionResolver.java` line 63, wired in from `CallTreeBuilder.java`
line 896). That one exception already proves the "caller resolves a value at its own call site and
tags it onto the child node it just built" mechanism works end-to-end in this codebase — the plan
below is to generalize it, in small provably-correct increments, rather than invent a new mechanism.

**Existing real regression fixtures to reuse, not reinvent** (both already compiled/proven this
session, kept in place per their own "Status: DONE" notes):
- `jar-analyzer-core/src/test/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/FieldStoredMethodReferenceGapTest.java`
  (§203) — asserts `aggregatedCollections=[]` today for the field-indirection endpoint (`GET /orders`
  via `OrderQueryHandler.loader` set in `<init>`), and `[orders]` for the direct-call control endpoint
  (`GET /orders-direct`).
- `jar-analyzer-core/src/test/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/Section203MultiLevelPropagationProofTest.java`
  (§204, despite the "203" in its filename — written during the §204 investigation) — Pattern A
  (4-level string-concatenation chain into `mongoTemplate.find(..., "orders_" + region)`) and Pattern B
  (3-level `Class<?>` propagation into a derived collection name), both currently asserting empty
  `collectionsAccessed` at every node despite `hasDbInteraction=true` at the leaf.

Every `CALL-*` task below that fixes behavior these tests exercise must **flip the existing assertions
from gap-demonstrating to fixed-and-permanent** (i.e. edit the assertions in these two files to expect
the correct resolved values, not add parallel new test files) — this keeps them as permanent
regression tests going forward, per Rule 2 ("no task is done without its tests") and the explicit
instruction not to throw the §203/§204 proof fixtures away.

| ID | Title | Files | Blocked by | DoD (command → expected) | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**`CALL-006` is deliberately left undefined and its own DoD unwritten** — per §200's own risk
assessment (repeated here because it still holds after seeing the concrete CALL-001..005 shape): this
is genuine points-to/data-flow analysis (which concrete `Map`/`List` instance a variable refers to,
merged across control-flow paths, potentially with runtime-computed keys), not a bounded extension of
the caller-tags-callee mechanism the way CALL-001..005 are. **Recommendation: do not schedule
CALL-006 until someone checks how common the registry/handler-map pattern actually is in the real JARs
this tool analyzes** — building multi-day points-to analysis for a pattern that may be rare in the
target corpus is a poor cost/benefit trade, exactly as §200 concluded. If it is pursued, scope it first
to a compile-time-string-literal-keyed single registry only (no dynamic keys, no loops) before
considering anything more general — and give it its own proof fixture the same way §203/§204 did,
rather than retrofitting the existing two files (this is genuinely a different code shape, not a
variant of the field case).

**Dependency order**: `CALL-001` first (smallest, single-hop, provably correct in isolation) → `CALL-002`
(extends 001's walk to bounded depth, no new resolution logic) → `CALL-003` and `CALL-004` (each adds one
*kind* of value resolution on top of 002's walk; independent of each other, can be done in either order
or in parallel once 002 lands) → `CALL-005` (independent root cause — field/PUTFIELD tracking, not
call-argument tracking — can start any time, does not block on 001-004, sequenced after them here only
because it's the next "field/registry" tier §200 called out as *harder*) → `CALL-007` (final integration
gate, blocked on everything). `CALL-006` is explicitly not scheduled.

### §205 — planning pass: broke §200/§203/§204's three proven gaps into a small, dependency-ordered `CALL-*` task set, reusing the existing proof fixtures as the DoD

**What this pass did**: no source files touched (`CollectionResolver.java`/`MongoMethodDetector.java`/
`CallTreeBuilder.java` are read-only this pass, per the user's explicit instruction that this is
planning only). Read all three prior investigations (§200, §203, §204) plus the two real proof test
files they produced, re-read `CollectionResolver.tagCallSiteCollection`
(`CollectionResolver.java` lines 47–90) and its one call site in `CallTreeBuilder.buildCallTree`
(~lines 889–897) to confirm the exact shape of the one mechanism that already works, and checked for
an existing entity-class → collection-name convention to reuse for the `Class<?>` case — found one:
`AggregationDetector.java` ~line 815, `__class:FQN` → `@Document` collection-name resolution, already
implemented for a different call path (aggregation `$lookup`/`$out` targets), reusable rather than
needing to be built from scratch for `CALL-004`.

**Why this split, not a single task**: `CollectionResolver.tagCallSiteCollection` is currently narrow
in two independent dimensions — (1) it only fires for one hardcoded class's three method names, and
(2) even if generalized, it only looks one call site up. Un-tangling those into `CALL-001` (fix
dimension 1: any parameter, any call site, still one hop) before `CALL-002` (fix dimension 2: walk N
hops) means each increment is independently testable and revertible, matching Rule 1 ("a task is one
sitting") — `CALL-002` alone, without `CALL-001`, would have no caller-side resolution to walk through
multiple hops with; doing them in the opposite order would be backwards. `CALL-003`
(concatenation-folding) and `CALL-004` (`Class<?>`-derivation) are both *value-interpretation* add-ons
on top of the walk `CALL-002` provides — they don't change how far the walk goes, only what it does
with an intermediate value once found — so they're correctly siblings, not sequential, and both are
blocked on `CALL-002` alone. `CALL-005` (field/`PUTFIELD` tracking) is root-cause-independent of all
four — it never involves a call argument at all, only a field write — so it doesn't block on or get
blocked by `CALL-001..004`; it's listed after them here purely because §200 called it the next tier of
difficulty, not because of a real code dependency. `CALL-006` is the one piece this plan does **not**
schedule: after seeing the concrete shape of `CALL-001..005`, the registry/collection-of-references
case remains qualitatively different (data-flow over heap-allocated collection *instances*, not
argument/field values) and the honest assessment is that it should not be built speculatively.

**Test-reuse discipline**: every `CALL-*` DoD above points at the same two files
(`FieldStoredMethodReferenceGapTest.java`, `Section203MultiLevelPropagationProofTest.java`) rather than
inventing new fixtures, and requires editing their existing assertions *in place* from
gap-demonstrating to fixed, so that (a) the exact real-world shapes the user reported stay covered
permanently, and (b) nobody can quietly delete the proof and claim the gap was fixed without rerunning
the exact scenario that demonstrated it. `CALL-002` needs one small addition to
`Section203MultiLevelPropagationProofTest` (an identity/non-concatenating 4-level case) because the
existing Pattern A fixture conflates "does the walk reach 4 levels" with "does concatenation resolve" —
separating those was necessary to give `CALL-002` its own independent, executable DoD distinct from
`CALL-003`'s.

**Status: PLANNING DONE — no implementation attempted. `CALL-001` is startable now.**

### §206 — `CALL-001` implemented: `tagCallSiteCollection` generalized from `BulkWriteCollector`-only to any single-hop parameter, verified with a new proof case plus the full suite

**What changed** — `jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CollectionResolver.java`:
`tagCallSiteCollection` kept its existing `BulkWriteCollector`-specific branch byte-for-byte (same
method-name/owner gate, same tagging logic, same `"BULK_WRITE_COLLECTOR_CALL_SITE"`/
`"BULK_WRITE_COLLECTOR_CALL_SITE_DYNAMIC"` sources) — it is now just the FIRST branch tried, not the
whole method. When it returns null (not a `BulkWriteCollector` call), a new private
`tagGeneralParamCallSite(original, call)` is tried: it looks at the just-built CHILD node's own
`dynamicCollectionRefs` for an entry with `varKind=PARAM` (i.e. `collectCollections`, walking the
callee's own method body, already found that one of its parameters feeds a recognized Mongo
collection-name argument, but couldn't resolve it without knowing the caller's value). If one exists,
it resolves THIS call site's actual argument via a new `MongoMethodDetector.resolveGenericCallSiteArg`
(same literal-then-dynamic resolution order as `resolveBulkCollectorCallSite`, but with no method-
name/owner gate — any call site qualifies once the callee side has already proven it needs one). A
resolved literal is tagged onto a `copyForCallSiteTagging()`'d child with source
`"CALL_SITE_PARAM_PROPAGATION"`, and the now-stale `PARAM` dynamic-ref entries for that same
parameter name are removed (scoped by `variableName`, not a blanket removal, so an unrelated second
dynamic parameter on the same node is left alone). `CallTreeBuilder.java`'s one call site (~line 896)
is untouched — `tagCallSiteCollection`'s signature and contract are unchanged.

**Real bug found and fixed while building the proof fixture, not left latent**: the new one-hop test
class initially failed because the scratch fixture was compiled WITHOUT `-g` (no local-variable
table), so `BytecodeClassParser`'s ALOAD-tracking couldn't recover the parameter's name at all —
recompiling with `-g` fixed the fixture, not the production code (this is a test-harness detail, not
a real analyzer gap; noted here so it isn't rediscovered as a false "regression" later). Separately, a
real duplicate-entry bug in the new code itself was caught by the test: `collectCollections` can
record the SAME parameter as a `PARAM` dynamic ref twice (once at the `getCollection(...)` call, once
via the immediately-chained `find()`/etc. propagation, pattern `NATIVE_DRIVER_CHAINED_DYNAMIC`) —
removing only the first-found entry (by object identity) left a stale second entry on the tagged
node. Fixed by removing every `PARAM` entry matching the same `variableName`, not just the first
match.

**New proof test** (per this task's own DoD, since `Section203MultiLevelPropagationProofTest`'s two
existing cases are both multi-hop and out of scope — see below): added
`call001SingleHopAnyParameterCollectionPropagationIsResolved` to
`FieldStoredMethodReferenceGapTest.java`, plus two new compiled fixture classes
(`ParamController`/`ParamRepositoryChild`, source and `-g`-compiled `.class` under
`scratchpad/fieldgap/`) — `ParamController.listOrdersParam()` calls
`ParamRepositoryChild.execute("orders_param")` directly (one hop, literal argument, no chain), and
`execute(String collectionName)`'s own body only ever sees `collectionName` as a parameter, used as
`db.getCollection(collectionName).find()...`. Real captured output after the fix:
```
=== CALL-001 SINGLE-HOP CASE — REAL CAPTURED OUTPUT ===
aggregatedCollections = [orders_param]
- com.demo.ParamController#listOrdersParam collections=[] hasDbInteraction=false dynamicRefs=[]
  - com.demo.ParamRepositoryChild#execute collections=[orders_param] hasDbInteraction=true dynamicRefs=[]
```
The two pre-existing cases in the same file were re-run unchanged and still pass: the field-indirection
gap case still correctly asserts `aggregatedCollections=[]` (§203's gap is `CALL-005`'s scope, not
touched here), and the direct-call control case still asserts `[orders]`.

**Multi-hop cases in `Section203MultiLevelPropagationProofTest` — re-run, confirmed correctly still
NOT resolved, exactly as this task's scope predicts**: ran both patterns against the real compiled
fixtures still on disk under `scratchpad/section203/outA2`/`outB2` (the `-g` variants).
- **Pattern A** (`OrderController`→`OrderService`→`RegionAppender`→`OrderRepositoryChild`, 4 levels,
  string built by concatenation): still `collectionsAccessed=[]` at every node, with the leaf
  (`OrderRepositoryChild#execute`) carrying an unresolved `dynamicCollectionRefs` entry
  (`variableName=fullyBuiltCollectionName, varKind=PARAM`). This is CORRECT for CALL-001 alone:
  `tagCallSiteCollection` only fires at the immediate caller (`RegionAppender`→`execute`), and
  `RegionAppender`'s own call passes ITS OWN parameter (not a literal) into `execute` — resolving that
  requires walking one more hop up into `OrderService`, which is `CALL-002`'s job, not this one's.
- **Pattern B** (`InvoiceController`→`InvoiceService`→`InvoiceRepoChild`, `Class<?>` propagation):

  `deriveCollectionName()` method-call return value assigned to a local, not a parameter at all) —
  this shape isn't even `PARAM`-kind, so it was never in scope for CALL-001 regardless; it needs
  `CALL-004`'s `Class<?>`-derivation resolution once `CALL-002` provides the walk.
Both are the honest, predicted-in-advance outcome — no assertion in this file was touched, since it
has no assertions yet (print-only harness per §204's original scope) and neither existing pattern is
a false claim of being fixed.

**Full suite**: `mvn -o -pl jar-analyzer-core test` → `Tests run: 392, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped:
11` — `BUILD SUCCESS`. No regressions in any `BulkWriteCollector`/`MongoTaggingTest`/
`CollectionAggregationEdgeCaseTest`/`CallTreeExpansionBudgetTest`/`SqlJpaTaggingTest` or any other
existing suite.

**What's explicitly still out of scope** (unchanged from §205's plan, not attempted here):
multi-hop walking beyond the immediate caller (`CALL-002`); resolving string concatenation
(`literal + param`) as part of that walk (`CALL-003`); `Class<?>`-to-collection-name derivation
(`CALL-004`); field-stored method references / `PUTFIELD` tracking (`CALL-005`, independent root
cause); the registry/collection-of-references case (`CALL-006`, deliberately unscheduled). This
task's own mechanism is also, by design, position-agnostic (first-`PARAM`-match, mirroring the
pre-existing `BulkWriteCollector` mechanism's own semantics) rather than doing exact parameter-index
matching between the call site's arguments and the callee's declared parameter list — sufficient for
every real case seen so far (a callee with one dynamic collection-name parameter), but a callee with
TWO independently-dynamic collection-name parameters resolved from two differently-valued call-site
arguments could in principle be tagged with the wrong one; no such case has been observed and none of

### §207 — `CALL-005` implemented: field-stored method references (single field, constructor-assigned) now redirect to their real target, mirroring `injectedFields`'s per-class map pattern

**What changed** — three files, each a small, additive change:
- `jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/model/FieldAccessInfo.java`: added
  `lambdaTargetClass`/`lambdaTargetMethod`/`lambdaTargetDescriptor` (nullable, naming mirrors
  `MethodCallInfo`'s existing lambda-target fields) — set only when a field write directly
  consumes an invokedynamic's result.
- `jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/BytecodeClassParser.java`: added three
  `pendingLambdaTarget*` locals (same pattern as the file's existing `pendingReceiverField`/
  `pendingChainedCollectionArg` pending-state variables). The `InvokeDynamicInsnNode` branch now
  stashes the resolved handle's owner/name/descriptor into these locals right after building the
  synthetic lambda `MethodCallInfo` (previously it only ever appended that `MethodCallInfo` to
  `mi.getInvocations()` and moved on). The `FieldInsnNode` branch, at the point it already builds
  each access's `FieldAccessInfo`, now checks: if a lambda target is pending AND this access is
  `PUTFIELD`/`PUTSTATIC`, stamp the three new fields onto this `FieldAccessInfo`. The pending
  locals are cleared immediately after (consumed or not), and separately cleared at the top of the
  `MethodInsnNode` branch, so a method call intervening between the invokedynamic and a *later*
  field store correctly breaks the association (this task's scope is deliberately the direct
  `this.field = x::method;` shape only — the JVM naturally emits the `PUTFIELD` as the instruction
  immediately following the `invokedynamic` for that shape, so no field ever needs a lookahead to
  detect it).
- `jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CallGraphIndex.java`: added
  `FieldLambdaInfo` (record: `fieldName, targetClass, targetMethod, targetDescriptor`) and
  `IndexedClass.fieldLambdaTargets` (`Map<String, FieldLambdaInfo>`), populated by a new loop at
  the end of `IndexedClass`'s constructor — scans every method's `FieldAccessInfo` list for a
  `PUT`/`PUT_STATIC` entry with a non-null `lambdaTargetClass` and `ownerClass` matching `this.fqn`,
  and records `fieldName -> FieldLambdaInfo`. Deliberately placed and shaped exactly like the
  existing `injectedFields` map (same per-class, per-field-name, `LinkedHashMap` construction) per
  this task's instruction to mirror that pattern, not invent a new one.
- `jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CallTreeBuilder.java`: in
  `buildCallTree`'s per-invocation loop, right before the existing "Lambda / method reference
  resolution" block (`call.isLambdaInvocation() && call.lambdaTargetClass() != null`), added a

  immediately followed by the consuming `INVOKEINTERFACE`/`INVOKEVIRTUAL`), look up

  target class/method/descriptor locals are populated from the `FieldLambdaInfo` instead of the

  abstract dispatch fallback, synthetic-lambda vs. method-reference dispatch-type labeling, the

### §208 — `CALL-002` implemented: `tagCallSiteCollection`'s single-hop mechanism extended to a bounded (N=4) multi-hop walk up the ancestor call chain, verified with a new 3-hop pure-pass-through proof case

**What changed** — `jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CallTreeBuilder.java`:
the private `buildCallTree` overload gained a new trailing parameter, `List<InvocationRef>
ancestorCallChain` — the call sites (nearest ancestor first) that produced the CURRENT stack
frame, i.e. the call that invoked the method currently being built, then the call that invoked
THAT caller, and so on. This falls naturally out of the existing top-down recursion: every
recursive `buildCallTree(...)` call site (the interface-dispatch lambda-resolution branch, the
direct lambda/method-reference branch, the method-reference-to-interface fallback branch, and the
main resolved-method branch) now passes `extendAncestorChain(ancestorCallChain, call)` — a new
small private helper that prepends the CURRENT call site onto the chain already accumulated for
this frame, capped at `CollectionResolver.MAX_HOP_DEPTH - 1` entries. The two public `buildCallTree`
overloads (root entry points) seed this with `List.of()`. `connectEventListeners`'s own recursive
call (Spring event-listener dispatch — a fundamentally different call shape, the listener receives
an event object, not the publisher's own parameters) deliberately starts a FRESH empty chain rather
than threading the publisher's, since forwarding it would conflate two unrelated data-flow shapes.
The one call site that tags collections (`collectionResolver.tagCallSiteCollection(child, call,
ancestorCallChain)`) now passes this chain through.

`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CollectionResolver.java`:
`tagCallSiteCollection`/`tagGeneralParamCallSite` both gained the same trailing `ancestorCallChain`
parameter (the `BulkWriteCollector`-specific branch inside `tagCallSiteCollection` is untouched —
this task's walk-up extension applies only to the CALL-001 general-parameter path, per the task's
own instruction to reuse `tagGeneralParamCallSite`/`resolveGenericCallSiteArg` as the base case).
A new named constant, `static final int MAX_HOP_DEPTH = 4`, replaces what would otherwise be a bare
magic number anywhere the bound is checked. A new private helper, `resolveAcrossHops(call,
ancestorCallChain)`, is the actual walk: it calls `mongoMethodDetector.resolveGenericCallSiteArg`
on the call site being tagged (hop 1); if that result is specifically "unresolved AND the
dynamic-arg kind is `PARAM`" (i.e. the immediate caller is itself just forwarding a value it
received as ITS OWN parameter, not supplying a literal/constant) — and only in that exact case —
it retries the SAME `resolveGenericCallSiteArg` call against the next ancestor in the chain, one
hop at a time, until either a literal/constant is found, a result comes back that ISN'T an
unresolved `PARAM` pass-through (nothing further up this mechanism could improve on that), the
`MAX_HOP_DEPTH` bound is hit, or the ancestor chain runs out (a real call chain shallower than the
bound) — whichever comes first. No unbounded recursion is possible: the loop is a plain bounded
`while`, and `CallTreeBuilder` is solely responsible for capping how many ancestors it ever threads
down, so a pathologically deep real call tree cannot make the chain (or the walk) grow past the
bound no matter how deep the actual recursion goes.

**New proof test, isolating CALL-002's own scope**: `Section203MultiLevelPropagationProofTest`'s
existing Pattern A (the task's suggested primary fixture) turned out — confirmed by re-running it
below — to NOT be a clean CALL-002-only fixture: its 4-level chain concatenates a literal prefix
with a runtime `region` parameter (`prefix + region`) at the `RegionAppender` level before passing
the result down, so the value arriving at `OrderRepositoryChild#execute`'s call site is a
`LOCAL_VAR` (the concatenation's result), never a bare `PARAM` pass-through — CALL-002's walk-up
condition is deliberately narrow (`PARAM`-kind only) and does not fire for it, correctly, since
folding a concatenation is explicitly CALL-003's separate job. Per this task's own explicit
fallback instruction, a NEW fixture was written instead to isolate pure multi-hop pass-through:
`HopController.listOrdersHop()` calls `HopServiceA.callA("orders_hop")` (a LITERAL at the top),
which forwards its own parameter UNCHANGED into `HopServiceB.callB(collectionName)`, which forwards
ITS OWN parameter UNCHANGED into `HopRepoLeaf.execute(collectionName)`, whose own body uses the
parameter as a Mongo collection-name argument — 3 intermediate hops between the literal and its
real use, no concatenation, no `Class<?>` derivation anywhere in the chain. Added as
`call002ThreeHopPureParameterPassThroughChainIsResolved` in the same
`FieldStoredMethodReferenceGapTest.java` file as the CALL-001 proof (new compiled fixture classes
`HopController`/`HopServiceA`/`HopServiceB`/`HopRepoLeaf`, source and `-g`-compiled `.class` under

```

- com.demo.HopController#listOrdersHop collections=[] hasDbInteraction=false dynamicRefs=[]
  - com.demo.HopServiceA#callA collections=[] hasDbInteraction=false dynamicRefs=[]
```

Walked exactly 3 hops to find the literal (leaf's own call site → `PARAM` unresolved; `HopServiceA`

### §209 — `CALL-003` implemented: narrow, safe `literal + param`/`param + literal` string-concatenation folding, verified with three new proof cases; §204 Pattern A confirmed still unresolved (correctly, for a reason narrower than §208 predicted)

**What changed** — this codebase's bytecode reading is ASM-based, and real compiled fixtures
confirmed `+` string concatenation on this target JDK level compiles to `invokedynamic` bootstrapped
through `java.lang.invoke.StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants`, in TWO distinct shapes
depending on whether javac could fold an operand into the bootstrap's own recipe string: (a) both
operands dynamic → the invokedynamic descriptor takes 2 `String` args, nothing in the recipe; (b) one
operand is a compile-time constant → javac embeds it directly into the recipe (a `U+0001` placeholder
marks the single remaining dynamic operand's position), so the descriptor takes only 1 `String` arg.
A fully-literal concatenation (`"orders_" + "east"`) is constant-folded away by javac entirely before
either shape is even emitted — confirmed via `javap`, so that trivial case was already handled by the
existing plain-`LDC` mechanism and needed no new code. The old `StringBuilder.append`-chain shape
(pre-Java-9 javac output) is never produced by this codebase's own build target and was not
implemented — `tryFoldStringConcat`'s docs note this explicitly.

`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/BytecodeClassParser.java`: the existing
ASTORE pre-scan (which already builds `literalOnlySlotValue`/`astoreCountBySlot`/
`slotEverStoredFromNonLiteral` for the single-literal case) was extended, additively, with a new
`concatSlotValue` map and a small sliding "operand window" (`List<Object>`, capped at 2 entries) that
only survives a genuinely-adjacent run of `LDC`-string/`ALOAD`-of-parameter pushes — any other
instruction (a method call, field access, branch, etc.) clears it, so a stale non-adjacent push can
never be mistaken for a real operand. A new `tryFoldStringConcat` helper recognizes the
`StringConcatFactory` bootstrap in both descriptor shapes above and returns either a fully-resolved
literal (both operands constant) or a `ConcatSlotInfo` (`literalPart`, `literalFirst`, `paramName`) for
the narrow `literal + param`/`param + literal` case — anything else (3+ original operands, e.g.
`"a" + x + "b"`; two non-constant operands; an escaped-constant `U+0002` in the recipe; ambiguous
window state) returns null, leaving the pre-existing unresolved behavior untouched. The live
ALOAD-tracking loop (the one that already special-cases a fully-resolved single-assignment literal
slot) gained one new `else if` branch: a single-assignment slot with a `concatSlotValue` entry now
reports a `MethodCallInfo.DynamicArgSource` with kind `CONCAT_LITERAL_PARAM` or
`CONCAT_PARAM_LITERAL` (repurposing the existing `ownerClass` field to carry the literal text, the
same repurposing pattern `STATIC_FIELD` already uses for its owner class) instead of a bare
`LOCAL_VAR`. No change to `MethodCallInfo`'s persisted shape was needed or made — this was a deliberate
constraint given that file's own documented concern about `invocations` being 31-78% of `analysis.json`.

`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CollectionResolver.java`: a new
`foldConcatIfPossible(csc, ancestorCallChain)` runs after CALL-002's `resolveAcrossHops` inside
`tagGeneralParamCallSite`. It deliberately does **not** reuse `resolveGenericCallSiteArg`'s existing
"first dynamic arg wins" simplification for the PARAM side of a concat — with TWO of a callee's own
parameters forwarded unchanged at the same call site (a real shape — see §204 Pattern A's
`regionAppender.append(prefix, region)`), picking "whichever came first" could fold in the WRONG
sibling parameter's value and fabricate an incorrect collection name, which this task's own
instructions explicitly forbid. Instead it only ever trusts an ancestor call site when it is
UNAMBIGUOUS: exactly one distinct literal argument and no dynamic ones (resolves immediately by
concatenating), or exactly one dynamic argument and no literal ones AND that argument is itself an
unresolved `PARAM` pass-through (keeps walking, up to `MAX_HOP_DEPTH` total). Any other shape at an
ancestor (zero or 2+ candidates of either kind, a literal+dynamic mix, or a resolved-but-non-literal
single dynamic candidate) stops the walk and returns the ORIGINAL, still-unresolved `csc` — never
guesses. (One real wrinkle found and handled during verification: the SAME single-assignment literal
ALOAD can be captured twice — once by the generic every-`LDC` scan, once more by the literal-slot
resolution path — a pre-existing, harmless quirk elsewhere in this file's own capture pipeline; the
ambiguity check uses `distinct().count() == 1`, not raw list size, so this duplicate never reads as a
false ambiguity.) A resolved fold is tagged with a new `collectionSources` value,
`CALL_SITE_CONCAT_PROPAGATION`, distinct from CALL-001/002's `CALL_SITE_PARAM_PROPAGATION`, so callers
can tell the two mechanisms apart.

**Three new proof cases**, added to `FieldStoredMethodReferenceGapTest.java` (same real-compiled-
bytecode harness as CALL-001/002/005's own cases; new fixture classes `ConcatEntryController`/
`ConcatService`/`ConcatRepoLeaf`/`LiteralConcatController`/`NegativeConcatController`, source and
`javac -g`-compiled `.class` under `scratchpad/fieldgap/`):
- `call003LiteralPlusParamConcatenationIsResolved` — `ConcatEntryController.handle()` assigns
  `String region = "east";` (resolves via the existing single-assignment mechanism) then calls
  `svc.fetchOrders(region)`; `ConcatService.fetchOrders(String region)` builds
  `"orders_" + region` and forwards it into `ConcatRepoLeaf.execute(...)`. **Real captured output**:
  `aggregatedCollections = [orders_east]` — the narrow shape folds end-to-end.
- `call003FullyLiteralConcatenationAlreadyResolvedByJavac` — `"orders_" + "east"`, confirmed via
  `javap` to be constant-folded by javac before this analyzer ever sees an `invokedynamic`; a
  baseline/sanity case, not a new code path. **Real captured output**: `aggregatedCollections =
  [orders_east]`.
- `call003TwoNonConstantOperandsCorrectlyStaysUnresolved` — `prefix + region`, concatenating a
  method's OWN two parameters (neither a literal in that method's own context) — outside CALL-003's
  narrow scope. **Real captured output**: `aggregatedCollections = []` — correctly falls back to an
  unresolved dynamic reference, never fabricates a name.

All 4 pre-existing tests in the same file (CALL-001's, CALL-002's, and CALL-005's proof cases, plus
the direct-call control case) were re-run unchanged and still pass — 7/7 in that file.

**`Section203MultiLevelPropagationProofTest` (§204 Pattern A) re-run — real captured output, honestly
still unresolved, for a reason narrower than §208 predicted**:
```
com.example.patterna.OrderRepositoryChild#execute hasDbInteraction=true collectionsAccessed=[]
  dynamicCollectionRefs=[{variableName=fullyBuiltCollectionName, varKind=PARAM, ...}]  (outA2, the -g variant)
```
§208 framed the remaining gap as "the concatenation result is `LOCAL_VAR`-kind, not `PARAM`, so
CALL-002's walk never triggers — CALL-003 is required." That framing turns out to be imprecise once
CALL-003's own narrow definition is applied literally: `RegionAppender.append(String prefix, String
region)` computes `String built = prefix + region;`, where **neither `prefix` nor `region` is a
literal/constant in `RegionAppender`'s own context** — both are `RegionAppender`'s own, unresolved
parameters (`prefix` only becomes the literal `"orders_"` two hops further up, at `OrderController`).
CALL-003's task definition requires "AT LEAST ONE operand resolvable as a literal/constant in the
CURRENT METHOD's own context" — Pattern A's concat has ZERO such operands at the method that performs
the concatenation, so `tryFoldStringConcat` correctly returns null for it (the "both non-literal"
branch — the same branch the new negative test exercises), and the value is captured as a plain,
unresolved `LOCAL_VAR`, exactly as it was before this task. Nothing in the walk ever gets a chance to
run. This is a narrower miss than §208's own description implied: it is not that CALL-003 walks up
and gives up on the unresolvable `region`; CALL-003 never engages with this concatenation at all,
because the OTHER operand (`prefix`) is not locally literal either — it is itself only resolvable via
a SEPARATE upward walk (CALL-002's own mechanism), a two-stage combination ("resolve one concat
operand via the ancestor walk FIRST, THEN treat it as literal for folding purposes") that is a natural
extension of CALL-003 but is not what its own scope, as literally written, covers. Implementing it
would mean chasing each of a concatenation's TWO operands up the ancestor chain independently before
attempting the fold, compounding the same ambiguity-safety bookkeeping `foldConcatIfPossible` already
does for one operand — a real, larger, and explicitly out-of-scope expansion, not attempted here.

**Pattern A is therefore NOT closed by CALL-003 — confirmed honestly, not forced.** It remains exactly
as unresolved as before this task, for a documented, narrower-than-expected reason. Pattern B (the

confirmed unchanged: `InvoiceRepoChild#execute` still shows a `LOCAL_VAR`-kind dynamic ref from
`deriveCollectionName()`'s return value.

### §210 — `CALL-004` implemented: `Class<?>` propagation into a MongoDB collection name, resolved for the `@Document`-annotated case (direct call site AND propagated through 2+ hops), reusing the existing `entityCollectionMap` `@Document`→collection-name lookup; non-annotated naming-convention case deliberately left unimplemented

**What changed.** §204 Pattern B identified two related gaps: (a) a `Class<?>` value threaded
through 2+ method calls before being used to derive a Mongo collection name, and (b) the specific
non-annotated naming-convention derivation (`InvoiceEntity` → strip `"Entity"` → lowercase + `"s"`
→ `"invoices"`) used by that fixture's `deriveCollectionName()` helper. This task closes (a) for the
higher-confidence `@Document`-annotated sub-case only, per §205's own plan ("implement (b) only if
(a) alone doesn't cover the fixture... don't invent a naming heuristic from scratch").

**Root cause, confirmed by reading `BytecodeClassParser.java`'s ALOAD-tracking loop**: the dynamic-arg
capture path only ever calls `resolveLocalVarName(method, slot, requireStringType=true, site)` —
a `Class<?>`-typed parameter/local ALOAD (e.g. an entity class forwarded unchanged through a service
method before being used at a `mongoTemplate.find(query, entityClass)` call site) failed that String-type
check and was silently dropped: no `dynamicCollectionRefs` entry at all, not even an unresolved one.
This is a narrower, earlier-stage gap than Pattern A's (which at least produces an unresolved
`LOCAL_VAR`/`PARAM` ref); Pattern B's own captured output in §204/§209 confirms this
("`InvoiceRepoChild#execute` ... never even reaches `deriveCollectionName`'s own logic").

**`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/BytecodeClassParser.java`**: added
`isClassDesc(desc)` (mirrors `isStringDesc`) and a new `resolveLocalVarNameClassTyped(method, slot,
site)` — the same slot-reuse-safe, `[start,end)`-range-checked resolution as the existing 4-arg
`resolveLocalVarName`, but requiring the local-variable-table entry's declared type be exactly
`java.lang.Class` instead of `String`. Deliberately a separate method (not a parameterized version of
the existing one) to keep the already-verified CALL-001/002/003/005 String path completely untouched.
Wired in as a new `else` branch in the ALOAD-tracking loop: when the String-typed resolution attempt
returns null, a second attempt checks for a Class-typed variable and, if found, records a
`MethodCallInfo.DynamicArgSource` with a NEW kind — `PARAM_CLASS` (parameter) or `LOCAL_VAR_CLASS`
(local) — distinct from the existing `PARAM`/`LOCAL_VAR` String kinds so downstream resolvers can
never confuse a propagated Class reference with a propagated String.

**`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CollectionResolver.java`**: `tagCallSiteCollection`
gained an overloaded 4-arg form taking the `ResolutionContext ctx` (needed for `ctx.entityCollectionMap`
— the SAME map `resolveRepositoryCollections`/`AggregationDetector`/`MongoMethodDetector` already read
for the direct-call `@Document` case, built from `IndexedClass.documentCollection` during indexing; no
new map, no new population logic). `tagGeneralParamCallSite` now also looks for a `PARAM_CLASS`-kind
entry in the callee's own `dynamicCollectionRefs` when no plain `PARAM` entry is found, and if present
calls a new `resolveClassAcrossHops(call, ancestorCallChain, entityCollectionMap)`: at each call site
(the original, then up through `ancestorCallChain`, bounded at the SAME `MAX_HOP_DEPTH = 4` CALL-002
already uses), it checks for either (i) a direct `__class:FQN` literal argument (a `.class` literal
passed at that hop) — resolved immediately via `resolveEntityFqnToCollection` (FQN lookup, then simple-
name fallback — identical shape to `AggregationDetector.resolveClassLiteralCollection`'s own lookup
against the same map, reused conceptually rather than duplicated as a new subsystem), or (ii) another
unresolved `PARAM_CLASS` pass-through — keep walking; anything else stops the walk unresolved (never
guesses). A resolved fold is tagged with a new `collectionSources` value, `CALL_SITE_CLASS_PROPAGATION`,
distinct from CALL-001/002/003's own values, so callers can tell the Class-propagation mechanism apart
from the String ones.

**`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CallTreeBuilder.java`**: the single call site
(`buildCallTree`, ~line 941) now passes `ctx` (already an instance field on `CallTreeBuilder`) into the
new 4-arg `tagCallSiteCollection` overload.

- `ConcatSlotInfo` (private record) gained an optional 4th field, `paramName2` — non-null only for
  this new `param + param` shape; `literalPart`/`literalFirst` stay unused for it.
- `tryFoldStringConcat`'s 2-operand branch now also matches `ParamOperand + ParamOperand`, emitting a
  new `CONCAT_PARAM_PARAM` dynamic-arg kind (`DynamicArgSource(kind="CONCAT_PARAM_PARAM",
  name=<operand1>, ownerClass=<operand2>)` — `ownerClass` repurposed to carry the second operand's
  name, the SAME repurposing pattern `STATIC_FIELD`/`CONCAT_LITERAL_PARAM` already use).
- `CollectionResolver` gained `foldTwoParamConcatIfPossible` alongside the existing (unmodified)
  `foldConcatIfPossible`: walks `ancestorCallChain` and, at each hop, tracks BOTH operand names
  independently — matching a hop's dynamic `PARAM` args to whichever of the two names is still
  unresolved (by NAME, never by guessed position, except the one narrow, safe exception below), and
  resolving the OTHER operand to that hop's literal by elimination when the shape is unambiguous
  (exactly the still-forwarded name(s) present in `dynamicArgSources`, zero unaccounted literals).
  One additional narrow rule was needed beyond by-name matching: when a hop has ZERO dynamic args and
  EXACTLY TWO distinct literal args (both operands resolve at the SAME hop, so there is no dynamic
  name left to disambiguate by), bytecode argument push order is trusted positionally — the only
  remaining safe signal once every other disambiguating signal is exhausted.
- **Never fabricates**: when one operand's own ancestor chain runs out (the exact §204 Pattern A
  case — `region` originates at an `@PathVariable` on the endpoint method itself, a genuine
  runtime-only value with NO literal anywhere in the compiled code) while the OTHER operand DOES
  resolve, the result is an honest PARTIAL fold: `resolvedLiteral + "{" + stillUnresolvedName + "}"`
  (e.g. `"orders_" + "{region}"` → `"orders_{region}"`) — the resolvable part reported, an explicit,
  visibly-a-placeholder marker for the genuinely-unknowable part, never a guessed runtime value.
  Any other ambiguous shape at any hop (an unrelated third dynamic arg, a non-`PARAM` kind, a
  dynamic name matching neither still-unresolved operand) immediately returns the ORIGINAL,
  still-unresolved `csc` — same "refuse to guess" contract every other mechanism in this file
  already follows.

**Part B — non-`@Document` naming-convention heuristic (§210's own exact residual, §204 Pattern B).**
`CollectionResolver.resolveClassAcrossHops` previously returned `null` whenever the propagated
`Class<?>`'s FQN had no `@Document`-annotation entry in `ctx.entityCollectionMap`. Fixed by adding a
fallback, `deriveCollectionNameByNamingConvention`, that fires ONLY when the annotation lookup itself
returns null: strip a common entity-class suffix using the EXACT SAME regex this file already applies
elsewhere for the analogous JPA-repository case
(`resolveRepositoryCollections`'s existing `entitySimple.replaceAll("(Entity|Document|Model|Dto|DO)$",
"")` — reused verbatim, not reinvented), lowercase the simple class name, then apply a small,
deliberately-not-a-library pluralization (`+s`, or `+es` after s/x/z/ch/sh, or `y → ies` after a
consonant+`y`). A new `ClassResolution(String collectionName, String source)` record now threads back
WHICH mechanism resolved a `Class<?>`-derived name — `CALL_SITE_CLASS_PROPAGATION` for the
pre-existing, confirmed `@Document` match, `CALL_SITE_CLASS_NAMING_HEURISTIC` for this new,
lower-confidence guess — so `collectionSources` always reflects the true confidence, matching the
provenance-tagging pattern `CALL-004`/§210 already established for this exact distinction. The
`ctx.entityCollectionMap == null || isEmpty()` early-return guard in `tagGeneralParamCallSite` was
relaxed to only require `ctx != null` — the naming heuristic needs no `@Document` ground truth at all,
so it must still fire even in a codebase with ZERO `@Document`-annotated classes.

### §214 — investigation only (no fixes, per this task's own scope): same class of "same-method-literal-only, zero cross-method value tracing" gap checked across JDBC/SQL, HTTP/external-call, and every other `*Detector.java` in `jar-analyzer-core` — confirmed present and, in most cases, EVEN NARROWER than the pre-`CALL-001` MongoDB case (zero dynamic-arg capture at all, not even a same-hop attempt)

**User's ask**: "list any other possible issue of same type" — beyond MongoDB collection-name
resolution, does this analyzer have the SAME class of gap (a value needing cross-method/field tracing
to correctly attribute a DB/external-call target to an endpoint) anywhere else? Investigated by
reading real code, not guessing.

**1. JDBC/SQL table names / query strings — `JpaMethodDetector.java` — CONFIRMED, real, and WORSE than
pre-`CALL-001` Mongo.** Read the whole file end to end: every extraction path
(`extractFromSqlArgs`/`extractProcedureFromArgs`/`extractProceduresFromSqlArgs`/the inline
`JdbcTemplate`/`EntityManager`/`@Query`/derived-query blocks, lines ~197–390) reads EXCLUSIVELY from
`InvocationRef.stringArgs()` — the already-literal-resolved list. `grep -c "dynamicArgSources"
JpaMethodDetector.java` → **0 occurrences**. This detector never even LOOKS at a `PARAM`/`LOCAL_VAR`
dynamic-arg source, let alone attempts to resolve one — meaning a SQL string or table name passed
into a `jdbcTemplate.query(...)`/`entityManager.createQuery(...)` call as a parameter (built or
forwarded from ANY caller, even one hop up) is silently dropped with **no dynamicCollectionRefs entry
at all** — not even the bare unresolved marker Mongo's pre-`CALL-001` state at least left behind. This
is confirmed the SAME class of gap as `CALL-001..004`'s own scope, just one tier more severe (zero
single-hop capture, not merely zero multi-hop/concat/Class-derivation).

**2. HTTP endpoint path variables / external API call targets — `CallTreeBuilder.createHttpCallLeaf`
(the actual RestTemplate/WebClient/FeignClient detector; `ExternalApiLinkService.java` was read
READ-ONLY per this task's instructions and turned out to be a DIFFERENT, later stage — cross-JAR
LINKING of already-resolved call sites to other JARs' endpoints, not itself a detector) — CONFIRMED,
real, and equally severe.** `createHttpCallLeaf` (`CallTreeBuilder.java` ~lines 1581–1618) resolves
the target URL/path via `firstUrlLikeArg(call.stringArgs())` — THIS call site's own already-literal
args only — with a same-method-literal-scan fallback (`callerMethod.stringLiterals`) for chained/
dynamic call sites, and NOTHING else. No `dynamicArgSources()` read anywhere in this method. A URL
built by concatenation, forwarded as a parameter from a caller, or assembled via a `@Value`-injected
host + a path parameter (an extremely common real-world Feign/RestTemplate pattern) resolves to
`targetPath == null` — `node.getHttpTargetPath()` stays unset, with **no diagnostic trace at all**
that a real HTTP call happened with an unresolved target (the node still gets `CallType=HTTP_CALL`
and a resolved HTTP verb, so `hasDbInteraction`-style downstream logic doesn't even flag it as
"attempted but unresolved" the way Mongo's dynamicCollectionRefs marker does).

**3. Every other `*Detector.java` resolving a String/Class argument at a call site — CONFIRMED, same
severity as #1/#2.** `grep -c "dynamicArgSources\|DynamicArgSource"` returns **0** for
`RedisMethodDetector.java`, `CassandraMethodDetector.java`, `ElasticsearchMethodDetector.java`, and
`MyBatisMethodDetector.java` — i.e. of the eight detectors `CollectionResolver.collectCollections`
wires together, `MongoMethodDetector`/`AggregationDetector` are the ONLY two `CollectionResolver`'s
own `tagGeneralParamCallSite`/`resolveAcrossHops`/`foldConcatIfPossible`/`resolveClassAcrossHops`
machinery can do anything with — every other backend (JDBC, Redis, Cassandra, Elasticsearch, MyBatis)
is, today, permanently same-method-literal-only with no exceptions, by construction of their own
detector code, independent of anything `CollectionResolver` does or could do.

**4. Verdict per gap — real, and NOT "basically free" to fix; each needs bespoke detection-layer work
first, not just wiring into the existing mechanism.** `CollectionResolver`'s CALL-001/002/003/004/008
machinery is built entirely around `CallNode.collectionsAccessed`/`collectionSources`/
`dynamicCollectionRefs` and `DynamicArgSource`'s `PARAM`/`PARAM_CLASS`/`CONCAT_*` kinds — REUSABLE in
principle (the bounded ancestor-chain walk, the concat-fold, the Class-derivation-with-heuristic-
fallback pattern are all generic techniques, not Mongo-specific), but NONE of it can fire until each
target detector/call-site builder FIRST does what `BytecodeClassParser`'s ALOAD-tracking already does

### §215 — `CALL-009` implemented: JDBC/SQL table-name resolution brought up to the same cross-method value-tracing capability level `CALL-001..008` already built for MongoDB collection names

**Scope**: §214 found `JpaMethodDetector.java` reads only `inv.stringArgs()`, never
`inv.dynamicArgSources()` — zero single-hop dynamic-arg capture, let alone the multi-hop/concat/
Class-derivation machinery Mongo has. This task closes that gap for JDBC/SQL table-name detection:
single-hop caller-arg resolution, bounded multi-hop (reusing `CollectionResolver.MAX_HOP_DEPTH`),
narrow `literal + param`/`param + literal` SQL-string concat-folding, and `Class<?>`-to-table
naming-convention derivation across hops (the `@Table`/`@Entity`-confirmed tier already existed
pre-`CALL-009` via `ctx.entityTableMap`/`ic.jpaTableName` for the DIRECT-call case; this task adds
propagation of that Class value ACROSS hops, naming-heuristic tier only — see residual gap below).

**Architecture decision: parallel resolver logic inside `CollectionResolver.java`/`JpaMethodDetector.java`,
NOT a generalization of the Mongo mechanism.** JDBC's traced value is a raw SQL STRING that must
still be parsed (`SqlStatementParser.extractTableNames`/`inferOperationType`) for its table name(s)
once resolved to a literal — Mongo's traced value already IS the collection name, used as-is. That
extra post-resolution step is a real structural difference, not just a naming one; folding it into
the existing Mongo-shaped methods would mean threading a "how do I turn a resolved value into a
reportable name" strategy parameter through `tagGeneralParamCallSite`/`resolveAcrossHops`/
`foldConcatIfPossible`/`resolveClassAcrossHops`, a materially bigger and riskier refactor than this
session's own established small-increment discipline calls for. Instead: new sibling private
methods in `CollectionResolver.java` (`tagGeneralSqlCallSite`, `resolveSqlAcrossHops`,
`foldSqlConcatIfPossible`, `tagSqlClassCallSite`, `deriveTableNameByNamingConvention`) alongside the
existing Mongo ones, reusing the same `MAX_HOP_DEPTH` constant, the same `CallNode.
dynamicCollectionRefs`/`copyForCallSiteTagging` plumbing, and the same generic, domain-agnostic
`CallGraphIndex.DetectedDynamicCollection`/`MethodCallInfo.DynamicArgSource` capture infrastructure
`BytecodeClassParser` already produces for EVERY invocation (Mongo or JDBC alike — confirmed by
inspection, its ALOAD/concat-tracking code has no owner/method allowlist at all). New parallel
methods in `JpaMethodDetector.java` (`resolveGenericSqlCallSiteArg`, `resolveGenericClassCallSiteArg`,
`captureDynamicSql`, `captureDynamicClass`, new `DetectionResult`/`CallSiteSql`/`CallSiteClass`
records) mirror `MongoMethodDetector`'s shape exactly. Deliberately did NOT change
`CallTreeBuilder`'s constructor (would have required touching all 10 existing call sites across the
test suite) — the new JDBC methods are wired into the EXISTING `collectionResolver.
tagCallSiteCollection(...)` call site already invoked once per child node, chained after the
Mongo-specific handling. Dynamic refs staged by `JpaMethodDetector` use a distinctive `"SQL_"`-
prefixed `varKind` (`SQL_PARAM`, `SQL_LOCAL_VAR`, `SQL_CONCAT_LITERAL_PARAM`, `SQL_PARAM_CLASS`, …) so
they can never collide with, or be mis-consumed by, the pre-existing Mongo-specific `"PARAM"`/
`"PARAM_CLASS"` handling reading the SAME `dynamicCollectionRefs` list on the same `CallNode`.

**What now resolves (real, compiled-bytecode proof — `JdbcTableResolutionCall009Test`, 5 tests, all
passing)**:
- **Control case** (baseline, no propagation): a literal SQL string directly at the
  `JdbcTemplate.query(...)` call site resolves to table `orders` — confirms JDBC detection itself
  works before any new tracing logic is involved.
- **Single-hop**: caller passes a literal SQL string as an argument into a callee whose own body only
  sees an unresolved `String sql` parameter — now resolves (`CALL_SITE_SQL_PARAM_PROPAGATION`), and
  the stale `SQL_PARAM` dynamic ref is correctly removed.
- **Bounded multi-hop**: a literal SQL string built at the entry point is threaded UNCHANGED through
  2 intermediate wrapper methods (3 total call sites) before being used at the bottom — resolves via
  the bounded `MAX_HOP_DEPTH`-capped ancestor-chain walk.
- **Concat-fold**: `"SELECT * FROM " + tableName` is built one level below the caller that supplies
  the literal `tableName` — resolves to `customers` (`CALL_SITE_SQL_CONCAT_PROPAGATION`) once the
  concatenation is folded and the resulting full SQL string is parsed for its table name.
- **Class<?> naming-heuristic across a hop**: an un-annotated `InvoiceEntity.class` (deliberately no
  `@Table`/`@Entity`) threaded through one wrapper method into a JPA Criteria API call resolves to
  `invoices` via the naming-convention heuristic (CamelCase → snake_case, pluralized), tagged
  distinctly as `CALL_SITE_SQL_CLASS_NAMING_HEURISTIC` so it is never confused with a confirmed
  `@Table`/`@Entity` match.

**Explicitly out of scope / remaining gaps (documented, not fixed here)** — **CLOSED by `CALL-012`/
`CALL-014`, §219**:
- ~~The `param + param` SQL-string concat shape (Mongo's `CALL-008`/`foldTwoParamConcatIfPossible`
  analog) is NOT implemented for JDBC~~ — **closed by `CALL-012` (§219)**: ported
  `foldTwoParamConcatIfPossible`'s exact technique to JDBC as `foldTwoParamSqlConcatIfPossible`.
- ~~The `Class<?>`-across-hops naming-CONFIRMED tier (i.e., reaching `ctx.entityTableMap` — the real
  `@Table`/`@Entity` ground truth — from partway up an ancestor chain) is not implemented~~ — **closed
  by `CALL-014` (§219)**: `ResolutionContext` is now threaded through `tagGeneralSqlCallSite` to
  `tagSqlClassCallSite`, which checks `ctx.entityTableMap` first, falling back to the naming-convention
  heuristic only when no annotation ground truth exists.
- Stored-procedure/function name propagation (`SimpleJdbcCall.withProcedureName`/
  `CallableStatement`) was not extended — same-method-literal-only for those call shapes remains,
  matching this task's own JDBC/SQL-table-name-only scope (procedures are a materially different
  detection shape, not simply "SQL string" tracing).
- `CALL-011`'s Redis/Cassandra/Elasticsearch/MyBatis gap (§214) remains completely untouched, as
