### §216 — `CALL-010` implemented: HTTP/external-call target-path resolution brought up to the same cross-method value-tracing capability level `CALL-001..009` already built for MongoDB collections / JDBC tables

**Scope**: §214 found `CallTreeBuilder.createHttpCallLeaf` reads only the current call site's own
`stringArgs()` (falling back to a best-effort scan of the calling method's own string literals) —
zero caller-argument tracing at all, not even CALL-001's single-hop tier. This task closes that gap:
single-hop caller-arg resolution, bounded multi-hop (reusing `CollectionResolver.MAX_HOP_DEPTH`), and
narrow `literal + param`/`param + literal` URL-string concat-folding, for RestTemplate/WebClient-style
HTTP client calls (the same call shapes `HTTP_CLIENT_METHOD_TO_VERB` already recognizes).

**Architecture decision: inline extension of `CallTreeBuilder.createHttpCallLeaf` itself, NOT a new
parallel-sibling detector class (unlike `CALL-009`'s own `JpaMethodDetector`-mirrors-`MongoMethodDetector`
decision).** Read `JpaMethodDetector`'s §215 architecture first and explicitly checked whether the
same shape applies here — it does not, for two real structural reasons specific to this call path,
not just to keep the diff small:
1. **No pre-existing "detector scans the callee's own body" stage exists for HTTP at all.** Mongo's
   and JDBC's mechanisms both key off a callee's own `dynamicCollectionRefs` entry, populated by a
   detector (`MongoMethodDetector`/`JpaMethodDetector`/`collectCollections`) that walks the callee's
   body separately, BEFORE `CollectionResolver.tagCallSiteCollection` ever runs — that's the entire
   reason those two need the `copyForCallSiteTagging`/memoization-safety dance and a parallel resolver
   object. `createHttpCallLeaf` has no such split: it builds the `HTTP_CALL` leaf node directly, once,
   at the exact call site, with the enclosing method's real `ancestorCallChain` already in scope in
   the very same stack frame (confirmed by reading the call site at
   `CallTreeBuilder.java` ~line 962, next to `extendAncestorChain`'s existing usage) — no separate
   "callee body" node exists to memoize or copy defensively.
2. **No post-resolution parsing step is needed.** JDBC's traced value is a raw SQL string that must
   still be parsed for its table name(s) (`SqlStatementParser`) — a genuine second stage that
   justified JDBC's own parallel sibling methods. HTTP's traced value (a URL/path string) IS the
   reportable value already (after the existing `extractPathFromUrl`/`extractHost` helpers, unchanged
   and reused as-is) — there is no analogous "value → domain object" translation step to justify a
   separate resolver class.

Given both structural differences are absent here, adding a new `HttpMethodDetector` sibling class
would only add indirection with no matching justification — small, targeted new private methods
directly in `CallTreeBuilder.java` (`resolveHttpPathAcrossHops`, `foldHttpConcatIfPossible`, plus two
tiny predicate helpers and a `HttpPathResolution(String path, String source)` provenance record) are
the right-sized fix, reusing `InvocationRef.stringArgs()`/`dynamicArgSources()` (the same
domain-agnostic `BytecodeClassParser` capture infra CALL-001..009 already confirmed has no
owner/method allowlist) and `CollectionResolver.MAX_HOP_DEPTH` (referenced directly — same package,
package-private — not redefined).

**Base-URL-field pattern (task step 4's "field-stored-value machinery" question) — investigated,
found NOT implementable without a new, riskier parser change, marked explicitly out of scope.**
Checked whether `CALL-005`'s field-lambda machinery generalizes: it does not — `CALL-005` tracks
`PUTFIELD` immediately following an `invokedynamic` that produces a *functional-interface* value
(method references), an entirely different bytecode shape from a `String`-typed base-URL field. The
actually relevant question is whether `BytecodeClassParser`'s existing string-concat capture
(`tryFoldStringConcat`/`ConcatSlotInfo`) already covers `this.baseUrl + path`. By inspection (before
writing any fixture) it does NOT: `tryFoldStringConcat`'s two-operand and one-operand cases only ever
recognize a `String` LITERAL or a `ParamOperand` (local var/parameter) on the non-literal side —
there is no `FieldOperand` case at all, so a base-URL INSTANCE FIELD used as one operand of a `+`
concatenation is silently dropped by the existing capture (confirmed against a real compiled
`this.baseUrl + "/orders/" + id`-shaped fixture during investigation: `dynamicArgSources()` came back
empty for that call, whereas the identical shape with a local variable/parameter operand instead of a
field was captured correctly). A bare field used as the WHOLE, un-concatenated argument (e.g.
`restTemplate.getForObject(baseUrl, ...)`) IS already captured today (`FIELD`-kind dynamic arg,
pre-existing generic capture) but is a materially rarer real shape than the base-URL-plus-relative-path
pattern the task specifically calls out. Extending `tryFoldStringConcat`/`ConcatFold`/`ConcatSlotInfo`
to add a `FieldOperand` case is a real, non-trivial change to shared parser infra used by EVERY
detector (Mongo/JDBC/HTTP alike) — a materially bigger, higher-blast-radius change than this task's
own small-increment discipline and off-limits-file caution calls for, and well outside "trivially free
using already-built machinery." **Decision: explicitly out of scope for CALL-010, documented here as
a residual gap** (see below), not silently skipped.

**What now resolves (real, compiled-bytecode proof — `HttpCallResolutionCall010Test`, 4 tests, all
passing)**:
- **Control case** (baseline, no propagation): a literal URL directly at the
  `RestTemplate.getForObject(...)` call site resolves to `httpTargetPath=/api/orders`,
  `httpTargetPathSource=DIRECT_LITERAL` — confirms the pre-existing direct-call-site behavior is
  unchanged.
- **Single-hop**: caller passes a literal URL as an argument into a callee whose own body only sees
  an unresolved `String url` parameter — now resolves via `ancestorCallChain[0]`
  (`CALL_SITE_PARAM_PROPAGATION`).
- **Bounded multi-hop**: a literal URL supplied at the entry point is threaded UNCHANGED through 2
  intermediate wrapper methods (3 total call sites) before being used at the bottom — resolves via
  the same `MAX_HOP_DEPTH`-capped ancestor-chain walk Mongo/JDBC already use.
- **Concat-fold**: `"http://order-svc/api/orders/" + region` (built into a local variable, then
  passed to `getForObject`) resolves to `/api/orders/east` once the literal-prefix + resolvable-param
  concatenation is folded (`CALL_SITE_CONCAT_PROPAGATION`), reusing the SAME single-operand
  `literal + param`/`param + literal` shape CALL-003/CALL-009 already established (only fires when
  the concat result is stored to a local var before use — see the base-URL-field note above for the
  one concat shape that is NOT captured today).
- **Base-URL-field pattern**: explicitly **NOT implemented** — see architecture decision above for
  the real reason (a `BytecodeClassParser` capture gap, not a `CollectionResolver`/`CallTreeBuilder`
  gap) and why fixing it here would have been a disproportionately large, shared-infra change.

**Explicitly out of scope / remaining gaps (documented, not fixed here)**:
- The base-URL-instance-field + relative-path concatenation pattern (`this.baseUrl + path`) — see
  above; requires a new `FieldOperand` case in `BytecodeClassParser.tryFoldStringConcat`/
  `ConcatSlotInfo`, a shared-infra change affecting every detector, deliberately deferred.
- ~~The `param + param` URL-concat shape (Mongo's `CALL-008`/HTTP analog) is not implemented~~ —
  **closed by `CALL-013` (§219)**: ported the same by-name ancestor-chain-walking technique into
  `CallTreeBuilder.foldTwoParamHttpConcatIfPossible`. (The base-URL-instance-field pattern above
  remains a separate, still-open residual gap — untouched by `CALL-013`.)
- `WebClient`'s fluent builder (`.uri(...)` after `.get()`/`.post()`) is not specifically traced
  beyond what the pre-existing `HTTP_CLIENT_METHOD_TO_VERB` entry-point recognition already covers —
  this task only extended path RESOLUTION at whatever call site `createHttpCallLeaf` is invoked for,
  not the entry-point recognition itself (unchanged, out of this task's scope).
- Feign clients (`createFeignCallLeaf`) are unaffected/untouched — Feign's path already comes from
  the declared interface method's mapping annotation (a more reliable source of truth than any
  argument-tracing could be), not from call-site arguments, so no gap existed there to begin with.
- `CALL-011`'s Redis/Cassandra/Elasticsearch/MyBatis gap (§214) remains completely untouched, as
  scoped.

**Full suite**: `mvn -o -pl jar-analyzer-core test` → `BUILD SUCCESS`, **410/410, 0 failures, 0
errors, 11 skipped** (406 pre-`CALL-010` baseline + 4 new `HttpCallResolutionCall010Test` cases).
Zero regressions in any prior `CALL-001..009` case. Kept full backward compatibility for the private
2-arg `createHttpCallLeaf(InvocationRef, IndexedMethod)` signature (existing reflection-based tests
`HttpClientTaggingTest`/`CallTreeVisibilityTest` call it directly) by adding it as a thin overload
delegating to the new 3-arg `createHttpCallLeaf(InvocationRef, IndexedMethod, List<InvocationRef>)`
with a `null` ancestor chain — no existing test file was modified.

**Files touched**: `CallTreeBuilder.java` (main — `createHttpCallLeaf` extended plus new private
`resolveHttpPathAcrossHops`/`foldHttpConcatIfPossible`/helpers/`HttpPathResolution` record;
`extendAncestorChain`/`CollectionResolver.MAX_HOP_DEPTH` reused, not duplicated), `CallNode.java`
(main — new `httpTargetPathSource` field + getter/setter + `copyForCallSiteTagging` propagation, same
provenance-tagging pattern `collectionSources`/`CALL-004`/`CALL-008`/`CALL-009` already established),
and the new `HttpCallResolutionCall010Test.java`. New scratch fixture sources/classes added to the
session scratchpad (`call010/{src,out}/{control,singlehop,multihop,concat}/`) — not committed.
`CollectionResolver.java` NOT touched (only its `MAX_HOP_DEPTH` constant is referenced, read-only).
`BytecodeClassParser.java` NOT touched (the base-URL-field gap found during investigation is a real,
documented residual — see above — deliberately not fixed in this pass). `plsql-parser/*`,
`DependencyCrawler.java`, `EntityProceduresReader`/`EntityTablesReader`/`EntityJoinsReader`,
`callGraphViz.js`, `scope.js`, `AnalyzerController.java`, `EndpointReportBuilder.java`,
`tableFramework.js`, `api.js`, `CALL-005`'s lambda-target fields, and `CALL-009`'s JDBC-specific
additions in `JpaMethodDetector.java` all untouched, per this task's explicit off-limits list.

**Status: DONE. `CALL-010` closed** for its own explicitly scoped subset (single-hop, bounded
multi-hop, single-operand concat-fold) — HTTP/external-call target-path resolution now has real
cross-method value tracing where it previously had none at all (not even CALL-001's single-hop tier
existed before this task). The base-URL-instance-field pattern is a genuine, investigated, explicitly
documented residual gap requiring a shared-infra (`BytecodeClassParser`) change, deliberately deferred
rather than attempted under this session's small-increment/off-limits-file discipline; `param + param`
concat-folding remains deferred too, matching `CALL-009`'s own precedent. `CALL-011`
(Redis/Cassandra/Elasticsearch/MyBatis) remains unscheduled per §214.

### §217 — trigger source view 404: `.pkb` naming heuristic collides with the trigger naming convention

User reported (verbatim): "did find what i caues of this A request returned 404 (nothing loaded)...
http://localhost:8083/api/parser/analyses/ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE/source/
ANALYZER_REF.TRG.TRG_REF_REGION.pkb" (URL trimmed of the trigger name in the report, exact repro
below).

**Root cause**: `parser/js/sourceView.js`'s `_resolvePackageSource(sourceFile)` exists to turn a
package-subprogram's own per-procedure source filename (`schema.PKG_NAME.subprogram.sql`, e.g.
`ANALYZER.ERP_PKG_PLANNER.COMPUTE_TOTAL.sql`) into the combined package-body file that actually
exists on disk (`ANALYZER.ERP_PKG_PLANNER.pkb`) — needed because a subprogram's `lineStart`/
`lineEnd` refer to positions in that combined file, not the per-procedure one. It decided "is this a
package subprogram" purely by counting dot-separated segments (`parts.length === 3`) — but this
project's trigger naming convention is ALSO exactly 3 segments: `schema.TRG.triggerName.sql` (e.g.
`ANALYZER_REF.TRG.TRG_REF_REGION.sql`), with `TRG` as a fixed sentinel marking "this is a trigger",
never a real package name. The heuristic misfired for every trigger, transforming the correct,
real, 200-serving filename into `schema.TRG.pkb` — which never exists (no combined file for
triggers) — and requesting that instead, hence the 404. Confirmed against 2 real triggers in this
corpus (`ANALYZER_REF.TRG.TRG_REF_REGION.sql`, `ANALYZER.TRG.ERP_TRG_SO_STMT_AD.sql`) — both hit
this, not a one-off.

**Fixed**: excluded the `TRG` sentinel explicitly (`parts[1].toUpperCase() !== 'TRG'`) rather than
threading the node's own `objectType` through every one of `_resolvePackageSource`'s 3 call sites,
which would have been a larger, riskier change for the same outcome — the sentinel is a fixed,
known naming-convention marker, not something that will ever collide with a real package name.

**Verified**: confirmed the exact bogus URL from the report now correctly resolves to `null` (no
`.pkb` substitution attempted) while the real package-subprogram case is unaffected — both checked
directly, plus live HTTP: `GET .../source/ANALYZER_REF.TRG.TRG_REF_REGION.sql` → 200 (the real file,
was already fine on its own), `GET .../source/ANALYZER_REF.TRG.pkb` → 404 (correctly still 404 —
that file genuinely doesn't exist; the fix is that nothing should ever request it for a trigger
anymore). Static JS is bundled into the packaged jar for this app (confirmed, not served from disk
directly) — rebuilt `unified-web`, restarted with the same mode-4 config every prior section used,
confirmed the deployed file carries the fix via a direct curl of the served script.

**Files changed**: `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/parser/js/sourceView.js`. Not committed.

### §218 — `CALL-011` implemented (partial): Elasticsearch index-name resolution brought up to the same cross-method value-tracing capability level `CALL-001..010` already built for MongoDB/JDBC/HTTP; Redis/Cassandra/MyBatis investigated and deferred with per-detector reasons

**Scope**: §214 flagged four detectors with zero `dynamicArgSources` usage: `RedisMethodDetector.java`,
`CassandraMethodDetector.java`, `ElasticsearchMethodDetector.java`, `MyBatisMethodDetector.java`. This
task read all four in full, decided an architecture per-detector on its own merits (not a forced
uniform approach), implemented cross-method value tracing for the one that was a clean, low-risk fit
(Elasticsearch), and investigated the other three deeply enough to make an honest, specific,
individually-justified deferral call on each rather than a blanket skip.

**Per-detector investigation and decision:**

- **Elasticsearch — IMPLEMENTED (`CALL-011a`).** Architecture: parallel-to-Mongo (NOT JDBC-style),
  same reasoning `CALL-010`'s HTTP decision used to rule OUT the JDBC shape for itself, but here the
  MONGO shape fits instead of neither: an ES index name is the traced value AS-IS (no post-resolution
  parsing step, unlike JDBC's raw-SQL-string case) — this is architecturally identical to Mongo's own
  collection-name case, not HTTP's "no callee-body detector stage" case, because
  `ElasticsearchMethodDetector.detect(...)` already IS a "scan the callee's own body" stage (exactly
  like `MongoMethodDetector`/`JpaMethodDetector`), called from `CollectionResolver.collectCollections`
  before `tagCallSiteCollection` ever runs — the exact structural precondition CALL-010's own writeup
  identified as what JDBC/Mongo have and HTTP lacks. Added `ElasticsearchMethodDetector.DetectionResult`
  (mirrors `MongoMethodDetector.DetectionResult`) plus `detectWithDynamic`/`resolveGenericCallSiteArg`/
  `CallSiteIndex`, and new sibling methods in `CollectionResolver.java`
  (`tagGeneralEsCallSite`/`resolveEsAcrossHops`/`foldEsConcatIfPossible`), reusing
  `CollectionResolver.MAX_HOP_DEPTH` directly (not redefined) and the SAME domain-agnostic
  `dynamicArgSources()`/concat-capture infra `BytecodeClassParser` already produces for every
  invocation. Dynamic refs staged by `ElasticsearchMethodDetector` use an `"ES_"`-prefixed varKind
  (`ES_PARAM`, `ES_CONCAT_LITERAL_PARAM`, …) so they can never collide with Mongo's `PARAM`/JDBC's
  `SQL_PARAM` entries on the same `CallNode.dynamicCollectionRefs` list — same technique `CALL-009`
  established for its own `SQL_`-prefixed tags.

  **What now resolves (real, compiled-bytecode proof — `ElasticsearchIndexResolutionCall011Test`, 4
  tests, all passing):**
  - **Control**: a literal index name directly at the `ElasticsearchOperations.search(...)` call site
    resolves to `catalog_index` — confirms direct-call detection is unaffected.
  - **Single-hop**: caller passes a literal index name as an argument into a callee whose own body
    only sees an unresolved `String index` parameter — now resolves
    (`CALL_SITE_ES_PARAM_PROPAGATION`), stale `ES_PARAM` ref removed.
  - **Bounded multi-hop**: a literal index name supplied at the entry point is threaded UNCHANGED
    through 2 intermediate wrapper methods (3 total call sites) before being used at the bottom —
    resolves via the bounded `MAX_HOP_DEPTH`-capped ancestor-chain walk.
  - **Concat-fold**: `"orders_" + region` built into a local variable one level above the leaf call
    resolves to `orders_east` once the literal-prefix + resolvable-param concatenation is folded
    (`CALL_SITE_ES_CONCAT_PROPAGATION`).
  - Class-object-derived naming (the Mongo/JDBC "confirmed-annotation-or-heuristic tier") was
    evaluated and NOT implemented: `ElasticsearchMethodDetector` already has a DIRECT-call
    Class-derivation path (`entityCollectionMap`, populated from `@Document(indexName=...)`, consulted
    inline in `detect`/`detectWithDynamic`) — extending it across hops would need a `PARAM_CLASS`-style
    dynamic-arg capture plus an ancestor walk mirroring `resolveClassAcrossHops`/`tagSqlClassCallSite`.
    Deliberately deferred (not attempted this pass): unlike Mongo/JDBC, no real fixture or corpus
    evidence of an ES entity `Class<?>` being threaded across method boundaries (rather than used
    directly at the `save`/`index` call site) was found during this investigation — implementing an
    ancestor-walk for a pattern with no observed real occurrence risks the same
    "engineering effort with no matching justification" this session's own established discipline
    (§216's HTTP writeup) explicitly cautions against. A small, low-risk follow-on if a real case
    surfaces later, exactly like JDBC's own documented residual gaps.
  - `param + param` concat-folding not implemented, matching `CALL-009`/`CALL-010`'s identical scoping
    precedent (narrow single-operand `literal+param`/`param+literal` shape only).

- **Cassandra — DEFERRED (`CALL-011b`), genuinely dual-shaped, not a lazy skip.**
  `CassandraMethodDetector` has TWO structurally different detection paths in ONE class:
  `CassandraTemplate`/`CassandraOperations` methods (`insert`/`select`/`delete`/…) are a direct
  value-IS-the-table-name shape (Mongo/ES-style, no parsing needed), but `CqlSession.execute`/
  `executeAsync` carry a raw CQL STRING that must be parsed via `extractTableFromCql` AFTER
  resolution — a JDBC-style extra step. Building real cross-method tracing for Cassandra properly
  would mean implementing BOTH the ES-style direct-value mechanism AND a second, JDBC-style
  parse-after-resolve mechanism inside the SAME detector, each needing its own fixtures — materially
  more work than Elasticsearch's single clean shape, for a backend this codebase's own real corpus
  shows is a much smaller fraction of DB call sites than Mongo/JDBC (confirmed by inspection: only
  this one detector file references Cassandra at all, vs. multiple JPA/Mongo call shapes threaded
  through the whole call-tree/report pipeline). Given this session's remaining scope and the
  established "don't force a uniform architecture where the code doesn't actually match" principle,
  this is deferred as a real, investigated, documented residual — not preemptively skipped.
- **Redis — DEFERRED (`CALL-011c`), genuinely lower real-world value, not lazy.** Redis keys are
  overwhelmingly built per-request/per-entity (e.g. `"session:" + userId`, `"cache:order:" + orderId`)
  — even with full cross-method tracing, the CALLER'S OWN literal argument at any given call site is
  very often itself a per-request runtime value (an ID, a token), not a stable compile-time constant
  the way a Mongo collection name or a JDBC table name is. Cross-method value tracing's entire value
  proposition is recovering a STABLE, reportable name that was merely passed through wrapper methods —
  that precondition is much weaker for Redis key patterns than for the other four backends. There is
  also no annotation-driven naming convention analog to `@Document`/`@Table`/`@Document(indexName=)`
  to anchor a Class-derivation tier. `RedisMethodDetector` also has zero pre-existing `DetectionResult`/
  dynamic-capture infrastructure to build on (confirmed by inspection — `detect` returns a bare
  `List<DetectedCollection>`, always falls back to a literal `"redis:unknown-key"` placeholder, never
  attempts a same-hop dynamic capture at all), so this would be new machinery built from scratch for a
  backend whose resolved values are least likely of the five to be analytically useful once found.
- **MyBatis — DEFERRED (`CALL-011d`), structurally thin value-tracing target, not lazy.**
  `MyBatisMethodDetector` has two detection paths: (A) `SqlSession.selectOne`/`selectList`/etc. with a
  mapper-statement-ID string arg (`"com.example.OrderMapper.findAll"`) resolved via `namedQueryMap`,
  and (B) `@Select`/`@Insert`/… annotations on `@Mapper` interface methods. Path (B) is annotation-
  based — an annotation's `value` attribute is a compile-time constant fixed on the METHOD DECLARATION
  itself, not a call-site argument; there is no "cross-method" dimension to trace at all (annotations
  cannot be threaded through wrapper methods the way a String/Class argument can). Path (A)'s
  statement-ID string is, in the overwhelming majority of real MyBatis usage, a hardcoded literal at
  the call site (mapper namespace + method name is a fixed, compile-time string by MyBatis's own
  convention) — real cross-method dynamic passing of a mapper statement ID was not found to be a
  pattern this investigation could substantiate as common enough to justify new tracing machinery,
  and even if resolved, the value still requires a SECOND indirection (`namedQueryMap` lookup, itself
  keyed by the exact resolved literal) before it becomes a table name — a JDBC-shaped extra step
  layered on top of an already input that's rarely dynamic. Given the combination of (paths A+B both
  structurally weak candidates for this technique) and this session's remaining scope, deferred as a
  real, investigated, documented residual rather than attempted.

**Full suite**: `mvn -o -pl jar-analyzer-core test` → `BUILD SUCCESS`, **414/414, 0 failures, 0
errors, 11 skipped** (410 pre-`CALL-011` baseline, confirmed by running the full suite before any
change in this task — matches §216's own cited number exactly — + 4 new
`ElasticsearchIndexResolutionCall011Test` cases). Zero regressions in any prior `CALL-001..010` case.

**Files touched**: `ElasticsearchMethodDetector.java`, `CollectionResolver.java` (both `main`), plus
the new `ElasticsearchIndexResolutionCall011Test.java`. New scratch fixture sources/classes added to
the session scratchpad (`call011/{src,out}/{control,singlehop,multihop,concat}/`) — not committed.
`RedisMethodDetector.java`, `CassandraMethodDetector.java`, `MyBatisMethodDetector.java` NOT touched
(each deferred with its own reason above — no speculative partial edits left in any of them).
`BytecodeClassParser.java` NOT touched (its existing generic ALOAD/concat/dynamic-arg capture already
covers Elasticsearch call sites with no changes needed, confirmed by inspection and by the passing
concat-fold test). `CallTreeBuilder.java` NOT touched (no constructor change needed — wired into the
EXISTING `collectionResolver.tagCallSiteCollection(...)` call site already invoked once per child
node, chained after the Mongo/JDBC-specific handling, same pattern `CALL-009` established).
`plsql-parser/*`, `DependencyCrawler.java`, `EntityProceduresReader`/`EntityTablesReader`/
`EntityJoinsReader`, `callGraphViz.js`, `scope.js`, `AnalyzerController.java`,
`EndpointReportBuilder.java`, `tableFramework.js`, `api.js`, `CALL-005`'s lambda-target fields, and
`CALL-009`/`CALL-010`'s own JDBC/HTTP-specific additions all untouched, per this task's explicit
off-limits list.

**Status: `CALL-011a` (Elasticsearch) DONE.** `CALL-011b` (Cassandra), `CALL-011c` (Redis), and
`CALL-011d` (MyBatis) are DEFERRED, each with its own specific, investigated, documented technical
reason above (dual-shape detection requiring two mechanisms in one class; low real-world stable-value
payoff with no existing dynamic-capture infra; and a structurally thin/mostly-non-dynamic call-site
shape, respectively) — not a blanket "skip the rest" decision. Per this task's own instructions, each
was investigated on its own merits before being deferred; none were skipped preemptively.

### §219 — `CALL-012`/`CALL-013`/`CALL-014` implemented: close three small, documented residual gaps left open by `CALL-009` (§215) and `CALL-010` (§216) — JDBC `param+param` SQL-concat-fold, HTTP `param+param` URL-concat-fold, and the JDBC `Class<?>`-across-hops CONFIRMED tier

**Scope**: §215's own write-up named two residual gaps and §216's own write-up named one of the same
two (the base-URL-instance-field pattern, the third gap §216 documented, is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE
for this task and was left completely untouched — see below):
1. JDBC's `param + param` SQL-string concat-fold (Mongo's `CALL-008`/`foldTwoParamConcatIfPossible`
   analog) was never implemented for JDBC — only the single-operand `literal + param`/`param + literal`
   shape.
2. HTTP's `param + param` URL-concat-fold — the identical gap, for `CallTreeBuilder.createHttpCallLeaf`.
3. JDBC's `Class<?>`-across-hops CONFIRMED tier — `tagSqlClassCallSite` had no `ResolutionContext`
   threaded to it at its call site inside `tagCallSiteCollection`, so a propagated `Class<?>` with a
   REAL `@Table`/`@Entity` annotation still only ever resolved via the lower-confidence
   naming-convention heuristic, even when `ctx.entityTableMap` (the real ground truth) had an entry
   for it.

**Part A — JDBC `param+param` concat-fold (`CALL-012`, closes §215's own residual).**
`CollectionResolver.foldSqlConcatIfPossible`'s dispatch now checks for the `CONCAT_PARAM_PARAM`
dynamic-arg kind (already emitted domain-agnostically by `BytecodeClassParser.tryFoldStringConcat`
since `CALL-008`/§213 — confirmed by inspection: its 2-operand branch has no owner/method allowlist,
so it already fires for JDBC call sites with zero changes needed there) and routes to a new sibling
method, `foldTwoParamSqlConcatIfPossible`, which is a direct line-for-line port of
`foldTwoParamConcatIfPossible`'s exact by-name-only ancestor-chain-walking technique, adapted from
`MongoMethodDetector.CallSiteCollection` to `JpaMethodDetector.CallSiteSql`: both still-unresolved
operand names are chased independently up `ancestorCallChain`, an ancestor hop is only ever trusted
when its shape unambiguously identifies which operand is which (by name, or by bytecode push-order
positional trust only when both operands resolve at the exact same hop with zero dynamic args), and a
genuinely-unresolvable operand (the ancestor chain runs out, e.g. a `@PathVariable`) produces an
honest `resolved{unresolvedName}` PARTIAL fold rather than fabricating a value — the identical
"never guess" contract `foldTwoParamConcatIfPossible` already established. `isSqlConcatShape` was
extended to recognize `CONCAT_PARAM_PARAM` alongside the existing `CONCAT_LITERAL_PARAM`/
`CONCAT_PARAM_LITERAL` kinds.

**Part B — HTTP `param+param` concat-fold (`CALL-013`, closes §216's own residual).**
Identical technique, ported into `CallTreeBuilder.java` this time (not `CollectionResolver.java`,
matching `CALL-010`'s own architecture decision to extend `createHttpCallLeaf` inline rather than add
a parallel detector class — no structural reason changed since §216's writeup, so the same
architecture choice still applies). `isHttpConcatShape` now also recognizes `CONCAT_PARAM_PARAM`;
`foldHttpConcatIfPossible`'s dispatch routes to a new `foldTwoParamHttpConcatIfPossible`, the same
by-name ancestor-chain walk, returning a `HttpPathResolution` (tagged `CALL_SITE_CONCAT_PROPAGATION`,
the same source tag the single-operand HTTP concat fold already uses — no new tag needed since HTTP,
unlike Mongo, never distinguished single- vs. two-operand concat folds by source string in the first
place) or `null` (never fabricates) instead of a `CallSiteCollection`/`CallSiteSql` record.

**Part C — JDBC `Class<?>`-across-hops CONFIRMED tier (`CALL-014`, closes §215's own residual).**
`tagCallSiteCollection` already had `ResolutionContext ctx` in scope (threaded in by the one
production call site, `CallTreeBuilder.java`'s `buildCallTree`, since `CALL-004`/§210 — confirmed by
inspection before starting, no constructor/call-site signature change needed anywhere) but never
passed it down through `tagGeneralSqlCallSite` to `tagSqlClassCallSite`. Both methods now take `ctx`
as an added parameter, threaded through unchanged. `tagSqlClassCallSite` now consults
`ctx.entityTableMap` (the exact same `@Table`/`@Entity` ground-truth map
`resolveRepositoryCollections`/`JpaMethodDetector.detect`'s own direct-call-site case already use,
populated once per analysis run in `CallTreeBuilder.java`'s `entityTableMap.put(ic.fqn, ic.jpaTableName)`
block) via the existing `resolveEntityFqnToCollection` helper (already used by Mongo's
`resolveClassAcrossHops` — reused verbatim, not duplicated) FIRST, tagging a hit
`CALL_SITE_SQL_CLASS_PROPAGATION` (a new, higher-confidence source distinct from the pre-existing
`CALL_SITE_SQL_CLASS_NAMING_HEURISTIC`), falling back to `deriveTableNameByNamingConvention` only when
`ctx`/`ctx.entityTableMap` is null or has no entry for that class — exactly mirroring `CALL-004`'s own
`ClassResolution(collectionName, source)` tiering pattern for Mongo (`CALL_SITE_CLASS_PROPAGATION` vs.
`CALL_SITE_CLASS_NAMING_HEURISTIC`).

### §220 — `CALL-015` implemented: §216's LAST documented residual gap — the HTTP base-URL-instance-field concat pattern (`this.baseUrl + path`) — closed safely in shared `BytecodeClassParser` infra, zero regressions across the whole CALL-001..014 arc

**Scope**: §216's own write-up named this pattern — `this.baseUrl + path`, one operand a
same-class instance/static field, not a local variable or parameter — as explicitly NOT implemented,
calling it "a `BytecodeClassParser` capture gap, not a `CollectionResolver`/`CallTreeBuilder` gap"
and flagging it as risky shared infra touched by every detector (Mongo/JDBC/HTTP/Elasticsearch).
This task's job was to implement it if it could be done safely and narrowly, or defer it with a clear
technical reason otherwise.

**Step 1 — read `tryFoldStringConcat`/`ConcatSlotInfo` in full before writing anything**, per this
task's own instructions. Confirmed the exact operand representation: `ParamOperand(name)` for an
ALOAD-of-same-method-parameter push, a plain `String` for an LDC-literal push, and `NON_OPERAND` as a
sentinel for anything untracked (a GETFIELD included) — a GETFIELD today falls into the window
scan's generic `else` branch and unconditionally clears the sliding operand window, so `this.baseUrl
+ path` never even reaches `tryFoldStringConcat` with a usable window; it silently falls back to
plain unresolved `LOCAL_VAR`, exactly as §216 described.

**Step 2/3 — is there already a "field's value is always X" tracking mechanism to reuse?** Checked
`CallGraphIndex`'s `fieldLambdaTargets`/`pendingLambdaTarget*` (CALL-005) — read-only, per this
task's own explicit instruction not to touch it; conceptually similar ("this field was written this
value somewhere") but built for method-reference redirection, not string values, and not reusable
as-is. Found `BytecodeClassParser.classConstantsByFieldName` (`main`, existing, pre-CALL-015): a
whole-class prescan that already resolves a `GETSTATIC`-loaded same-class **static final** String
constant inline, exactly the shape needed — but scoped ONLY to fields with a bytecode
`ConstantValue` attribute (which the JVM only emits for `static final` fields with a compile-time
constant initializer), so it does not cover the realistic **instance** field case (`private final
String baseUrl = "...";` or non-final `@Value`-injected fields) this task's own pattern needs.

**Step 4 — new mechanism, scoped narrowly and safely**: added a second whole-class prescan,
`fieldSingleLiteralValue`, alongside `classConstantsByFieldName` — scans every method in the class
(constructors included) for `PUTFIELD` on an owner-class field where an `LDC` STRING is the
DIRECTLY, ADJACENTLY preceding instruction (mirroring this file's own other adjacency-only literal
tracking, e.g. `concatSlotValue`'s own window). A field qualifies ONLY if:
- it is assigned EXACTLY ONE distinct literal value anywhere in the class, AND
- it is NEVER assigned from a non-literal source anywhere in the class (a `PUTFIELD` with no
  adjacent LDC — e.g. `this.baseUrl = baseUrl;`, the real constructor-parameter/`@Value`-injected
  shape — marks the field permanently disqualified).

**Step 5 — the actual concat-fold wiring turned out to need ZERO changes to `tryFoldStringConcat` or
`ConcatSlotInfo`** (a materially narrower, lower-risk change than §216's own write-up anticipated,
which expected "a new `FieldOperand` case" at that level). Real reason: resolution of a field's
value is fully LOCAL to a single whole-class prescan (unlike a `PARAM`, which genuinely needs
deferred, cross-method resolution by `CollectionResolver`/`CallTreeBuilder` later). So a `GETFIELD`
read of a field already proven single-literal is substituted INLINE, at the same point in the
window-scan loop that an `LDC` string already is (`pendingLiteral = fieldLiteral; concatWindow.add
(fieldLiteral);`) — from that point on it is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from a literal to
`tryFoldStringConcat`, which already handles `literal + ParamOperand` (`CONCAT_LITERAL_PARAM`) and
`ParamOperand + literal` (`CONCAT_PARAM_LITERAL`) with zero changes needed. An unresolvable
`GETFIELD` (not in `fieldSingleLiteralValue`) deliberately falls through unchanged to the existing
generic `else` branch, clearing the window and leaving the concatenation correctly unresolved — the
exact same "never guess" behavior as before this task. This also meant CALL-010's/CALL-013's own
HTTP concat-fold dispatch in `CallTreeBuilder.java` needed **zero changes** — `CONCAT_LITERAL_PARAM`
already flows through `foldHttpConcatIfPossible` unmodified.

**A real, orthogonal bug found and fixed IN THE TEST FIXTURE (not production code) while building
proof**: the first compiled fixtures (via plain `javac`, no `-g`) produced `dynamicArgSources=null`
for the concat-produced local variable entirely — traced with a throwaway debug harness (removed
after use) down to `resolveLocalVarName` requiring a `LocalVariableTable` (only present with `-g`)
to name the ALOAD'd parameter operand inside the window scan; without it, the `ALOAD`-of-parameter
push resolves to `NON_OPERAND` instead of `ParamOperand`, and the fold silently fails — reproduced
with a MINIMAL fixture using a **plain string literal** (no field involved at all) to confirm this
was a pre-existing fixture-compilation gap unrelated to this task's own change, not a regression.
Fixed by compiling all `CALL-015` fixtures with `-g`, matching `HttpCallResolutionCall010Test`'s own
established practice.

**Real captured output (from the passing test)**:

        httpTargetPath=/api/orders httpTargetPathSource=CALL_SITE_CONCAT_PROPAGATION

**Full suite**: `mvn -o -pl jar-analyzer-core test` → `BUILD SUCCESS`, **419/419, 0 failures, 0
errors, 11 skipped** (417 pre-`CALL-015` baseline, confirmed fresh at the start of this task — + 2

path re-ran unchanged.

**Files touched**: `jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/BytecodeClassParser.java`
(new `fieldSingleLiteralValue` whole-class prescan alongside the existing `classConstantsByFieldName`
one, and one new `else if` branch in the per-method concat-window scan; `tryFoldStringConcat`/
`ConcatSlotInfo`/`CallTreeBuilder.java`/`CollectionResolver.java` all untouched), new
`jar-analyzer-core/src/test/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/FieldBaseUrlConcatResolutionCall015Test.java`

**Row-by-row honesty check (step 2 of this task)**: the field-concat row looks like 4/4 only because
`BytecodeClassParser`'s `fieldSingleLiteralValue` prescan (CALL-015) sits in the shared bytecode-parse
layer, upstream of every detector — a resolved field literal is substituted inline as an ordinary
`LDC` push before ANY detector-specific code runs, so Mongo/JDBC/Elasticsearch inherited it for free
the moment CALL-015 landed for HTTP. This was verified by reading `BytecodeClassParser.java`'s window
scan directly, not assumed from §220's own write-up (which only *demonstrates* the HTTP case, since
that's what its own fixture targets, but does not claim domain-specificity — confirmed here that the
substitution point has no detector-kind branch at all).

collection or SQL table), and the fix is a direct, low-risk mirror of three already-proven,
already-tested implementations — no new design decisions, no new record fields, no new detector-kind
gating logic. Built as `CALL-016`.

### §224 — `CALL-017` implemented: Elasticsearch index-name resolution brought up to the same `Class<?>`-across-hops capability Mongo (CALL-004/CALL-008) and JDBC (CALL-009/CALL-014) already have

**Scope**: §221's own completeness audit proposed this as a real, deliberately-not-built gap: unlike
`CALL-016` (a pure mirror fix), `ElasticsearchMethodDetector` had ZERO `PARAM_CLASS`-kind dynamic-arg
tracking — a `Class<?>` entity reference threaded through 2+ method calls before reaching an ES
`search`/`save`/... call site produced no `dynamicCollectionRefs` entry at all, so there was nothing
for `CollectionResolver` to walk. This task closes that gap: same two-tier resolution Mongo/JDBC
already have (CONFIRMED annotation match, falling back to a naming-convention HEURISTIC), plus one
real pre-existing bug found and fixed along the way (see below).

**A real bug found before any new plumbing was needed**: reading `ElasticsearchMethodDetector.java`
and `CallGraphIndex.java` together revealed that Elasticsearch's SAME-HOP, DIRECT-call `Class<?>`
resolution (`entityCollectionMap`, described in this file's own header comment as "from
`@Document(indexName="X")` on entity classes") was **already broken before this task**, not just
missing the across-hops case: `CallGraphIndex.IndexedClass`'s annotation-reading loop only ever read
`@Document`'s `collection`/`value` attributes into `documentCollection` — it never read `indexName`
at all. Spring Data Elasticsearch's real `@Document` annotation uses `indexName`, NOT `collection` —
the SAME annotation simple name (`"Document"`, matched by CallGraphIndex without checking the FQN,
exactly as documented in CALL-004/§210's own writeup) as Spring Data MongoDB's `@Document`, but a
DIFFERENT attribute. An ES entity annotated the real way, `@Document(indexName = "products_index")`,
therefore never populated `documentCollection` at all, so `ctx.entityCollectionMap` had no entry for
it and a `.class` literal used DIRECTLY at an ES call site for that entity resolved to nothing
(`es:unknown-index`) — not merely "no cross-hop propagation", but no resolution whatsoever, even at
the same call site. This was fixed as part of this task rather than filed as a separate residual,
since the CONFIRMED across-hops tier this task needed to build has no annotation ground truth to
consult until the same-hop reading gap is fixed first — they are the same root cause.

**`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CallGraphIndex.java`**: `IndexedClass`
gained a new field, `documentIndexName` (kept separate from `documentCollection`, never merged into
it, so a Mongo-flavored `@Document` and an Elasticsearch-flavored `@Document` are never confused with
each other). The existing `@Document`/`@Collection` annotation-reading block now also reads the
`indexName` attribute independently of the `collection`/`value` read already there — the two reads
are entirely independent (a class can have either, both, or neither), distinguished purely by WHICH
attribute is actually present on that particular annotation instance, per this task's own
instruction, not by any FQN check (CallGraphIndex has never had access to the annotation's FQN, only
its simple name — confirmed by inspection before starting). `ResolutionContext` gained a new map,
`entityIndexMap` (entity FQN/simpleName → index name), populated from `@Document(indexName=...)`
specifically — the CONFIRMED-tier ground truth for Elasticsearch, kept independent of
`entityCollectionMap` even though both are sourced from the same annotation simple name.

**`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CallTreeBuilder.java`**: one new block,
alongside the existing `ic.documentCollection != null` population of `ctx.entityCollectionMap`,
populates `ctx.entityIndexMap` from `ic.documentIndexName` the same way (FQN key + simpleName key).

**`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/ElasticsearchMethodDetector.java`**:
`detectWithDynamic` gained a new parameter, `entityIndexMap`, consulted FIRST when resolving a
`__class:FQN` literal argument at a call site (the pre-existing same-hop, direct-call case — this is
the bug-fix half of this task, not new cross-hop machinery), falling back to the legacy
`entityCollectionMap` only when the ES-specific map has no entry (kept as a shared-corpus fallback,
not removed, in case a project's own conventions happen to populate both). `detect`'s own signature
was left backward-compatible (defaults `entityIndexMap` to `Map.of()` internally) since it has no
production caller needing the new map. `resolveGenericCallSiteArg` (used by the pre-existing
CALL-011 single-hop/multi-hop/concat mechanisms) was deliberately left untouched — those mechanisms
resolve STRING index names, not `Class<?>` references, and are unaffected by this task.

**`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CollectionResolver.java`**: the one
production call site of `detectWithDynamic` (inside `collectCollections`) now also passes
`ctx.entityIndexMap`. `tagGeneralEsCallSite` (the dispatcher CALL-011 already built) now also
recognizes an `ES_PARAM_CLASS`/`ES_LOCAL_VAR_CLASS`-kind dynamic ref (distinguished from the plain
`ES_PARAM`/`ES_LOCAL_VAR` ones by the existing `ks.endsWith("_CLASS")` convention `CALL-009`/§215
already established for JDBC's own `SQL_..._CLASS` tag) and, when found, routes to a new sibling
method, `tagEsClassCallSite` — a direct structural mirror of `tagSqlClassCallSite`/CALL-014's own
JDBC confirmed-tier implementation, itself modeled on Mongo's `resolveClassAcrossHops`/CALL-004: walks
`ancestorCallChain` one hop at a time using the SAME domain-agnostic `firstClassLiteralArg`/
`firstClassDynamicArg` helpers Mongo's own mechanism already uses (reused verbatim, zero duplicated
logic, per this task's own explicit instruction not to re-invent the `PARAM_CLASS`/`LOCAL_VAR_CLASS`
capture machinery), bounded at the same `CollectionResolver.MAX_HOP_DEPTH = 4`. Once a Class literal
is found, resolves it in two tiers:
1. **CONFIRMED**: `ctx.entityIndexMap` via the existing `resolveEntityFqnToCollection` helper (FQN
   first, then simple-name fallback — identical lookup shape to every other confirmed tier in this
   file) — tagged `CALL_SITE_ES_CLASS_PROPAGATION`.
2. **HEURISTIC** fallback when no annotation ground truth exists: the SAME
   `deriveCollectionNameByNamingConvention` naming heuristic Mongo's `CALL-008` already established
   (CamelCase entity name minus a common suffix, lowercased, pluralized) — reused verbatim, not
   reinvented, per this task's own instruction — tagged `CALL_SITE_ES_CLASS_NAMING_HEURISTIC`.

No changes were needed to `BytecodeClassParser.java` at all: the `PARAM_CLASS`/`LOCAL_VAR_CLASS`
dynamic-arg capture built for Mongo in `CALL-004`/§210 has no owner/detector-kind gate (confirmed by
re-reading its ALOAD-tracking loop before starting) — it already fires for ANY Class-typed ALOAD
regardless of which detector's call site consumes it. `ElasticsearchMethodDetector`'s own
`detectWithDynamic`/`resolveGenericCallSiteArg` already pick up a captured `PARAM_CLASS`/
`LOCAL_VAR_CLASS`-kind dynamic arg via their existing, unfiltered `firstDynamicArg` helper (which
takes whatever is first in the list, regardless of kind) and prefix it `"ES_"` (CALL-011's own
disjointness convention) — so the CALLEE-body half of this capability ("does the callee's own body
correctly record an unresolved Class-typed dynamic ref instead of silently dropping it") was already
working with zero new code; only the CALLER-side resolution (`tagEsClassCallSite`) and the
same-hop annotation-attribute bug fix above were genuinely new.

**What now resolves (real, compiled-bytecode proof — `ElasticsearchClassAcrossHopsCall017Test`, 3
tests, all passing)**:
- **`directClassLiteralWithDocumentIndexNameAnnotationResolves`**: a `.class` literal passed straight
  at the ES call site for `ProductEntity`, annotated `@Document(indexName = "products_index")` —
  resolves to `products_index`. Before this task's `CallGraphIndex.java` fix, this same fixture
  resolved to nothing at all (`entityCollectionMap` never had an entry for an `indexName`-only
  annotation) — this is the bug-fix half of this task, proven directly, not just the new cross-hop
  mechanism.
- **`classPropagatedThroughTwoHopsWithDocumentIndexNameAnnotationResolvesConfirmed`**:
  `MultiHopEsController` passes `AnnotatedProductEntity.class` (real
  `@Document(indexName = "catalog_index")`) into `EsServiceMid.fetch(Class<?> entityClass)`, which
  forwards its own parameter unchanged into `EsRepoLeaf.execute(Class<?> entityClass)`, whose own
  body uses it directly as `esOps.search(entityClass)`'s argument — resolves to `catalog_index`,
  tagged `CALL_SITE_ES_CLASS_PROPAGATION` (the CONFIRMED tier), with the stale `ES_PARAM_CLASS`
  dynamic ref removed. Before this task, this call site produced NO `dynamicCollectionRefs` entry
  resolution at all — the exact gap §221/§222 identified and this task closes.
- **`classPropagatedThroughTwoHopsWithoutAnnotationResolvesViaNamingHeuristic`**: the identical
  2-hop shape, but `CatalogEntity` carries no `@Document` annotation at all — resolves to `catalogs`
  (CamelCase minus no matching suffix, lowercased, pluralized), tagged
  `CALL_SITE_ES_CLASS_NAMING_HEURISTIC`, distinctly from the confirmed-tier case above, proving both
  tiers fire correctly and are never confused with each other.

**Full suite**: `mvn -o -pl jar-analyzer-core test` → `BUILD SUCCESS`, **423/423, 0 failures, 0
errors, 11 skipped** (420 pre-`CALL-017` baseline, matching §221's own cited total exactly — + 3 new
`ElasticsearchClassAcrossHopsCall017Test` cases). Zero regressions in any prior `CALL-001..016` case,
including the pre-existing `ElasticsearchIndexResolutionCall011Test` (still 5/5) whose own direct/
single-hop/multi-hop/concat/param+param cases are completely independent of this task's new
`Class<?>`-typed code path.

**Files touched**: `jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CallGraphIndex.java`
(`IndexedClass.documentIndexName`, `ResolutionContext.entityIndexMap`, annotation-reading block),
`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CallTreeBuilder.java` (one new

### §225 — investigation only: return-value (`ARETURN`) propagation into a later DB call, `$lookup` pipeline-stage handling, and pipeline representation-shape coverage — real compiled probes; `CALL-018`/`CALL-019`/`CALL-020` planned

**Scope of this pass**: read-only on `CollectionResolver.java`/`CallTreeBuilder.java`/
`CallGraphIndex.java`/`BytecodeClassParser.java`/`AggregationDetector.java` (all `main`), per this
task's explicit instruction — nothing under `jar-analyzer-core/src/main` was edited. `CALL-017`
(§224) landed concurrently from another agent during this pass; its own baseline (420/420) and new
total (423/423) are unaffected by anything here, confirmed by fresh `mvn -o -pl jar-analyzer-core
test` runs before and after this task's own work (see counts below).

**Q1 — return-value (`ARETURN`) propagation into a later DB call: REAL, CONFIRMED GAP.**
Grepped `ARETURN` across every file in `jar-analyzer-core/src/main` — zero matches anywhere. The
entire existing forward-tracing mechanism (`CollectionResolver.tagCallSiteCollection`/
`tagGeneralParamCallSite`, `CollectionResolver.java` lines 47–140, `MAX_HOP_DEPTH=4`) only ever walks
**caller-argument** provenance up the ancestor call chain — it has no concept of a callee's *return
value* flowing back down into a sibling/later call. `BytecodeClassParser.java` line 53's own doc
comment for `NON_OPERAND` names this directly: *"e.g. ALOAD of a plain local, GETFIELD, a
method-call return value) — occupies a window slot so a real literal/param pair from before it can
never be mistaken for adjacency"* — i.e. a method-call return value is explicitly treated as opaque,
by design, in the one place (`tryFoldStringConcat`'s operand-window scan) that comes closest to
tracking non-literal provenance.

Real proof, `Call018ReturnValueAndLookupProbeTest.q1_returnValuePropagationNotTraced` — three real,
javac-compiled classes (`CBuilder.resolveCollectionName()` returns the literal `"invoices"`;
`BService.getCollectionName()` is a pure `return c.resolveCollectionName();` pass-through — a second
`ARETURN` hop; `DRepo.run()` calls `b.getCollectionName()`, stores the result in a local, and passes
that local directly into `mongoTemplate.aggregate(agg, collectionName, Object.class)`), reached from
a `@RestController` endpoint (`AController#handle` → `DRepo#run`, one real caller hop, per
`ResidualGapsCall012to014Test`'s established real-`.class`-file harness style). Real output:

```
com.demo.DRepo#run hasDbInteraction=true collectionsAccessed=[] collectionSources={}
  dynamicCollectionRefs=[{variableName=collectionName, varKind=LOCAL_VAR,
  pattern=MONGO_TEMPLATE_DYNAMIC, ...}, {variableName=collectionName, varKind=LOCAL_VAR,
  pattern=TEMPLATE_AGGREGATE_DYNAMIC, ...}]
```

`"invoices"` never appears in `collectionsAccessed` — the local `collectionName` is correctly
recognized as a MongoTemplate-aggregate collection ARGUMENT (the ALOAD-of-local dynamic-ref
machinery works fine), but its value's provenance (two `ARETURN` hops back to a literal) is not
resolved; it is reported only as an unresolved `LOCAL_VAR` dynamic reference. **This is the same
kind of gap `CALL-001..017`'s entire arc closed for caller-ARGUMENT provenance — it is real,
demonstrated, and not yet addressed for return-value provenance.**

**Q2 — `$lookup` pipeline-stage handling: ALREADY FULLY IMPLEMENTED, no gap found.**
`AggregationDetector.java` already has comprehensive `$lookup`/`$graphLookup` handling across
**four** representation shapes (documented in its own class-doc, lines 17–20): (A) `Document`-based
(`new Document("$lookup", ...)`), (B) Spring Data `LookupOperation`/`GraphLookupOperation`
(`AggregationDetector.java` lines 354–358, 403–418), (C) native-driver `Aggregates.lookup(...)`
(lines 481–502), (D) `BsonDocument`. `$lookup`'s `"from"` target is tracked as a **structurally
separate** field — `PipelineDetail.lookupTargets` (`AggregationDetector.java` line 161) — distinct
from `PipelineDetail.baseCollection` (line 182's own comment: *"The collection this pipeline
actually runs ON — as opposed to $lookup/$graphLookup..."*), and `CollectionResolver.java` lines
1486–1493 attach both onto the `CallNode`'s `pipeline` map under separate keys
(`pipeline.put("baseCollection", ...)` / `pipeline.put("lookupTargets", ...)`) — never merged, never
overwriting.

Real proof, `Call018ReturnValueAndLookupProbeTest.q2_lookupTargetSeparateFromBaseCollection` — one
real compiled class: `LookupController#handle` builds
`Aggregation.newAggregation(LookupOperation.newLookup().from("other_collection").localField(...)
.foreignField(...).as(...))` and calls `mongoTemplate.aggregate(agg, "base_collection",
Object.class)`. Real output:

```
collectionsAccessed=[base_collection, other_collection]
collectionSources={base_collection=MONGO_TEMPLATE, other_collection=AGGREGATION_API}
```

Both collections are captured, correctly distinguished by source tag, and — per the
`CollectionResolver.java` 1486–1493 citation above — `other_collection` is ALSO recorded separately
under the CallNode's structured `pipeline.lookupTargets`, not merely folded into the flat
`collectionsAccessed` set. Base collection is unaffected by `$lookup`'s presence (a control fixture
without `$lookup` — `NoLookupStatic`/diagnostic test — resolves `base_collection` alone, identically).
**No implementation work is proposed for Q2 — it is a documentation/verification finding, not a
gap.** (Note: an earlier fixture attempt using camelCase collection names, e.g. `"baseCollection"`,
was rejected by `DomainConfigLoader.isLikelyCollectionName`'s naming heuristic — lines 457–470 require
either all-lowercase `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` or `UPPER_CASE_WITH_UNDERSCORE` — which is a fixture-authoring
pitfall, confirmed via a `$lookup`-free control case with the same camelCase name, NOT a `$lookup`- or
aggregation-specific defect. Snake_case naming, matching this repo's own established test-fixture
convention (`MongoTaggingTest`'s documented `"orders"`/`"ORDER_COL"` choices), avoids it.)

**Q2b — representation-shape coverage: does NOT depend on the static type being exactly Spring
Data's `Aggregation`.** `AggregationDetector.detect()`/`buildRichPipelineDetail` dispatches by
**method-owner-class-name pattern matching on `InvocationRef`s** (e.g. `ownerMatchesTemplate` at
line 836 checks `owner.endsWith("MongoTemplate")`/`"MongoOperations"`/etc.; `simpleOwner.contains(
"Lookup")` at line 403; `"Aggregates".equals(simpleOwner)` at line 480), not on the Java *type* of
any single argument. Real proof, `q2b_rawDocumentPipelineShape` — one real compiled class using
`org.bson.Document`/`List<Document>` native-driver style
(`db.getCollection("base_collection_doc").aggregate(List.of(new Document("$lookup", new
Document("from","other_collection_doc")...)))`), zero Spring Data `Aggregation` type anywhere. Real
output: `collectionsAccessed=[base_collection_doc, other_collection_doc]`,
`collectionSources={base_collection_doc=NATIVE_DRIVER, other_collection_doc=PIPELINE_RUNTIME}` — both
collections captured correctly, confirming the Document/`List<Document>` shape (Section A in
`AggregationDetector.java`'s own class-doc) is independently handled, not merely tolerated as a side
effect of the Aggregation-object path. (A plain-`String` JSON-pipeline shape — `AggregationDetector`
Section handling `extractLookupDetail`/`LOOKUP_FROM_PATTERN` regexes, lines 133–140, 753–770 — was
read and cited but not independently re-compiled-and-probed in this pass; it is a regex-based path
structurally separate from both shapes actually tested here, and is not blocking `CALL-018/019/020`
below.)

**Regression-safety constraint (mandatory, verbatim, applies to all of `CALL-018/019/020` below):**

> `$lookup` target must be tracked as a SEPARATE collection reference, never merged into/replacing
> the base collection. The base/primary aggregation collection must ALWAYS continue to be captured
> correctly even when `$lookup` is present — this is a mandatory regression-safety constraint on any
> new work, verified by re-running the full existing test suite after any change.

### §229 — `CALL-018` implemented: single-hop return-value (`ARETURN`) resolution closes §225's Q1 gap for the narrow single-hop shape; the 2-hop `q1` fixture honestly stays unresolved (that's `CALL-019`)

**Scope**: read `BytecodeClassParser.java` and `CollectionResolver.java` in full first, plus re-read
`Call018ReturnValueAndLookupProbeTest.java`'s existing `q1` fixture (§225's own real, javac-compiled
proof of the gap) to understand the exact bytecode shape to make resolvable.

**Design decision — this is NOT the ancestor-call-chain walk `CALL-001/002` use.** `tagGeneralParamCallSite`
et al. answer "who called ME with this parameter" by walking UP `ancestorCallChain`. A return value
flows the OPPOSITE direction: the caller (`D`) invokes a callee (`Y`) and needs to know what `Y`
itself unconditionally returns — that requires looking DOWN into `Y`'s own already-parsed body via
`ctx.classMap`, which is fully indexed before any resolution runs. No ancestor walk, no
`MAX_HOP_DEPTH` bound needed — resolution is a direct, O(1) callee-body lookup. This made the change
materially smaller and safer than initially expected from §225's own framing.

**`BytecodeClassParser.java` changes** (surgical, inside the existing per-method concat-fold
pre-scan block that already tracks `astoreCountBySlot`/`literalOnlySlotValue`/`concatSlotValue` —
no new top-level pass added):
- New per-slot map `returnCallSlotValue: Map<Integer, MethodInsnNode>` — populated ONLY when an
  `ASTORE` is DIRECTLY (adjacency-only, same discipline as the concat-fold operand window — only
  `LabelNode`/`LineNumberNode`/`FrameNode` are transparently skipped) preceded by a `MethodInsnNode`
  call, i.e. the classic `String x = other.foo();` idiom. A `pendingCallForReturn` tracking variable
  is cleared by every OTHER instruction kind (LDC, ALOAD, GETFIELD-literal, invokedynamic, the
  catch-all `else`), so this can never misattribute a stale, non-adjacent call as the value's source.
- New whole-method ARETURN scan (same block): counts every `ARETURN` in the method; resolves a
  `singleReturnLiteral` ONLY when there is EXACTLY ONE `ARETURN` in the whole method AND it is
  directly fed by an LDC string (mirrors `CALL-015`'s "exactly one PUTFIELD"/`astoreCountBySlot`'s
  "exactly one ASTORE" never-guess-across-branches discipline exactly). A second `ARETURN`, or an
  `ARETURN` fed by anything else (a field, a param, another call's result — e.g. `BService`'s own
  `return c.resolveCollectionName();` pass-through), leaves it unresolved. Gated additionally on the
  method's own return type being exactly `java.lang.String`. Result stored on the new
  `MethodInfo.singleLiteralReturnValue` field.
- In the existing ALOAD-tracking loop, a new `else if` branch (positioned alongside the existing
  literal/`concatSlotValue` branches, mutually exclusive with the generic PARAM/LOCAL_VAR fallback):
  when a slot's single assignment came from `returnCallSlotValue` AND the call's own declared return
  type is `java.lang.String`, emits a new `MethodCallInfo.DynamicArgSource("RETURN_VALUE",
  calledMethodName, calledOwnerClassFqn)` — reusing the existing 3-field `DynamicArgSource` record
  exactly the way `STATIC_FIELD`/`CONCAT_LITERAL_PARAM` already repurpose it for a second piece of
  data, zero record/schema changes needed.

**`CallGraphIndex.java`**: added `IndexedMethod.singleLiteralReturnValue`, copied straight from
`MethodInfo.getSingleLiteralReturnValue()` in the constructor — one field, one assignment line.

**`CollectionResolver.java`**: new `tryResolveSingleHopReturnValue(ddc, ctx)`, wired into the existing
`mergeDynamicResult` (the SAME merge point every detector's unresolved dynamic reference already
flows through — Mongo `TEMPLATE_METHODS`/`DATABASE_METHODS` unresolved calls AND
`AggregationDetector`'s `pipelineDetail.dynamicRefs` both call `mergeDynamicResult`, so this one wire-up
covers both paths the real gap trace showed, `MONGO_TEMPLATE_DYNAMIC` and `TEMPLATE_AGGREGATE_DYNAMIC`,
with no detector-specific code needed). Fires only for `varKind=="RETURN_VALUE"`; looks up
`ctx.classMap.get(ddc.ownerClass())`, matches by simple method name + zero declared parameters
(narrow but sufficient for this task's plain-getter-shaped scope — an exact descriptor match would
need `DynamicArgSource` to carry a 4th field), and returns that method's own
`singleLiteralReturnValue` if present. Resolved values are tagged with a NEW, distinctly-named source
`RETURN_VALUE_SINGLE_HOP_RESOLVED` — never reusing any existing `CALL_SITE_*`/`ENUM_CONSTANT_*` tag —
per this task's own requirement to keep return-flow provenance auditable separately from
argument-flow provenance.

**Verification — real, both directions confirmed on real compiled bytecode.**
1. Built a NEW, purpose-built single-hop fixture (`call018/src/q1single`,
   `call018/out/q1single`): `DRepoSingleHop.run()` calls `CBuilder.resolveCollectionName()`
   **directly** (no intermediate pass-through), stores the return in a local, passes it straight into
   `mongoTemplate.aggregate(...)`. New test `call018_singleHopReturnValueResolves` (added to the
   existing `Call018ReturnValueAndLookupProbeTest.java` probe file, per this task's own guidance not
   to create a whole new file for one test): confirms `collectionsAccessed=[invoices]`,
   `collectionSources={invoices=RETURN_VALUE_SINGLE_HOP_RESOLVED}`. **PASSES.**
2. Re-ran the EXISTING `q1_returnValuePropagationNotTraced` (§225's own 2-hop `C→B→D` fixture,
   `BService.getCollectionName()` being a PURE pass-through `return c.resolveCollectionName();`) —
   its `assertFalse` was deliberately NOT inverted, because this fixture genuinely needs a SECOND
   return-hop (`BService`'s own return is itself another call's return, not a literal — its
   `singleLiteralReturnValue` is correctly null) — exactly the case `CALL-019`'s own task-table row
   already calls out as its job, not `CALL-018`'s. Real output confirms the new machinery IS running
   (the node's `dynamicCollectionRefs` now show `varKind=RETURN_VALUE` entries, versus §225's original
   trace showing plain `LOCAL_VAR`), but `collectionsAccessed` for `"invoices"` correctly stays empty.
   Documented honestly here rather than force-fit a passing assertion onto a 2-hop fixture a

### §249 — bulk "export everything as one file" for both screens: investigation + plan only, nothing built

User request (verbatim intent): a single-file bulk export (zip, or one combined JSON) available on
BOTH the PL/SQL and JAR screens, covering every JSON artifact and source file an analysis produces,
with an OPTION to select a subset (source only, or one specific facet) instead of always downloading
everything. Per this session's own established discipline for new (not bug-fix) work, this section is
investigation + a proposed plan only — nothing implemented, no files changed.

**What actually exists on disk for the real PL/SQL analysis, `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`**
(`data/plsql-parse/ORACLE/ORACLEDEMO/LOCAL/ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE/`):
- `tables.json` (114,050 bytes) — one JSON object keyed by `SCHEMA.TABLE`, each with
  `schema`/`tableName`/`objectType`/`operations`/`lines`.
- `edges.json` (551,410 bytes) — the full edge list (this is the same "unbounded, deliberately"
  endpoint export.js's Table Detail modal relies on, per the comment at
  `ParserAnalysisController.java:367/486-487`).
- `progress.json` (2,016 bytes) — analysis run metadata.
- `plsql-env-config.yaml` — the environment config used for the run.
- `api/index.json`, `api/call_graph.json`, `api/node_id_map.json` — top-level API-facing JSON.
- `api/nodes/*.json` — one JSON file per procedure/function/trigger node, e.g.
  `api/nodes/ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL.json`, `api/nodes/ANALYZER$ERP_PKG_PLANNER$WALK_UP.json`
  (51 such files for this analysis's 51 nodes).
- `api/tables/index.json`, `api/statements/` — additional per-facet API JSON.
- `sources/*.{prc,fnc,sql}` — one real PL/SQL source file per object, e.g.
  `sources/ANALYZER.ERP_USP_RECOST_PRODUCTS.prc`, `sources/ANALYZER.ERP_PKG_PLANNER.SET_CONTEXT.sql`
  (52 files).
- `.node-cache/*.json`, `.parse-cache/*`, `chunks/chunk_NNNN.json`, `edges/`, `resolver/` — internal
  parse/cache scaffolding, NOT user-facing artifacts; an export feature should exclude these
  (they're implementation detail, would confuse a downloaded bundle, and some are keyed by
  content-hash filenames that mean nothing to a human).
- There is already a bulk, unpaged export-shaped endpoint precedent:
  `GET /analyses/{name}/procedures/export` (`ParserAnalysisController.java:555`, built for `UI-024`/
  `export.js`'s XLSX Call Flow/Complexity/Summary sheets) — deliberately returns every procedure,
  unpaged, "because export means every procedure."

**What actually exists for the real JAR analysis.** The only JAR analysis present on local disk is
the small `demo-app` fixture (`data/jar/demo-app/`: `analysis.json` 7,683 bytes, `_summary_static.json`
1,967 bytes + a `.gz` sibling, `_header.json`, `domain-config.json`, `external-links.json`/
`external-links-pending.json`, `stored.jar`, and `decompiled/` with 1 cached `.java` file for this
tiny fixture). The real large corpus this session has repeatedly measured against — `unified-web.jar`
itself, self-analyzed, `id=unified-web`, **10,704 classes, 286 endpoints** (§192 and onward,
`docs/TASK-REGISTRY.md:8640` first instance) — is not present as flat files in this pass's search
(consistent with this session's mode-4/mongodb-storage history: that analysis's artifacts live in
Mongo via `ArtifactStore`, not on local disk). Its artifact shape, per the same JSON structure the
`demo-app` fixture shows in miniature: a summary document, a per-endpoint report set (`endpoints`,
fetched via `GET /{id}/summary/endpoints` and friends), a class tree (`GET /{id}/classes/tree`,
`GET /{id}/classes/packages`), per-endpoint call trees (`GET /{id}/endpoints/by-index/{idx}/call-tree`),
and one decompiled `.java` source per class (`decompiled/<FQCN>.java`) — for a 10,704-class jar, that
is potentially 10,704 separate decompiled-source artifacts, most of which are almost certainly
decompiled lazily/on-demand rather than all pre-generated (the `demo-app` fixture only has exactly 1
cached `.java` for its 1 analyzed class, consistent with lazy/on-demand decompilation rather than a
bulk pre-decompile step).

**What export capability already exists today, and how good a foundation it is.**
- PL/SQL screen: `parser/js/export.js` (1,413 lines) drives a modal (`#exportModal`) with format
  choice (JSON/CSV/XLSX) and section checkboxes — `expSummary`, `expProcs`, `expTables`, `expJoins`,
  `expCursors`, `expSequences`, `expCallGraph`, `expComplexity` — plus a scope radio (Full/Subtree/
  SubFlow/Direct, defaulting to whatever scope is currently active) and a Detail/Summary level toggle.
  This is a genuinely close foundation for the "checkbox subset" half of the user's ask — it already
  has the exact UI pattern (checkboxes per facet, one modal, one download button) the user is asking
  for, generalized. It does NOT currently offer a raw-source-code option, does not bundle as a zip
  (JSON/CSV/XLSX only, one file per invocation, not a multi-file bundle), and gathers everything via
  already-loaded/fetched data or the `/procedures/export` endpoint — no dedicated "download all raw
  artifacts as-is" path.
- JAR screen: `jar/js/summary-export.js` (`exportAllReports()`) + `jar/js/summary-export-modal.js`
  (`showExportModal()`, supporting full-project / single-endpoint / single-collection scope) already
  export multiple JSON files per click (5 files: `_full_endpoint_report.json`,
  `_full_verticalisation.json`, `_full_distributed_transaction.json`, `_full_batch_job.json`,
  `_full_views.json`) via sequential `_downloadJSON()` calls — i.e. it ALREADY does a "download several
  JSON files" export, just as N separate browser downloads, not one bundled file, and only for these
  5 derived analytics reports (not raw class list, not decompiled source, not the full call-tree set).
  `JA.summary.exportEndpointDetail(idx)` shows the per-endpoint single-JSON pattern already reused for
  scoped export.
- Both are a solid foundation to EXTEND, not a reason to build from scratch: the checkbox-driven
  modal, the section-flags-into-a-gather-function pattern, and the scope (full/subtree/endpoint/
  collection) selector all already exist independently on both screens and only need (a) a "raw
  source code" checkbox/option added to each gather step, (b) a bundling step (zip) instead of N
  separate `_downloadJSON()`/format-branch calls, and (c) on the JAR side, an "Everything" preset that
  is genuinely new (today's JAR export only ever emits derived reports, never the class list, call
  trees, or decompiled source).
- No existing single-file (zip or combined-JSON) bundling mechanism was found on either screen —
  confirmed by `grep -rl "ZipOutputStream\|java.util.zip" unified-web/src/main/java`, which returned
  only `WarAnalyzerController.java` and `AnalyzerController.java` (both use it for reading the
  uploaded .jar/.war's own zip structure, not for producing a downloadable export bundle) — and by
  `grep -rn "Content-Disposition"` across all controllers, which found none. Any "single zip file"
  deliverable is new work, not a rename of something that already exists.

**Is a similar options-selection UI pattern reusable?** Yes — `export.js`'s `#exportModal` (PL/SQL) and
`summary-export-modal.js`'s `#export-modal-overlay` (JAR) are each already exactly the "checkbox list +
scope radio + format choice + one download button" shape the user is asking for; the new bulk-export
UI should be a THIRD/extended mode of these same modals ("Everything" as one more radio option
alongside the existing per-facet checkboxes), not a new invented widget.

**Bundling mechanism recommendation: server-side zip, not client-side.** Reasoning, from this
session's own real measured numbers:
- The PL/SQL analysis's artifact set is small (this analysis: ~52 source files + ~51 node JSONs +
  a handful of top-level JSON, well under a few MB total) — client-side zipping (e.g. a JS zip
  library, fetching each already-existing endpoint and bundling in the browser) would work fine here.
- The JAR analysis's decompiled-source artifact set does NOT scale the same way: a 10,704-class jar's
  full decompiled source, if it all had to be fetched into the browser and zipped client-side, risks
  exactly the browser-memory/time problem the task flagged. Recommendation: build the bundle
  SERVER-SIDE (a new endpoint that streams a `ZipOutputStream` response with `Content-Disposition:
  attachment`, using the same `java.util.zip` machinery already imported elsewhere in this codebase)
  and serve one download — this avoids browser memory limits for large exports, keeps the client
  simple (one `<a href>` / fetch-and-save instead of assembling megabytes of text in JS), and is a
  single mechanism that works identically for the small PL/SQL case and the large JAR case rather than
  needing two different implementations. The existing checkbox-driven modals stay client-side (UI
  only); they'd POST the selected facet list to the new server endpoint instead of gathering data into
  the browser themselves.
- New backend endpoint(s) ARE needed for server-side bundling — none of the existing endpoints return
  a zip today. However, most of the DATA-fetching endpoints needed to build each facet already exist
  and can be called server-side as-is (PL/SQL: `/analyses/{name}/procedures/export`, `/tables`,
  `/joins`, `/cursors`, raw `sources/*` files already on disk via `ArtifactStore`; JAR:
  `/{id}/summary/endpoints`, `/{id}/classes/tree`, `/{id}/endpoints/by-index/{idx}/call-tree`,
  decompiled `.java` per class) — the new endpoint's job is orchestration (call each, write each
  result into a `ZipOutputStream` entry) not re-deriving data that doesn't already have a producer.

**Size/performance concern: decompiling all 10,704 classes on demand for an export would be
prohibitively slow** if decompilation is genuinely lazy/on-demand (consistent with the `demo-app`
fixture caching only 1 `.java` for its 1 touched class — no evidence any bulk pre-decompile step
exists). Recommendation: the "Everything" / "source code" export option for the JAR screen should
either (a) be scoped to ALREADY-CACHED/already-decompiled classes only, clearly labeled as such
("N of 10,704 classes decompiled and included; the rest are listed by name only" or similar), or (b)
for a genuine "decompile everything and zip it" request, run as a background job with a
"your export is ready" notification/polling pattern (this session's own memory note already
establishes `/api/queue` as the one real progress-endpoint convention to reuse for that, rather than
inventing a new progress mechanism) instead of a blocking synchronous HTTP download that would time
out or hang the browser tab. The PL/SQL side has no equivalent scale problem (52 source files, all
already on disk) — its export can safely stay synchronous.
