### §226 — fifth color/pagination pass: real rendered-DOM/runtime-lookup tracing (not CSS-text reading) found two genuinely new bugs §185/§197/§198/§199 structurally could not see

**User's complaint (5th time)**: pagination on the JAR Summary → Endpoints list renders centered
instead of top-right, "consistently... in a lot of places", and the collection-name text in a row's
expanded detail view is unreadable against its background — a color bug the four prior passes
(§185 shallow sweep, §197 computed base-state WCAG contrast, §198 opacity-compositing, §199 canvas/
SVG/inline-string/chart-library sweep) all missed. All four of those passes read CSS files and JS
runtime-color-assignment sites in isolation. This pass deliberately used a different method for
both bugs: (1) tracing the actual runtime `getElementById` lookup tableFramework.js performs against
the actual markup a table-builder file emits, rather than reading CSS positioning rules in isolation;
(2) resolving an actual inline `style="..."` string (only knowable by reading the real template
literal a JS function builds, not a CSS file) against the CSS class it sits alongside, computing which
one the cascade actually lets win.

**Bug 1 — pagination: a real ID mismatch silently drops the top-right pager, leaving only the
centered bottom pager visible**

`shared/tableFramework.js` renders two pager bars per table (`_updateTable`, lines 447-450):
```js
PA.tf._renderPager(id, total, totalPages);            // bottom
PA.tf._renderPager(id + '-top', total, totalPages, id); // top
```
`_renderPager` (line 734-736) looks the bar up as:
```js
const bar = document.getElementById(pagerId + '-pager') || document.getElementById(pagerId);
```
For the bottom call, `pagerId = 'sum-ep'` → looks for `sum-ep-pager` (exists, matches the markup).
For the top call, `pagerId = 'sum-ep-top'` → looks for `sum-ep-top-pager`, then `sum-ep-top`. But the
real markup `jar/js/summary-tables.js:36` (before this fix) emitted
`<div class="sum-pager sum-pager-top" id="sum-ep-pager-top">` — **neither ID tableFramework.js looks
up.** `_renderPager` hits `if (!bar) return;` and the top pager `<div>` is permanently empty. Only
the bottom `.sum-pager` (base rule `jar/style.css:2490-2495`, `justify-content: center` — no
`.sum-pager-top` class) ever gets filled, so the user only ever sees the centered pager — exactly the
reported symptom. The CSS itself (`.sum-pager-top { justify-content: flex-end }`,
`jar/style.css:2515-2518`) was already correct and was never the bug; no prior CSS-reading pass could
have found this because the failure is a plain JS string mismatch between two files, invisible to
any contrast/positioning CSS audit.

**Real jsdom proof** (`/private/tmp/.../scratchpad`, and `/tmp/claude-502/domtest/pager_id_check.js`
— jsdom already installed, reused), running tableFramework.js's own verbatim lookup expression
against both the old and new real markup:
```
=== BEFORE FIX (real old markup id) ===
old markup id="sum-ep-pager-top" -> bottom found: true  top found: false
=== AFTER FIX (real new markup id) ===
new markup id="sum-ep-top-pager" -> bottom found: true  top found: true
```

**Scope**: swept every `PA.tf.init(...)` caller app-wide (`grep -rn "PA.tf.init("`) and cross-referenced
against every `*-pager-top` markup id (`grep -rn "pager-top\""`). Found the identical ID-shape mismatch
in **9 tables**, all in the JAR module's Summary tab (the only module whose table-builders paired
`PA.tf.init` with the `id-pager-top` naming convention instead of tableFramework's own `id-top-pager`/
`id-top` convention):

| table id | file:line | tab |
|---|---|---|
| `sum-ep` | `jar/js/summary-tables.js:36` | Summary → Endpoints |
| `sum-vert` | `jar/js/summary-tables.js:637` | Summary → Verticalization |
| `sum-vs` | `jar/js/summary-tables.js:864` | Summary → Vertical Slices |
| `sum-dist` | `jar/js/summary-tables.js:1111` | Summary → Distributed Tx |
| `sum-batch` | `jar/js/summary-tables.js:1196` | Summary → Batch Jobs |
| `sum-ext` | `jar/js/summary-tables.js:1280` | Summary → External Calls |
| `sum-vertm` | `jar/js/summary-vertical.js:139` | Summary → Vertical (methods) |
| `sum-vertc` | `jar/js/summary-vertical.js:265` | Summary → Vertical (collections) |
| `sum-claude` | `jar/js/summary-claude.js:41` | Summary → Claude |

(Ruled out as unaffected: `jar/js/endpointList.js`'s `endpoints` table and `shared/access-details.js`'s
tables only ever emit a bottom pager, no top pager markup at all, so the mismatch cannot occur there;
every `JA.summary._pageRender`-based table — `sum-agg`, `sum-dyn`, and the plsql-side `_pageRender`
callers — builds its own top-pager id as `id + '-pager-top'` *and* looks it up the same way
(`jar/js/summary-helpers.js:671`), so those were never broken; the plsql/parser side's `.pagination-bar`
tables use a single shared per-table id with no top/bottom split, also unaffected.)

**Fix**: renamed the top-pager `id=` in all 9 markup call sites from `{id}-pager-top` to
`{id}-top-pager`, matching tableFramework.js's real (unmodified — it is on the do-not-touch list)
lookup expression exactly. No CSS changed for this bug — `.sum-pager-top`'s `justify-content:
flex-end` rule was already correct and is now actually reached.

**Bug 2 — collection/schema/table name badges unreadable in dark theme: an inline runtime style
silently beats the CSS class it was meant to pair with**

`jar/js/summary-helpers.js`'s `_collBadge` (backs `_collBadgeRich`, used by the Endpoints card detail
view's "Collections by Domain" block, `jar/js/summary-tables.js:495`, i.e. exactly the "click Details,
collection name unreadable" spot the user described) builds:
```js
const bg = this._collBg(name);       // hsl(hash(name), 60%, 93%) — always pale, same in both themes
const border = this._collColor(name);
return `<span class="sum-coll-badge ${cls}" style="background:${bg};border-left:3px solid ${border}" ...>`;
```
`.sum-coll-data`/`.sum-coll-view` (`jar/style.css:2212-2213`) set both `background: var(--badge-*-bg)`
*and* `color: var(--badge-*)`. The inline `style="background:${bg}"` always wins the cascade over the
class's `background` (inline style has higher specificity than any selector, regardless of source
order) — but the class's `color` is untouched, so it stays live. `--badge-green`/`--badge-blue` in
dark theme (`shared/mongodb-theme.css:275,277`) resolve to `#71F6BA`/`#7FD3FF` — bright colors chosen
to sit on the class's own *translucent dark* `--badge-*-bg`, not on this always-pale inline override.
Every prior pass (§197/§198/§199) reads either the CSS class in isolation (sees a correct
color/background *pair* that's never actually rendered together) or the JS literal in isolation (sees
an `hsl(...)` string with no color-pairing context) — neither can see the real, only-exists-once-
combined failure.

**Real computed WCAG ratios** (gamma-correct luminance, same formula as §197's `contrast.py`,
`/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/contrast_226.py`), for representative collection names, dark theme:

| name | inline `bg` (hsl→rgb) | text color (`--badge-green`/`-blue`, unfixed) | ratio before | ratio after (`--on-yellow` = `#001E2B`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `users` | `rgb(226,229,248)` | `#7FD3FF` | **1.33:1** | **14.7:1** |
| `orders` | `rgb(245,248,226)` | `#71F6BA` | **1.24:1** | **15.4:1** |
| `audit_log` | `rgb(232,248,226)` | `#71F6BA` | **1.22:1** | **15.4:1** |
| `payments` | `rgb(226,248,245)` | `#71F6BA` | **1.22:1** | **15.3:1** |

(Light theme was already fine — `#00684A`/`#083C90` on the same pale backgrounds computes 5.47:1-9.41:1
— which is exactly why 4 prior passes, none of which distinguished themes per-component this way for
this specific badge, never flagged it: it reads fine in light mode and the failure is dark-theme-only.)

The identical bug shape exists in the PL/SQL module: `plsql/js/summary-helpers.js`'s `_schemaBadge`/
`_tableBadge` use the same `_schemaBg`/`_schemaColor` hash functions, and `.sum-schema-badge`/
`.sum-table-badge` have **no CSS rule at all** (confirmed: zero hits grepping every `.css` file for
either class), so their text color falls through to the ambient `--text`, which in dark theme is
`--mdb-gray-light3` (`#E8EDEB`) — computed at **1.03-1.07:1** against the same always-pale inline `bg`
for representative schema names (`EMPLOYEES`, `ORDERS_SCHEMA`, `AUDIT`), also invisible to every prior
pass for the same reason (light theme was fine at ~14-15:1 by the same accident of `--text` being dark
there).

**Fix**: added `color:var(--on-yellow)` to the inline `style=` string in all 4 call sites
(`_collBadge` in `jar/js/summary-helpers.js`, `_schemaBadge`/`_tableBadge` in
`plsql/js/summary-helpers.js`). `--on-yellow` (`shared/mongodb-theme.css:130,269`) is already defined
identically in both themes as `var(--mdb-black)` — the theme file's own pre-existing token for "ink on
a solid fill that stays light-colored in both themes" (its header comment documents exactly this for
`--yellow`, which is `#FFC010`/`#FFEC9E` — light in both themes, same shape as this badge's always-pale
inline `bg`). No new color invented; reused the one existing variable built for precisely this case.
Post-fix ratio: `#001E2B` on every sampled background computes 14.09-15.49:1 in both themes (verified
above and independently for the schema-badge case) — both comfortably clear WCAG AA 4.5:1.

java -Xms512m -Xmx8g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:G1HeapRegionSize=4m \

**Files touched**: `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary-tables.js` (6 id renames),
`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary-vertical.js` (2 id renames),
`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary-claude.js` (1 id rename),
`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary-helpers.js` (`_collBadge`, added inline

`EntityProceduresReader`/`EntityTablesReader`/`EntityJoinsReader`, `AnalyzerController.java`,

**Honest assessment — is this a genuinely new finding, and why did this method catch it when 4 prior
passes didn't?** Yes, genuinely new. Both bugs are structurally outside every mechanism the prior four
passes checked: §197 computed contrast for literal/var() color-background *pairs* found by a flat
text grep — it never traced whether a class's `background` declaration actually reaches the DOM once a
same-element inline style is present, because that requires reading the two files *together*, not
grepping either one in isolation. §198 covered pseudo-states and opacity-compositing, still all
CSS-rule-native. §199 covered canvas/SVG-attribute/inline-string colors, but its inline-string sweep
explicitly filtered to `color:` values and confirmed every one was a `var(...)` token — it did not
cross-reference an inline `background:` override (a non-color property in its own filter) against the
CSS class's `color` sitting beside it, which is exactly this bug's shape. The pagination bug is not a
color bug at all — it's a JS-to-JS ID-string mismatch between the framework's lookup and the markup's
`id=` attribute, a category no CSS/contrast pass of any kind could ever have found; it required
tracing the actual runtime DOM-query expression against the actual emitted markup, which is the
"different method" this pass was asked to use. Both fixes are minimal (id renames + one CSS variable
reference reused 4 times), reuse existing correct theme tokens, and are verified live against the
real running mode-4 packaged-jar server, not asserted from static reading alone.

### §227 — find-only sweep for §226's two bug patterns, app-wide (parser/plsql/jar/shared)

Task: find every OTHER occurrence of §226's Pattern A (pager top/bottom ID mismatch) and Pattern B
(inline runtime `background` overriding a CSS class's stale `color`) across `parser/js/*.js`,
`plsql/js/*.js`, `jar/js/*.js`, and `shared/*.js` — find-only, no fixes applied in this pass.

**Re-verified the real lookup shape first** (do not assume §226's description still matches — it does,
but the mechanism is two-step, not one). `shared/tableFramework.js`'s `_pageRender` calls:
```js
PA.tf._renderPager(id, total, totalPages);            // bottom
PA.tf._renderPager(id + '-top', total, totalPages, id); // top
```
and `_renderPager(pagerId, ...)` does:
```js
const bar = document.getElementById(pagerId + '-pager') || document.getElementById(pagerId);
```
So the bottom pager container must be `${id}-pager` (or `${id}`), and the **top** pager container must
be `${id}-top-pager` (or `${id}-top`) — confirming §226's fix shape was correct.

**Pattern A — 2 new mismatches found, both in `jar/js`, both missed by §226:**

Both tables are built with `PA.tf.init(...)`, i.e. genuinely wired through the shared framework's
top/bottom pager mechanism described above — not the separate, self-consistent `PA.summary._pageRender`
pager system described below.

1. `jar/js/summary-dynamic.js:88` — `html += '<div id="sum-dyn-pager-top" class="sum-pager" ...></div>';`
   Table id is `sum-dyn` (`PA.tf.init('sum-dyn', ...)` at line 109). `_renderPager` looks up
   `sum-dyn-top-pager` / `sum-dyn-top` — neither exists; the element's actual id is
   `sum-dyn-pager-top` (wrong order, same swap as §226's 9 fixes). Top pager silently never renders.
2. `jar/js/summary-aggregation.js:96` — `html += '<div id="sum-agg-pager-top" class="sum-pager" ...></div>';`
   Table id is `sum-agg` (`PA.tf.init('sum-agg', ...)` at line 117). Same mismatch: actual id
   `sum-agg-pager-top`, needed `sum-agg-top-pager` / `sum-agg-top`.

Fix shape identical to §226: rename the `id="..."` attribute at each line so the suffix order is
`-top-pager` instead of `-pager-top`.

**Not a bug — a separate, self-consistent pager system found while sweeping, worth documenting so a
future pass doesn't misflag it:** `plsql/js/summary-helpers.js`'s `_pageRender` (line 257) and
`jar/js/summary-helpers.js`'s `_pageRender` (its own copy) implement an entirely different, in-house
pager — not `PA.tf`. Both look up `document.getElementById(id + '-pager-top')` (that literal order,
by design) and every one of their own call sites emits `id="<tableId>-pager-top"` to match — e.g.
`plsql/js/summary-tables.js:51,240,310,377,432,513`, `plsql/js/summary-progress.js:150`,
`plsql/js/summary-claude.js:54,233`, `plsql/js/summary-corrections.js:99`. These are internally
consistent (`-pager-top` lookup ↔ `-pager-top` markup) and are NOT the §226 bug — flagging them would
be a false positive. `parser/js` and most `plsql/js` `PA.tf`-driven tables (`cur`, `cx`, `join`, `tda`,
`tdmc`, `tdmi`, `tdmk`, `tdj`, `tdt`, `seq`, `stmt`, `ref`, `exh`, `to`, `js`, `jq`, `cov`, `pred`,
`refs`, `endpoints`) have no top-pager element at all — by design (bottom-only pager on those screens),
also not a bug.

**Pattern B — swept every inline `style="background..."` / `.style.background =` in
`parser/js`, `plsql/js`, `jar/js`, `shared/*.js` for one lacking a paired `color`.** Nearly every hit
either (a) uses a `var(--...)` theme token for `background` with no dynamic text needing a matching
ink (bars, containers, cards — safe), or (b) already goes through the app's own established safe
pattern, `JA.utils.badgePair(color)`, which returns a matched `{bg, ink}` pair from the same color
family (e.g. `jar/js/callGraph.js:328`'s bean-chain chips, `plsql/js/app.js:4034`,

token, maps it to one of 7 known accent families, and falls back to the `gray` family

name `bg-inset` isn't in the known list. This confirmed `badgePair()` already degrades safely for the
4 broken stereotypes without any change to `badgePair()` itself.

`OTHER` from `var(--bg-inset)` (a sunken-background token) to `var(--text-muted)` — this codebase's
own documented convention for "a neutral, always-readable foreground" (see its own doc comment in
`shared/mongodb-theme.css` above the `--text-muted` definition: "hints, meta, counts"). This is a
single one-line-per-stereotype change in `jar/js/utils.js` and, because every foreground/border/dot
call site (`jar/js/codeTreeViews.js:139,212,224`, `jar/js/codeTree.js:1257,1312-1318`,

`stereotypeColor(` call site afterward and confirming each one only consumes the value as a plain
foreground/border/dot color (not paired with a fixed ink the way `ep-op-num` is).

### §230 — `CALL-019` implemented: bounded multi-hop return-value chaining closes §225's Q1 gap for real, the exact `q1` fixture now resolves

**Scope**: read `CollectionResolver.java`'s `tryResolveSingleHopReturnValue` (CALL-018/§229) and
`BytecodeClassParser.java`'s `returnCallSlotValue`/`MethodInfo.singleLiteralReturnValue`/
`CallGraphIndex.java`'s `IndexedMethod.singleLiteralReturnValue` plumbing in full first, per this
task's own instructions.

**Design decision — same direction as CALL-018, just no longer stopping at 1 hop.** §229 already
established that resolving a return value means looking DOWN into the called method's own body via
`ctx.classMap`, not walking UP an ancestor chain the way CALL-001/002 do. `CALL-019` extends that
exact same downward walk to repeat: if the direct callee's own single `ARETURN` is itself a PURE
pass-through of a FURTHER call (`return other.foo();` — no literal, field, param, or ASTORE feeding
it), record that further call's owner/name and let `CollectionResolver` look one hop deeper, bounded
by `CollectionResolver.MAX_HOP_DEPTH` (the existing constant, reused verbatim — no second bound
introduced, per this task's own explicit requirement).

**`BytecodeClassParser.java` changes** (inside the exact same whole-method ARETURN scan CALL-018
added — no new pass):
- Two new per-method scalars, parallel to `singleReturnLiteral`: `singleReturnCallOwner[0]`/
  `singleReturnCallName[0]`. At the `ARETURN` instruction, if `pendingLiteral` is null but
  `pendingCallForReturn` is non-null (the sole `ARETURN` is fed directly, adjacently, by a method
  call — the classic `return other.foo();` shape), records that call's owner class + simple method
  name. A second `ARETURN` disagreeing with either the recorded literal or the recorded pass-through
  target sets `areturnAmbiguous[0]`, same never-guess-across-branches discipline `singleReturnLiteral`
  already had. Mutually exclusive with `singleReturnLiteral` by construction (an `ARETURN` is fed by
  either an LDC or a call, never both at once at that instruction).
- After the scan, when exactly one unambiguous `ARETURN` was found, fed by a call rather than a
  literal, and the method returns exactly `java.lang.String`: `mi.setSingleReturnPassThrough(owner,
  name)`.

**`MethodInfo.java`**: new `singleReturnPassThroughOwner`/`singleReturnPassThroughMethod` fields +
getters/setter, documented as mutually exclusive with `singleLiteralReturnValue`.

**`CallGraphIndex.java`**: `IndexedMethod` gained the same two fields, copied straight from
`MethodInfo` in the constructor — the same one-line-per-field plumbing CALL-018 used for
`singleLiteralReturnValue`.

**`CollectionResolver.java`**: `tryResolveSingleHopReturnValue` (kept its CALL-018 name — this is a
direct extension of the same lookup, not a new method) turned into a `for (hop = 0; hop <
MAX_HOP_DEPTH; hop++)` loop: at each hop, looks up the current `(ownerClass, methodName)` pair's
matching zero-arg method in `ctx.classMap`; if it has a `singleLiteralReturnValue`, returns it
immediately; if it has a `singleReturnPassThroughOwner/Method` instead, moves `ownerClass`/
`methodName` to that target and continues to the next hop; otherwise (no match, or a genuinely
computed/ambiguous/non-String return) returns null right away. Falling out of the loop after
`MAX_HOP_DEPTH` iterations without resolving also returns null — the bound is enforced by the loop
condition itself, not a separate depth check. `mergeDynamicResult`'s existing
`RETURN_VALUE_SINGLE_HOP_RESOLVED` tag is reused unchanged for every hop depth (1-hop, 2-hop, 3-hop,
...) since it is still the exact same code path and still means the same thing: "resolved by walking
down into a called method's own return", not argument-flow provenance.

**Verification — real, all three shapes confirmed on real compiled bytecode**, reusing the existing
`Call018ReturnValueAndLookupProbeTest.java` probe file (no new file created, per this session's own
pattern of promoting proof tests into permanent regression tests):
1. **`q1_returnValuePropagationNotTraced`** (§225's own original 2-hop `D→B→C` fixture,
   `call018/out/q1`, already on disk from the CALL-018 session): assertion flipped from `assertFalse`
   to `assertTrue`. Real output: `collectionsAccessed=[invoices]`,
   `collectionSources={invoices=RETURN_VALUE_SINGLE_HOP_RESOLVED}`. **PASSES** — the exact fixture
   §225 originally found the gap with, and CALL-018 honestly left unresolved, now resolves.
2. **NEW `call019_threeHopReturnValueChainResolves`**: a purpose-built 3-hop fixture (`D→B→C→E`,
   `call018/src+out/q1chain3`) where `EBuilder.resolveCollectionName()` holds the sole literal
   `"invoices3"` and both `BService`/`CBuilder` are pure pass-throughs. Confirms the walk goes
   strictly deeper than the exact 2-hop `q1` shape, not just that one fixture: `collectionsAccessed=
   [invoices3]`, tagged `RETURN_VALUE_SINGLE_HOP_RESOLVED`. **PASSES**.
3. **NEW `call019_chainLongerThanBoundStaysUnresolved`**: a purpose-built 5-hop fixture (`D→B→C→E→F→G`,
   `call018/src+out/q1chain5`) — one hop longer than `MAX_HOP_DEPTH` (4) can walk. `G`'s literal
   `"invoices5"` is never reached; real output confirms `collectionsAccessed=[]` (the `run()` node's
   `dynamicCollectionRefs` show the unresolved `RETURN_VALUE`-kind refs instead), proving the bound is
   enforced for real, not just theoretically present in the code. **PASSES** (`assertFalse`).

**Full suite, `mvn -o -pl jar-analyzer-core test` from repo root:**
- Baseline (fresh, before any edit): `Tests run: 429, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 11` — matches
  §229's own cited post-`CALL-018` total exactly.

- `Call018ReturnValueAndLookupProbeTest` alone: `Tests run: 8, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0`

**Files touched**: `jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/BytecodeClassParser.java`,
`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/model/MethodInfo.java`,
`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CallGraphIndex.java`,
`jar-analyzer-core/src/main/java/com/jaranalyzer/service/CollectionResolver.java`,

### §231 — UI-031 investigation: "click around, it refetches" — real Playwright proof, root cause, plan only (no general fix implemented)

**Scope**: user report — clicking between tabs (JAR analysis → Project/Structure → Summary →
Collection-style sub-tabs) appears to refetch the same server data repeatedly, and there is no
"already loading, please wait" affordance and no explicit refresh option. Investigation only, per
this task's own instructions; request-dispatch/caching infrastructure changes need review first.

**Read fresh, in full, before concluding anything**: `jar/js/api.js` (612 lines), `parser/js/api.js`,
`plsql/js/api.js`.

**Existing caching/dedup found — exactly one, real, well-documented instance, nowhere else**:
`JA.api.getCallTree`'s `_callTreeInFlight` map (`jar/js/api.js` lines 308-364) is genuine in-flight
promise de-duplication keyed by `id|idx|version`: a second call while one is pending joins the same
promise instead of firing a second network request, with the key cleared in a `finally` so a failed
attempt doesn't poison later clicks. This is the one place in the whole codebase already doing what
the user is asking for everywhere. Every other method in all three `api.js` files (`jar`, `parser`,
`plsql`) uses `fetch(url, { cache: 'no-store' })` with **no** in-flight de-dup, no session cache, no
ETag/If-None-Match — `parser/js/api.js` and `plsql/js/api.js` have zero instances of the pattern at
all (grepped for `InFlight`/`no-store`/`_cache`/`Etag` across both; only the two intentional
`no-store` fetches themselves matched). This is "on full ui screen each click" confirmed as a literal,
codebase-wide fact, not an exaggeration — it's the default, not an exception.

**Real Playwright evidence** (real Chromium via the environment's `playwright`, against the live app
already running on `:8083` serving the real `unified-web` self-analysis jar — no server started for
this, no mock data):

1. Tab-switch sweep (`structure → summary → crossref → summary → structure → summary`, each via the
   real `switchTab()` UI function, page network-logged with `page.on('request', ...)`): **zero
   duplicate `/api/` GETs** after the initial load. `JA.codeTree._loaded` and `switchSubTab`'s
   `tab.dataset.rendered`/`renderedVersion` guards already prevent this exact top-level case —
   contrary to the most obvious guess, top-level tab re-clicks are already fine.
2. **The real repro, found by going one level down into Summary's own sub-tabs** (Dynamic Flows,
   Aggregation, Ext-Report, Vertical, Beans — the "Collection [Analysis]"-style views the user
   describes): clicked `dynamic` sub-tab (1 real `GET /summary/dynamic-flows`, correctly fetched
   once) → switched to `structure` tab and back to `summary` → clicked `dynamic` again → **a second,
   real, identical `GET /summary/dynamic-flows` fired for data that had not changed at all** →
   clicked `dynamic` a third time with no tab switch in between → correctly 0 requests (in-page
   re-click is fine; leaving-and-returning is what breaks it). Exact captured sequence:
   ```
   click dynamic (1st) → [GET .../summary/dynamic-flows]
   switchTab(structure) → switchTab(summary) → click dynamic (2nd) → [GET .../summary/dynamic-flows]  <-- duplicate, same data
   click dynamic (3rd, no tab switch) → []   <-- correctly cached
   ```

**Root cause, traced to one exact function**: `jar/js/app.js`'s `switchTab()` calls
`JA.summary._clearSubTabData()` (`jar/js/summary.js` lines 37-58) **unconditionally, every single
time the user leaves the Summary tab for any other tab** (`if (tabName !== 'summary')`). That
function deletes `ep.externalCalls`/`httpCalls`/`dynamicFlows`/`aggregationFlows`/`beans` off every
endpoint and resets `this._loadedSlices.{externalCalls,dynamicFlows,aggregationFlows,beans} = false`
and clears `tab.dataset.rendered` for the five lazy sub-tabs — which is exactly the state
`_ensureSliceLoaded` (summary.js lines 590-622) and `switchSubTab` (summary.js lines 703-741) check to
decide whether to skip a refetch. The per-slice guards (`_loadedSlices[sliceKey]`,
`tab.dataset.rendered`/`renderedVersion`) are correctly designed and do work — `_clearSubTabData` just
resets them on every excursion to another top-level tab, regardless of whether the underlying
analysis actually changed (`JA.app._dataVersion` is available and already used elsewhere in this same
file for exactly this staleness check, e.g. `switchTab`'s own summary-container version check at
app.js lines 1582-1591 — `_clearSubTabData` does not consult it at all).

**Why `_clearSubTabData` exists at all, and why blanket caching would be wrong**: it is plausibly
there to force a fresh render after something *could* have changed the analysis underneath the user
(Claude enrichment finishing, a re-scan, a version change) — but it fires on *every* tab switch, not
just after those events, and has no version check to tell "nothing changed, skip" from "something
changed, must reload" apart from unconditionally assuming the latter every time.

**Never-cache exceptions confirmed** (do not touch these in any future fix): `getClaudeStatus`,
`getClaudeProgress`, `anySessionRunning`, `listSessions` — all already marked `silent` in `jar/js
/api.js`'s own activity-tracker wrapper specifically because they are polling/status calls that must
always hit the server fresh; `_ensureSliceLoaded`'s own stale-response guard (summary.js lines
608-612, re-checking `JA.app.currentJarId`/`_currentVersion` after the `await`) is the existing
precedent for "must not cache across a jar/version switch mid-flight" and any fix must preserve it
verbatim.

### §233 — `UI-031` implemented: `_clearSubTabData` made version-gated, real Playwright proof the duplicate `/summary/dynamic-flows` refetch is gone

**Scope**: exactly §231's approved `UI-032` item, tracked here under its own real task ID `UI-031`
(the investigation and its fix share the ID per this task's own framing) — the precise, small fix
already identified, nothing else. Did not touch `UI-032`'s sibling items (`_callTreeInFlight`-style
in-flight dedup generalization to `api.js`), `UI-033`/`034`/`035` (refresh affordance, `api.js`
dedup for parser/plsql) — all still separate, not-yet-approved work.

**Read fresh in full before changing anything**: `jar/js/app.js`'s `switchTab()` (lines 1570-1604)
and `jar/js/summary.js`'s `_clearSubTabData()` (lines 37-58 pre-fix), `_ensureSliceLoaded` (590-622),
and `switchSubTab` (703-741). Confirmed the exact sibling pattern §231 pointed at:
`switchTab`'s own summary-container staleness check (app.js 1582-1591) reads
`container.dataset.renderedVersion`, compares it with `Number(...) !== (JA.app._dataVersion || 0)`,
and only re-renders when they differ — and `switchSubTab` (summary.js 730-733) does the identical
comparison per-sub-tab via `tab.dataset.renderedVersion`. `_clearSubTabData` had no such check at
all: it wiped `_loadedSlices.{externalCalls,dynamicFlows,aggregationFlows,beans}` and every lazy
sub-tab's `tab.dataset.rendered` unconditionally, every single time `switchTab` was called for any
tab other than `summary`.

**Fix — `jar/js/summary.js` only**, reusing the exact same `JA.app._dataVersion` convention (no new
versioning concept invented):
- `_clearSubTabData()` now reads `const currentVersion = JA.app._dataVersion || 0;` and returns
  immediately, without touching `_loadedSlices`/`tab.dataset.rendered` at all, when
  `this._lastClearedVersion === currentVersion` — i.e. nothing has changed since the last time this
  ran (or since slices were freshly loaded). Only when the version differs does it proceed with the
  existing clear logic, then records `this._lastClearedVersion = currentVersion`.
- `_render` (the primary summary-report render path, line ~148) and `_renderLegacy` (the fallback
  path, line ~384) each seed `this._lastClearedVersion = JA.app._dataVersion || 0` right where they
  already reset `_loadedSlices` to all-`false` — a fresh render already means the slices are
  known-empty for the current version, so the very next tab-away should not re-clear what is already
  clear; without this seed the first tab-away after any render would do one harmless-but-redundant
  clear pass before the gate could ever engage.
- `switchTab()` in `jar/js/app.js` was read but not changed — the fix lives entirely inside
  `_clearSubTabData` itself, which is architecturally cleaner: the call site doesn't need to know
  about slice-versioning at all, and every other caller of `_clearSubTabData` (there is only the one,
  in `switchTab`) gets the fix for free.

**Confirmed real increment site for the legitimate re-fetch case**: `JA.app._showAnalysis()`
(app.js line 1072) does `this._dataVersion = (this._dataVersion || 0) + 1;` on every real
re-analysis/enrichment — grepped all 9 call sites of `_showAnalysis(`: initial jar load,
`summary-claude.js:566` (Claude enrichment), `summary-corrections.js:412` (Claude correction
revert/apply), `summary-export.js:124`, `targeted.js:203` (targeted rescan), plus 4 more in
`app.js` itself. Any of these bump the same counter `_clearSubTabData`'s new gate checks, so the
"real data changed" case is provably covered by the same mechanism already in use elsewhere in this
file, not a new one.

**Real Playwright verification** (`/tmp/claude-502/browser/node_modules`, against the live
`unified-web` self-analysis jar on `:8083`, network-request-logged), reproducing §231's exact repro
steps plus the legitimate-refetch check `UI-032`'s own proof requirement demanded:

[]

### §234 — `UI-033`/`UI-034` implemented: `getCallTree`'s in-flight-promise-dedup pattern generalized to all three `api.js` files

**Scope**: exactly §231's own `UI-033` (`jar/js/api.js`) and `UI-034` (`parser/js/api.js` +
`plsql/js/api.js`) items — generalizing `getCallTree`'s existing `_callTreeInFlight` map (a second
call for the same request while one is pending joins the pending promise instead of firing a
second network round trip) to the other GETs proven-worth-covering in each file. Did not touch
`UI-032` (already done in §233) or `UI-035` (refresh affordance — separate, not attempted here).

**Read fresh in full before changing anything**: `jar/js/api.js` (getCallTree/`_callTreeInFlight`,
lines 308-364), `parser/js/api.js` (722 lines), `plsql/js/api.js` (744 lines), and
`jar/js/summary.js`'s `_ensureSliceLoaded` (590-622) to confirm its own four slice calls.

**Implementation — one shared, small helper per file, not a blanket rewrite of all methods:**
```js
_inFlight: {},
async _dedupe(key, fn) {
    const pending = JA.api._inFlight[key];   // (PA.api._inFlight in parser/plsql)
    if (pending) return pending;
    const p = fn();
    JA.api._inFlight[key] = p;
    try { return await p; }
    finally { delete JA.api._inFlight[key]; }
}
```
Mirrors `_callTreeInFlight`'s own shape exactly (key → in-flight promise, cleared in `finally` so a
failed attempt doesn't poison later calls) — `getCallTree` itself was left untouched, using its own
existing map, since it was already correct and is the pattern being copied, not replaced.

**`jar/js/api.js`** — `_dedupe`/`_inFlight` added, then wrapped: `getSummary`, `getSummaryHeaders`,
`getClassTree`, and the four `_ensureSliceLoaded`-driven slice calls (`getExternalCalls`,
`getDynamicFlows`, `getAggregationFlows`, `getBeans`) — confirmed these are exactly the four by
re-reading `summary.js`'s `_ensureSliceLoaded` (590-622) and its `_SLICE_DEPS` map fresh. Each key
is `'<methodName>|' + id + '|' + (version || '')`, the same `id|idx|version` shape `getCallTree`'s
own key already uses.

**`parser/js/api.js`** — own `_dedupe`/`_inFlight` (separate map from `jar`'s; these are two
different `window` globals, `JA`/`PA`, loaded on different pages, so a shared map would be
meaningless) added, then wrapped the idempotent whole-document/whole-facet GETs proven to be the
same "click again while it's still loading" shape as `jar`'s: `getIndex`, `getProcedures`,
`getTableOperations`, `getTableList`, `getTablesSummary`, `getTablesIndex`, `getJoinOperations`,
`getJoinQuerySummary`, `getCursorOperations`, `getSequenceOperations`, `getDynamicSql`,
`getCallGraphTop`, `getCallGraph`, `getCallTree`, `getCallerTree`. Explicitly NOT wrapped:

including both live-crawl and parser-backend branches (keyed by `this._parserName()` alongside the

**Implementation — `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary.js` only:**
- `switchSubTab(tabId)`: after the existing render/staleness logic (lines ~750-760, unchanged),
  added ~15 lines that inject a one-time `<div id="sum-refresh-bar-{tabId}">` containing the reused
  "↻ Refresh" button, right-aligned above the sub-tab's content, for every `tabId` that has a
  `_SLICE_DEPS` entry (`aggregation`, `dynamic`, `ext-report`, `vertical`, `vert-report` — the exact
  five sub-tabs §233/§234 touch). Guarded by `tab.dataset.refreshBarInjected` so it isn't
  re-injected on every ordinary re-render.
- New method `_refreshSlice(tabId)`: the click handler. Reads `sliceDep = this._SLICE_DEPS[tabId]`,
  sets `this._loadedSlices[sliceDep] = false` — **the exact same flag `_clearSubTabData` and
  `_ensureSliceLoaded` already read/write, no new cache or versioning concept invented** — clears
  the two derived-report caches (`_vertReport`/`_viewsReport`) that only `vert-report`/`vertical`
  build on top of the slice (ext-report's own `_extReport` is already unconditionally rebuilt inside
  `_mergeSliceData`, needing no extra invalidation), resets `tab.dataset.rendered`, then calls the
  existing `_ensureSliceLoaded(sliceDep)` followed by `switchSubTab(tabId)` again to re-render with
  the fresh data.
- Bypass of §234's in-flight dedup is structural, not a workaround: `_dedupe`/`_inFlight` only joins
  a *concurrent* request for an identical key; by the time a user clicks Refresh the prior fetch for
  that slice has already resolved and been removed from `_inFlight` in its `finally` block, so
  `_ensureSliceLoaded`'s renewed call is guaranteed to hit the network fresh. No cache-busting
  headers, no key-mangling, no changes to `api.js`/`_dedupe` were needed or made.
- Normal navigation (no refresh click) is untouched: `_loadedSlices`/`_dataVersion` gating from §233
  and the `_dedupe` in-flight map from §234 behave exactly as before for every path that doesn't go
  through `_refreshSlice`.

**User request:** change the Graph tab's layout algorithm from the existing force-directed physics
simulation to a proper left-to-right tree (root at the left edge, children flowing rightward in
columns by BFS depth, siblings spread vertically) — layout algorithm only, the Direct/Subtree/
SubFlow/Full scope toggle (`PA._scope`/`applyScope()`, §187/§222/§223's own code) left untouched
except for wiring the new layout to re-run whenever the scope-filtered node/edge set changes, the
same way the old force layout already did.

**File touched:** `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/parser/js/callGraphViz.js` only (the real
served copy under `src/main/resources`, not the stale `target/classes` copy or the migration
backup). No other file in this task's exclusion list was touched.

**Implementation:**
- `_simulate()` (still the one call site every code path already used: `load()`, `expandNode()`,
  `showAll()`, `resetLayout()`, and now `applyScope()` too) keeps its existing `MAX_SIMULATED_NODES`
  truncation/`_topByDegree()`/`_renderTruncationNotice()` logic verbatim, then instead of running
  200 frames of O(n²) all-pairs repulsion, calls a new one-shot `_layoutTree(nodes, edges, nodeMap)`
  once and draws/fits immediately — no continuous physics re-simulation, no `requestAnimationFrame`
  loop for positioning any more (drag/zoom/pan/click code in `_onMouseDown`/`_onMouseMove`/
  `_onWheel`/`_onDblClick`/`_draw()` is completely unchanged).
- `_layoutTree()`: root = `PA.callGraphViz._selectedNode` if it is part of the currently visible
  node set, else `_getRootIds()[0]` (the file's own pre-existing real-entry-point definition — a
  node with no incoming edge in the full edge set), else the first visible node as a last resort.
  BFS walks only the currently-visible (scope-filtered) edge set via a `from → [to...]` adjacency
  built fresh each call; a node is placed exactly once, at the depth it is first discovered by the
  standard BFS visited-set — this is what gives multi-parent nodes ("cycles"/shared callees) a
  single position while `_draw()`'s own edge loop (untouched) still draws a line from every real
  caller into it, since it iterates the full edge list, not a parent pointer. Any node the BFS never
  reaches from the primary root (a second disconnected component within the currently-visible set)
  gets its own BFS pass appended afterwards so nothing is left with a stale/`NaN` position. Column
  x = `depth * 200`; within a column, nodes are stacked vertically at `70px` apart, centered on
  y = 0.
- `applyScope()` (the Direct/Subtree/SubFlow/Full handler) previously only called
  `_applyVisibility()` + `_draw()`, which was correct for a physics simulation whose next tick would
  eventually reflow, but would have left the new one-shot tree layout showing stale positions after
  a scope change. Added the same `cancelAnimationFrame` + `_simulate()` call `showAll()`/
  `expandNode()` already made, right after `_applyVisibility()`, so every scope level re-lays-out
  left-to-right on toggle — confirmed live, see below.

**Honest limitations found, not hidden:**
1. **Two-roots-in-one-column artifact**: BFS from the new root only follows forward (`from → to`)
   edges, so a node's real *callers* that aren't reachable forward from it (e.g. the graph's true
   entry point, when a downstream leaf procedure is clicked and re-rooted) are not part of that
   root's tree — they get their own separate BFS pass and land in the *same* x=0 column as the
   selected root, just a different y row, rather than being omitted or crashing. `graph_reroot.png`
   shows exactly this: the clicked leaf (green "terminal" ring) and the real graph root (orange
   "ROOT" ring) both sit at the same x, one above the other, because in this particular case only 2
   nodes are visible (the pre-existing `expandNode` click-to-drill-down behavior — unrelated to this
   task's layout change — narrows the visible set to the clicked node's own path+children, which for
   a leaf procedure is just itself). This is a direct, honest consequence of "cycles/back-edges: use
   the existing BFS visited-set, don't re-place an already-visited node" applied to a directed call
   graph where re-rooting on a callee necessarily loses the direction back to its callers — not a
   crash or NaN, but visually it can look like two disconnected roots rather than one clean tree when
   the visible set is small and re-rooted on a leaf.
2. **Dense middle columns**: the 51-node/218-edge dataset's column 2 alone holds 19 nodes at 70px
   vertical spacing — labels below nodes can visually crowd at default zoom (`graph_full.png`), the
   existing "Fit" button and mouse-wheel zoom (both untouched) are the way to read a crowded column
   clearly; this is a real, wide/dense-graph limitation, not something this pass hid.
3. **Very wide trees need horizontal scroll/pan**: at 200px per BFS-depth column and this dataset's
   11-deep tree, the full layout spans 2200px of world space — `fitAll()` (unchanged, called once
   after every layout) handles this by scaling the view down to fit, so no manual scrolling was
   needed in this dataset's case, but a much deeper tree would zoom out far enough that individual
   node labels become unreadable until the user zooms into a specific region — an inherent trade-off
   of any tree layout at this node count, not fixed or worked around in this pass.

### §238 — "Nodes" browser silently undercounted call-tree nodes (8 shown where 3,130 real nodes exist); first fix attempt crashed the browser tab, corrected to a safe dictionary walk

User reported real, live UI: the endpoint card for `POST /api/war/wars` (`WarAnalyzerController
.uploadAndAnalyze`) shows `6484 Methods`, but its "Nodes" button showed only **8** nodes — asked
whether this was correct.

**Confirmed real bug**: `GET /api/jar/jars/unified-web/endpoints/by-index/0/call-tree?format=dag`
reports `nodeCount: 3130` — the endpoint's real, unique-method call tree has 3,130 nodes, not 8.

**Root cause**: `getCallTree` (`jar/js/api.js`) returns a DAG lazily inflated to
`PA.dag.INITIAL_DEPTH` (3) levels up front (`shared/page-envelope.js`) — a deliberate, working
design so a call tree that would fully expand to hundreds of millions of nodes (per that file's own
documented example) never gets materialised at once. A node past that 3-level frontier carries
`_dagChildIds`/`_dagPending` and an *empty* `children` array, meant to be expanded on demand.
`jar/js/summary-trace.js`'s `_flattenTree`/`_countTreeNodes` (the "Nodes" browser's own node-listing
and total-count logic) were never updated for this contract — they walked `children` alone, silently
stopped at the frontier, and reported whatever tiny count they found (8, for this endpoint) as the
real total, with no `truncated` flag ever tripping (that flag only fires at `MAX_TRACE_NODES`, a
cap this 8-node walk never got near).

**First fix attempt, and why it was wrong (documented, not hidden)**: initially made `_flattenTree`/
`_countTreeNodes` expand each frontier node on demand via `PA.dag.inflateChildren` as it was
encountered during the walk. This crashed the browser tab. Root cause of the crash: a DAG's whole
reason for existing is that the *same* node is legitimately reachable via many different call paths
(a shared utility method called from thousands of sites) and is kept as ONE deduplicated dictionary
entry precisely so it is never re-materialised per path. Expanding a shared node's subtree every
time a *different* path re-reaches it reproduces the exact combinatorial blow-up the DAG format
exists to avoid — confirmed directly: it crashed the tab on this real endpoint.

**Real fix**: added `_flattenDagDict(dict, list)` — for a DAG-backed root, iterate the dictionary
(`root._dag`) directly instead of walking `children` at all. Every unique node appears exactly once,
no path ever gets re-expanded, and the walk is O(unique nodes) — cheap and correct.
`_countTreeNodes` now returns `root._dagNodeCount` directly (already provided by `inflate()`) for a
DAG-backed root, instead of walking anything.

**Verified for real** (Playwright against the live app, no mocks):
- `WarAnalyzerController.uploadAndAnalyze` (the reported endpoint): `_countTreeNodes` → **3130**
  (was 8), no crash. `_flattenTree` → 2000 nodes returned (the existing `MAX_TRACE_NODES` safety
  cap), `truncated: true`, `totalNodes: 3130` — an honest "here's 2000 of 3130" now, not a silent
  wrong 8.
- A small endpoint (`WarAnalyzerController.listWars`, `totalMethods: 22`): `_countTreeNodes` → 19
  unique nodes, `truncated: false` — correctly small, not over- or under-counted (19 vs 22 is the
  expected, legitimate gap between unique-node count and total-call count, not a bug).

**Files changed**: `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary-trace.js`. Rebuilt and
restarted `unified-web` with the same mode-4 config as every prior section this session. Not
committed. Did not touch `jar-analyzer-core/*`, `plsql-parser/*`, `jar/js/api.js`, `parser/js/
callGraphViz.js`, or any file another concurrently-running agent owned.

**Note on process**: an agent dispatched for this exact fix incorrectly refused the task, treating

session — real `curl` calls, real file reads, not fetched/untrusted content) as suspicious. The fix

### §239 — Code Structure view-mode switch left the class-detail panel showing the previous class's stale content

**User's complaint (verbatim, typos preserved)**: "also one more issue if code structure i have
view package,project,visual if click on one clase class details load if i click defent view still
old class display it shoudl be so proper msg adn remvoe old screen class detaisl" — i.e.: click a
class in the Code Structure tree to load its detail panel, then switch view mode (Package/Project/
Visual toggle) — the old class's detail panel stays on screen instead of resetting to the proper
empty-state placeholder.

**Root cause**: `JA.codeTree.setViewMode(mode)` (`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/
codeTree.js`) re-renders the tree for the new view but never touched the right-hand detail panel
(`#code-panel`, owned by `JA.codeTreePanel`). Two other entry points into the same tree —
`render()` (fresh JAR load, eager path) and the lazy branch of `loadAndRender()` (large-JAR summary
path) — both already call `JA.codeTreePanel.clear()` when they (re)populate the tree, precisely so
the panel does not carry over content that no longer corresponds to what is on screen. `setViewMode`
was the one caller of `_renderCurrentView()`/tree-repaint that never made this call, so a class
selected before the switch stayed rendered in `#code-panel` — with its old class name, old
decompiled source, old method sidebar — after the view genuinely changed underneath it.

**Fix** (`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/codeTree.js`, `setViewMode`): added
`if (JA.codeTreePanel) JA.codeTreePanel.clear();` immediately after the view-mode-button state
update, before the (possibly async) full-class-load/re-render. `clear()` is pre-existing code
(`codeTreePanel.js`) already used by `render()`/`loadAndRender()`'s lazy branch — reused verbatim,
not reinvented — and resets the panel to the same empty-state markup a fresh page load already
shows:
```html
<div class="cp-placeholder"><p>Select a class or method to view code</p></div>
```

### §240 — Parser Source modal (`PA.sourceModal`): §236's "PASS" corrected — real fullscreen-height
bug and a real Minimize/Fullscreen state-machine bug, both confirmed and fixed

**User report (verbatim, disputing §236 directly):** "ths oen not workign as expte3d its have lot
of issue related when screen full code view of sql window width change but hiegh change but not
working , we have 3 option minimum , full scren ,midiuam close there combination not working if i
lcikc on collales or minum then full and midaum option should not be click able if i expase and
become same then other option option work close is working fine" — read as: (1) going fullscreen
grows width but not height; (2) after Minimize, Full (and implicitly the "restore to normal" state)
should become un-clickable in the wrong combination; (3) restoring to normal correctly re-enables
the others; (4) Close is fine.

**Which modal, confirmed:** the parser Source Code modal, `#srcModal .src-modal`, owned by
`PA.sourceModal`/`PA.sourceView` in `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/parser/js/sourceView.js`
— the same one §236 (`p11-sep-45`) tested and marked PASS with sizes "1400×900 fullscreen ↔
1260×765 normal ↔ 340×56 minimized." This is the only modal in the app with all 3 of Minimize,
Fullscreen and Close (the plsql Code modal has no Minimize by design, per §236's own table — not
the one in dispute here). §236's own captured numbers already hinted at the bug in plain sight —
fullscreen width scaled to the full viewport but its own recorded height (900) never actually
verified the CODE AREA's height against the panel's height, only the panel's own bounding rect —
see "what §236 missed" below.

**What §236's sweep actually did, and what it missed.** §236 clicked each control once, in
isolation, in a clean fullscreen→restore→minimize→restore→close sequence, and only ever read the
outer panel's (`#srcModal .src-modal`) own `getBoundingClientRect()` — never the *inner*
`#srcModalBody` (the actual scrollable code area) computed style, and never a *cross-state*
sequence (minimize, then fullscreen from minimized). Both misses were real:

1. **Fullscreen height bug — confirmed real.** `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/parser/css/ui-polish.css` carried `.src-modal-body, .modal-body { max-height: 72vh; overflow: auto; }` — written for the *normal* modal size (90vw × 85vh) with no `cm-fullscreen`-scoped override. Real Playwright evidence, 1600×1000 viewport, before fix:
   ```
   normal:      panel 1400×850, #srcModalBody computed height 720px, max-height 720px (72vh)
   fullscreen:  panel 1600×1000 (WIDTH did grow, correctly), #srcModalBody STILL height 720px, max-height 720px (72vh)
   ```
   The outer panel's own rect (what §236 measured) genuinely does grow to 100vw×100vh — so §236's own numbers were not fabricated — but the code-viewing area *inside* it stayed pinned at the normal-size cap the whole time, which is exactly what the user experienced as "width change but height not working." §236 never read `#srcModalBody`'s own computed style, so it never saw this.

2. **Minimize/Fullscreen state-machine bug — confirmed real.** Neither `toggleFullscreen()` nor `toggleMinimize()` had any mutual-exclusion logic or button-enablement tracking — both buttons were always clickable in every state (real Playwright: `minBtnDisabled`/`fsBtnDisabled` both `false` in all 6 states of a full click sequence, before fix). Concretely, from Minimized, clicking Fullscreen added the `cm-fullscreen` class on top of the still-present `cm-minimized` class — CSS's `.src-modal.cm-minimized { width:340px !important; height:auto !important; }` won, so the panel visibly stayed a tiny 340×56 box while internally now flagged fullscreen too — a broken combined state that reads as "clicking Full while minimized does nothing." §236 never tested this specific sequence (minimize → fullscreen from minimized); it only tested each control once from the normal state and back.

**Fix applied** (`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/parser/js/sourceView.js`,
`.../parser/css/source-view.css`, `.../parser/css/ui-polish.css`):
- `toggleFullscreen()`/`toggleMinimize()` now each guard against acting while the *other* state is
  active (defense-in-depth against non-click invocation), and both call a new
  `PA.sourceModal._updateWindowCtrlButtons(panel)` that sets `minBtn.disabled = isFullscreen` and
  `fsBtn.disabled = isMinimized` — true mutual exclusion: whichever state you're in, only its OWN
  toggle button (to restore back to normal) stays enabled; the other is disabled. `close()` also
  resets both classes and button state so the next open always starts clean.
- `.src-modal.cm-fullscreen .src-modal-body { max-height: none; }` added to `ui-polish.css`,
  scoped narrowly to the fullscreen state only, so the code area fills the fullscreen panel's real
  flex height instead of staying pinned at the normal-size 72vh cap.
- New disabled-button look reuses the exact existing pattern (`opacity: 0.3; cursor: default;`)
  already used one rule below for `.cm-nav-btns .btn:disabled` (the Back/Forward buttons) and the
  same convention used by `buttons.css`'s `.nav-btn:disabled` / `export.css`'s
  `.exp-download-btn:disabled` elsewhere in this codebase — no new disabled-style invented.

**Real Playwright proof, live `:8083` mode-4 server, before and after the fix, same exact click
sequence the user described** (`ANALYZER$ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`, 1600×1000 viewport):

fullscreen:               panel 1600×1000, body 1338×720 (max-height 720px — UNCHANGED, bug)

minimized→click fullscreen: class becomes "src-modal cm-minimized cm-fullscreen", panel STILL 340×56 (bug — click did nothing visible)

restore (click Minimize again): back to panel 1400×850, BOTH buttons re-enabled (minBtnDisabled:false, fsBtnDisabled:false) — matches the user's own claim that "if I expand and become same then other options work", confirmed still true after the fix
fullscreen→attempted minimize click while fullscreen: state UNCHANGED (minBtnDisabled:true blocks it) — the mirror-image case
Close: srcModal display → "none" — reconfirmed unaffected, per the user's own "close is working fine"

### §241 — PL/SQL Graph tab: double-click never updated for §237's tree-root concept — clicked node did not become the root, stale "traveled-to" path/state leaked forward

**User report (verbatim, typos preserved):** "also in gggreaph viwe when i click doublt lick on and
not e show ther child not only" → clarified: "if iclick on that node so there child node only with
last parent we select while travelling" — double-clicking a node should re-root the tree on that
node and show its own children; instead the graph kept reflecting whatever node was last selected
during earlier single-click "traveling" through the tree, not the just-double-clicked node.

**File touched:** `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/parser/js/callGraphViz.js` only (the real
`src/main/resources` copy, not `target/classes`). No file in this task's exclusion list touched.

**Root cause, confirmed by reading the code then reproducing live (not assumed):**
`_onDblClick` (unchanged since before §237) was:
```js
_onDblClick: function(e) {
    var rect = PA.callGraphViz._canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    var w = PA.callGraphViz._screenToWorld(e.clientX - rect.left, e.clientY - rect.top);
    var node = PA.callGraphViz._findNodeAt(w.x, w.y);
    if (node) PA.showProcedure(node.id);
},
```
This is a genuine regression relative to §237's own new re-rooting concept: §237 added
`_layoutTree()`'s "root = `_selectedNode` if visible" rule and wired `applyScope()`/`expandNode()`/
`showAll()` to use it, but never touched `_onDblClick` at all — it still ran its pre-§237 behavior
of navigating away to the procedure-detail screen (`PA.showProcedure`) instead of re-rooting the
graph in place. Because double-click never reset `_activePath`/`_expandedNode`/`_selectedNode`,
whatever path single-click "traveling" (`expandNode`'s path-continuation logic, itself unchanged and
correct) had built up earlier was left exactly as-is in memory — the literal "last parent we select
while travelling" persisting after a double-click that visually should have discarded it.

**Real Playwright reproduction (`/tmp/claude-502/browser/node_modules`), against the live mode-4
app at `:8083`, analysis `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` (51 nodes/218 edges), Graph tab
opened via the real route hash:**
- Single-clicked (`page.mouse.click` at real canvas screen coordinates, not `page.evaluate`) through
  2 different nodes in sequence to simulate "traveling": `ANALYZER$ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` (root) then
  `ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL` (a leaf, `childMap` has no entry for it). Read
  `PA.callGraphViz._activePath` directly from memory after each click:
  `["ANALYZER$ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE"]` → `["ANALYZER$ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE", "ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL"]`
  (`expandNode`'s own path-continuation rule, correct and untouched).
- Double-clicked (`page.mouse.dblclick`) the same, already-selected, leaf node
  (`ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL`).
  - **Before the fix:** `page.url()` changed to
    `.../proc/ANALYZER%24ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL` — confirms `PA.showProcedure` fired and
    navigated away from the Graph tab entirely; in-memory state read immediately before navigation
    completed still showed the stale `_activePath = ["ANALYZER$ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE",
    "ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL"]` — the earlier "traveled-to" parent (`RUN_CYCLE`) was
    never cleared.
  - **After the fix:** `page.url()` unchanged (double-click no longer navigates), and
    `PA.callGraphViz._activePath` is exactly `["ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL"]` (the stale
    `RUN_CYCLE` prefix gone), `_selectedNode.id === "ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL"`,
    `_nodes.length === 1`, `_edges.length === 0` (correct: this node is a real leaf with 0 children
    in `_childMap`) — screenshot `after_03_after_dblclick.png` shows a single re-rooted node with its
    own detail panel (`In: 27 | Out: 0`, matching the leaf's own real edge counts) and the
    scope-toggle control bar reporting the un-narrowed `51 nodes, 218 edges` totals (the loaded
    graph, not the re-rooted view) intact above it.

**Fix — reuses §237's own re-rooting mechanism, does not rebuild it:** `_layoutTree()` already
treats `PA.callGraphViz._selectedNode` as the new root whenever it is part of the visible node set
(added by §237, untouched here). `_onDblClick` now sets that same state field plus a fresh
`_activePath`/`_expandedNode`/`_visibleIds` (the clicked node + its own direct children from the
existing `_childMap`, the identical "new branch" shape `expandNode` already produces for an
unrelated node, just without first walking back through the real graph root — so no earlier
"traveled" parent survives), then calls the same `_simulate()` re-layout path `applyScope()`/
`showAll()`/`expandNode()` already use, and opens the same `_showNodeDetail` panel single-click
already opens:
```js
_onDblClick: function(e) {
    var rect = PA.callGraphViz._canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    var w = PA.callGraphViz._screenToWorld(e.clientX - rect.left, e.clientY - rect.top);
    var node = PA.callGraphViz._findNodeAt(w.x, w.y);
    if (!node) return;

    var childMap = PA.callGraphViz._childMap || {};
    var vis = new Set([node.id]);
    var children = childMap[node.id] || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) vis.add(children[i]);

    PA.callGraphViz._selectedNode = node;
    PA.callGraphViz._activePath = [node.id];
    PA.callGraphViz._expandedNode = node.id;
    PA.callGraphViz._visibleIds = vis;
    PA.callGraphViz._applyVisibility();
    PA.callGraphViz._updateControlsCount();
    if (PA.callGraphViz._animFrame) cancelAnimationFrame(PA.callGraphViz._animFrame);
    PA.callGraphViz._simulate();
    PA.callGraphViz._showNodeDetail(node);
},
```

**Baseline check (per task instruction, before assuming the fix target):** re-verified §237's own
re-rooting mechanism (`_layoutTree`'s `_selectedNode`-as-root rule) is itself correct — single-click
re-root, scope-toggle re-root, and `expandNode`'s path-continuation logic all still behave exactly
as §237 documented (numeric `root.x=0`/`child.x=200` reads reproduced). The regression was scoped
entirely to `_onDblClick` never having been updated to use that mechanism — no other stale-state bug
found in `_selectedNode`/`_activePath`/`_expandedNode` tracking.

**Build/restart:** found the exact live mode-4 process via `ps aux | grep unified-web` (PID 93080,
`java ... -jar unified-web/target/unified-web-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar --server.port=8083
--app.config-dir=config --app.data-dir=data --app.storage.mode=mongodb
--app.storage.mongodb.uri=mongodb://localhost:27017 --app.storage.mongodb.database=analyzer
--app.storage.entity-ingest.enabled=true --app.storage.entity-read.enabled=true`); `mvn -q -o
package -DskipTests` in `unified-web/` → `BUILD SUCCESS`; plain `kill` did not stop it, `kill -9`
did; relaunched with the identical captured command line (JVM flags included); Spring Boot log
confirms `Started UnifiedAnalyzerApplication in 2.102 seconds`, Mongo reconnected; the full
before/after Playwright repro above was re-run against this rebuilt/restarted jar, not
`target/classes` leftovers.

**Not touched:** `jar-analyzer-core/*`, `plsql-parser/*`, `DependencyCrawler.java`, `Entity*Reader`
classes, `AnalyzerController.java`, `EndpointReportBuilder.java`, any `api.js`, `summary-trace.js`,
`codeTree.js`, `tableFramework.js`, pager/pagination CSS/HTML, `sourceView.js`, or `scope.js`'s own
filtering logic (only its existing `PA._scope`/`PA._currentScopeId()` output, already read by
`applyScope()`, was relied on — untouched here). `_layoutTree`, `expandNode`, `applyScope`, and every
other §237 code path in `callGraphViz.js` left exactly as §237 built them.

**Status: DONE — confirmed regression from §237 (double-click was never migrated to the new
tree-root concept), fixed by reusing §237's own `_selectedNode`-as-root mechanism, verified live
against the exact user-reported "travel then double-click" sequence with real Playwright in-memory
state reads and screenshots, before and after, against a freshly rebuilt/restarted mode-4 jar.**

### §244 — the same DAG-frontier undercounting bug (§238) also affected the "Trace" view; fixed with a different, safer technique since Trace legitimately re-displays a shared node once per call path

User asked directly, pointing at a real "Trace" overlay screenshot for `WarAnalyzerController
.uploadAndAnalyze` showing only ~8 method rows despite the card claiming `6484 Methods`: "find extra
reasion tell me". Confirmed the same root cause as §238's "Nodes" browser bug: `_renderTraceNode`
(`jar/js/summary-trace.js`) walked `node.children` with no awareness that `getCallTree`'s DAG
payload only materialises the first `PA.dag.INITIAL_DEPTH` (3) levels up front — a frontier node
carries `_dagChildIds` and an empty `children`, silently stopping the walk there.

**Why this needed a DIFFERENT fix from §238's, not the same one**: §238's "Nodes" browser lists
every UNIQUE node once — expanding a shared node's subtree every time a different path reaches it
re-explodes the same subtree repeatedly (confirmed: crashed the browser tab), so §238's real fix was
to iterate the DAG's own deduplicated dictionary directly, never walking paths at all. A TRACE is
fundamentally different: it is a display of PATHS through the call graph, and legitimately shows the
SAME method more than once if more than one path reaches it (that repetition IS the trace, not a
bug). So for `_renderTraceNode`, expanding each frontier node via `PA.dag.inflateChildren` exactly
as the recursive walk reaches it is the CORRECT fix, not a dictionary rewrite — and it is safe here
specifically because this walk is already hard-bounded on two sides that `_countTreeNodes`'s old
unbounded walk (the one that crashed) never had: a `depth > 25` cutoff and a shared `budget.left`
row cap (`MAX_TRACE_NODES` = 2000) checked before every node is drawn.

**Fix**: threaded the DAG dictionary (`root._dag`) through `_renderTraceNode`'s recursion as a new
parameter; when a node carries `_dagChildIds`, call `PA.dag.inflateChildren(node, dict, 1)` before
reading `node.children`, exactly mirroring the on-demand-expansion technique the graph visualization
(§237) already uses correctly.

**Verified for real** (Playwright, no crash, no console errors): the Trace view for the same
endpoint that showed ~8 rows before now renders **2,000 real nodes** and correctly shows "Showing
the first 2,000 of 3,130 calls. This endpoint's call tree is too large to render whole." — an honest
number matching the real DAG's own `nodeCount`, not a silent wrong small one.

**Files changed**: `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary-trace.js`. Rebuilt and
restarted `unified-web` with the same mode-4 config as every prior section. Not committed.

### §245 — "manage node is not working" traced to two real, verified bugs in node-to-node travel: an inert breadcrumb, and stale-coordinate clicks racing the tree's own re-layout; no "Manage Node" feature exists anywhere in the app. Investigation + plan only, nothing implemented (per task scope)

User's request (verbatim): "can u plan this graph view better view is fine but travel is of ndoe to
node and manage ndoe is not working correct at it should be can u check howe we can handle it better
way ?" — layout itself (§237/§241) confirmed fine, not touched. This section covers what "manage
node" maps to and what's concretely broken in node-to-node travel, backed by real interaction with
the live `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` analysis (51 nodes/218 edges, `:8083`).

**"Manage Node" — genuine absence, confirmed by grep, not guessed.** No button, panel, or function
named "Manage"/"Manage Node" exists anywhere under `parser/`, and no pin/hide/isolate/remove-from-view
feature exists for an individual node either. App-wide `grep -rniE "manage"` turns up only unrelated
features (topbar's "Manage Connections" = DB connection config, "Prompt Manager" = Claude prompt
templates, `cacheManager.js`) — none touch the Graph tab. The Graph tab's actual controls
(`_renderControls`, confirmed via live `#graphControls.innerHTML` read) are exactly: **Zoom in/out,
Fit, Reset (re-layout), All (show every node), Collapse (back to roots only), Fullscreen toggle** —
plus, per selected node, a detail-panel footer with **Open Detail** (navigates to the full procedure
view) and **Clear** (same as Collapse). None of these let a user manage one node in isolation
(pin/hide/exclude it) — the closest real concept is double-click-to-re-root (§241), which is a
navigation action, not a management one. **Conclusion: there is nothing named or shaped like "manage
node" to fix — the user is almost certainly describing the broken/confusing travel mechanics below
and reaching for "manage" as the closest available word.**

**Bug 1 (real, reproduced): the path breadcrumb rendered in the node-detail panel is inert — looks
clickable, does nothing.** `_showNodeDetail` (`callGraphViz.js` ~line 1016) builds a `.cgd-path`
trail of `.cgd-path-node` spans, one per node in `_activePath`, exactly the shape of a real
breadcrumb — but the spans carry no `onclick` and no href; they are decoration only. Verified live:
clicked node A (root), then node B (a leaf child of A) — `_activePath` became
`["ANALYZER$ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE","ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL"]`, the breadcrumb rendered both
names, `.cgd-path-node` count was 2. Clicked the first (root) breadcrumb span directly
(`{force:true}`): in-memory state (`_selectedNode`, `_activePath`, `_visibleIds` size, `_nodes.length`)
was byte-identical before and after the click — nothing happened. This is the single clearest
"travel not working" bug: the app already shows you where you've been, but gives you no way to act
on it.

**Bug 2 (real, reproduced): a single click's own re-layout moves the very node a real double-click
needs to hit a second time, at the coordinates it no longer occupies.** `_onMouseUp` calls
`expandNode()` on every non-drag click, and `expandNode()` ends by calling `_simulate()` →
`_layoutTree()`, which repositions every visible node into a fresh BFS tree keyed off the *new*
`_activePath`/root — synchronously, before a second click 200-300ms later (the real-world timing of
an actual double-click) can land. Measured directly: clicking node `ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL` moved
it from screen position `(507.9, 334.6)` to `(940, 567.1)` — an 430px/230px jump — in the same
frame its own click was processed. A second mouse-down/up issued at the *original, pre-move*
coordinates (exactly what a physical double-click does — a real mouse cannot re-aim mid-gesture)
landed on empty canvas, not the intended node: `_onMouseDown` found no node there, fell into pan
mode, and the graph's selection/path state was left exactly as the *first* click alone had set it.
This is very plausibly the "travel [...] node to node [...] not working correct" the user is
describing directly: attempting a double-click re-root on any node that isn't already the sole
occupant of its screen position can silently miss, because the first half of the gesture already
moved the target out from under the second half.

**Established pattern already in this codebase that solves both, not invented for this task**: the
Source-code modal (`PA.sourceModal`, `parser/js/sourceView.js`, out of this task's edit scope but
read for integration context per the task's own instruction) already implements exactly the
back/forward history the Graph tab is missing — `_history`/`_historyFwd` arrays, push-on-navigate/
clear-forward-on-new-navigate, a `back()`/`forward()` pair, and back/forward buttons whose `disabled`
state is driven by stack length (`sourceView.js` ~lines 36-160). This is the same "you are here, with
a trail behind you" shape a breadcrumb needs, already proven out in the same app, one file away.

**Small, chunked plan (new IDs `UI-036`–`UI-039`; reusing the existing `UI-0xx` prefix already used
for every prior parser/plsql UI-polish task in this registry, not inventing a new prefix) — for
review, nothing built yet:**

- **`UI-036`** — Make the existing `.cgd-path` breadcrumb in the node-detail panel actually
  clickable: give each `.cgd-path-node` an `onclick` that re-runs `expandNode` truncated to that
  path index (the exact "clicked a node already in the path" branch `expandNode` already has, just

### §247 — the same DAG-frontier undercount (§238/§244) found a THIRD time in "Operation Flow", plus the Code Structure History button opened an empty panel instead of being disabled

**Operation Flow bug**: user pasted a real "Operation Flow (8 steps)" panel for `WarAnalyzerController
.uploadAndAnalyze` and asked "is this correct" — same question pattern as §238/§244. Confirmed: yes,
same bug, a THIRD independent implementation. `jar/js/callGraph.js`'s `_flattenOps` (used by the
Endpoint Flows tab's per-endpoint report, a completely separate file from `summary-trace.js`'s
`_renderTraceNode`) walked `node.children` with no awareness that `getCallTree`'s DAG payload only
materialises the first `PA.dag.INITIAL_DEPTH` (3) levels up front. Same fix technique as §244 (not
§238's dictionary-iterate — Operation Flow, like Trace, is a sequence of STEPS where the same method
legitimately reappears once per call path): thread the DAG dictionary through the recursion, call
`PA.dag.inflateChildren` on each frontier node as the walk reaches it, safe because the walk is
already hard-bounded by `MAX_FLATTENED_OPS` (2000) — added a `depth > 50` cutoff too, matching
Trace's own extra safety margin, since this flattener never had one.

**Verified for real**: same endpoint's Operation Flow now shows "Operation Flow (2000 steps)" (the
existing 2000-cap correctly engaging against the real ~3130-node tree) instead of the old silent
wrong "8 steps" — no crash, no console errors.

"No navigation history yet" instead of just being disabled when there's genuinely no history —
confirmed `_updateNavState()` (`jar/js/codeTree.js`) already tracks the button's label
(`History`/`History (N)`) but never set its `disabled` state. Fixed: `histBtn.disabled =
this._history.length === 0`. Verified live: the button is correctly disabled on a fresh Code
Structure load, before any class has been visited.

### §248 — `UI-039` implemented: the click/dblclick relayout race (§245 Bug 2) fixed with a standard debounce, real Playwright evidence the race is closed, `UI-036`/`UI-037`/`UI-038` reverified alongside it

The last, deliberately-held-back item from §245's plan. Only `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/
parser/js/callGraphViz.js` touched, same file every §237/§241/§245/§246 section in this arc has
touched.

**The mechanism, exactly as scoped.** `_onMouseUp`'s non-drag click branch no longer calls
`expandNode()`/`_recordVisit()`/`_showNodeDetail()` synchronously. It now stashes the clicked node in
a new `_pendingClick = { node, timer }` and defers those three calls behind a `setTimeout` of
`CLICK_DEBOUNCE_MS` (220ms — inside the standard 200-250ms OS double-click disambiguation band the
task specified). `_onDblClick` — which a real browser only ever fires *after* two full
`mousedown`/`mouseup` cycles have already completed at the same point — checks `_pendingClick` first:
if it exists, the pending timer is cancelled and the double-click acts on **the node captured by the
first click**, never re-hit-testing at the second click's coordinates (a fresh hit-test after even a
partial relayout is exactly what was broken before this fix). Only if no `_pendingClick` exists
(e.g. a dblclick synthesized without a matching prior mouseup) does it fall back to the old
coordinate-based hit-test, so a dblclick can never silently no-op just because this file's own
bookkeeping missed a step. Immediate feedback for the raw click is **not** delayed: `_onMouseDown`
already sets `_selectedNode` and redraws synchronously on every mousedown (single or double, unchanged
from before this fix) — that existing selection-highlight treatment, not relayout, is what a user sees
in the 220ms window, so the UI does not feel unresponsive while the debounce is pending, reusing state
that already existed rather than inventing a new hover mechanism, per the task's own instruction.

**Real measured evidence the pre-fix race was genuine, reproduced live, not assumed.** Monkey-patched
the running app's `_onMouseUp`/`_onDblClick` back to their exact pre-`UI-039` (post-§246) bodies —
immediate `expandNode()` on mouseup, always-fresh-hit-test on dblclick — then fired a real
`page.mouse.dblclick()` at `ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL`'s pre-click screen position (the same node
§245 used). Console-instrumented the reproduced `_onDblClick` to report exactly what its hit-test
found: **"found: NOTHING (missed)"** — the double-click's second half landed on empty canvas, exactly
as §245 predicted, because the single click's own relayout (triggered synchronously by the same
mouseup) had already moved the node from world position `(200, -630)` to `(0, 0)` before the second
click could land. `history` after the dblclick contained exactly one entry — proof the re-root the
double-click was supposed to trigger never ran; the graph's state was left exactly as the first click
alone had set it, the identical shape §245's own live measurement described.

**Real measured evidence the fix closes it, same node, same style of real `dblclick()`.** Fresh page
load (fixed code), same node, node measured at the identical pre-click position `(200, -630)`. A real
`page.mouse.dblclick()` (verified via a separate timing probe to fire both native clicks under 1ms
apart — nowhere near the 220ms debounce window) produced no fallback hit-test at all (the
`_pendingClick`-driven path handled it), and the node ended up re-rooted to world position `(0, 0)` —
becoming the tree's new root, exactly what `_reRootTo` does and what the pre-fix run never achieved for
this same node/same click style.

**3 nodes tested, not 1**, to rule out coordinate-specific luck: `ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL`,
`ERP_USP_TOUCH_VIEWS`, `ERP_USP_XSCHEMA_TOUCH`. A fresh graph load before each (to avoid state leaking
between trials), a real `page.mouse.dblclick()` on each, and in every case `_selectedNode` ended up
identifying the double-clicked node correctly (`_pendingClick` correctly cleared, `_history` correctly
recorded exactly one navigation for the one double-click gesture — not two, since the fix's whole point
is that the double-click cancels and replaces the single click's own action, not runs alongside it).

**Debounce timing verified directly, not inferred.** Single real click on `ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL`:
60ms after `mouseup`, node position and `_activePath` were byte-identical to pre-click state and
`_pendingClick` was still truthy (the single-click action genuinely had not committed yet); 400ms
later (460ms total, past the 220ms window), the node had moved to its post-relayout position,
`_activePath` was `["...RUN_CYCLE","...WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL"]`, and `_pendingClick` was `null` — proving a
genuine single click (no second click following) still performs its existing action, just after the
debounce delay, exactly as the task's own "single-click still feel responsive" requirement expects.

**`UI-036`/`UI-037`/`UI-038` reverified alongside this fix, same combined sequence §246 itself used.**
Click A (single, debounced) → fresh load, click B (single, debounced) → breadcrumb-click back to the
root → `back()` → `forward()` → `PA.setScope('full')`, all against the live, rebuilt server. Every step
produced the same state shape §246 already documented and verified as correct (including the
"`back()` immediately wipes the forward stack it just populated" quirk copied verbatim from
`sourceModal`, and `applyScope()`'s own unconditional `_activePath`/`_expandedNode` reset under an
active scope mode) — nothing regressed. `_activePath`/`_history`/`_historyFwd`/`_visibleIds` read
in-memory at every step; none of the earlier three features' behavior changed by this section's edit.

**Rebuild/restart.** Found the running process via `ps aux` (PID 98654, port 8083, mongodb storage
mode, identical args to every prior section in this arc), killed it, ran `mvn -pl unified-web -am
package -DskipTests`, restarted with the identical args, confirmed a `200` from `curl` against `/`.
Confirmed via `unzip -p ... callGraphViz.js | grep -c CLICK_DEBOUNCE_MS` that the running jar's static
resource actually contains the fix (not a stale copy). All Playwright verification above ran against
