### §250 — floating help/theme/chatbot/log/export buttons made consistent bottom-left/bottom-right across jar, parser and plsql, replacing three genuinely different layouts

**Real before-evidence, per page, per control (Playwright `getBoundingClientRect()`, not assumed):**

| Control | jar (before) | parser (before) | plsql (before) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Theme toggle | floating bottom-right (`right:20,bottom:92`) | docked inside `.topbar-actions` (top area, ~`x:552,y:63`) | docked inside `.topbar-actions`, genuinely top-right on the analysis screen (`x:1408,y:7`) |
| Help "?" | floating bottom-**right** (`x:1470,y:928`) | floating bottom-**left** (`x:66,y:944`) | **absent** — `help.css`/`help.js` were never included on this page at all |
| Chatbot (`cbx-fab`) | bottom-right (`x:1520,y:920`) | bottom-left (`x:114,y:944`) | bottom-right (`x:1520,y:920`) |
| Log FAB (shared) | bottom-left (`x:28,y:920`) | bottom-left (`x:18,y:944`) | bottom-left (`x:28,y:920`) |
| Export | none page-wide (only per-endpoint, from Summary rows) | inline in `.topbar-actions`, top (`y:69`) | inline in `.topbar-actions`, top (`y:14`, i.e. literally top-right) |

This is the exact complaint: three pages, three different corners for the same controls, and
plsql additionally missing a help button entirely. Screenshots: `/tmp/claude-502/browser/before_*.png`
(jar/parser home+analysis, plsql home) and `/tmp/claude-502/browser/before_plsql_analysis_*.png`
(plsql with a real analysis loaded, proving the top-right theme/export placement).

**Root causes found by reading source, not guessed:**
1. `shared/theme-toggle.js` preferred `document.querySelector('.topbar-actions, ...')` as a dock host
   before falling back to floating — parser/plsql have `.topbar-actions`, jar doesn't, so the same
   shared script produced two different layouts depending on which page loaded it.
2. `shared/help.css`/`help.js`, `shared/chatbox.css`, `shared/log-fab.css` each hard-coded their own
   independent `left`/`right` fixed offsets with no shared convention — nothing tied them together
   into one cluster.
3. `plsql/index.html` never included `help.css`/`help.js` at all (confirmed absent from its
   `<script>`/`<link>` list vs. jar/parser, which both have it).
4. `parser/css/ui-polish.css` had a page-only `!important` override already pinning log/help/chat into
   one bottom-left row (`.log-fab, .help-btn, .chat-fab, .cbx-fab { ... left: 18/66/114px }`) — this
   masked the shared-CSS fix on the first rebuild/verify pass (log FAB still bottom-left on parser only,
   caught by the after-screenshot diff, not assumed fixed).
5. Export was never a floating control anywhere — parser/plsql have it inline in `.topbar-actions`
   (top), jar has no page-wide export at all (only a per-endpoint one from Summary/Endpoint Report rows,
   confirmed by grep — `jar/js/summary-claude.js`'s `JA.summary.showExportModal({endpointIdx})`).

**The fix — shared CSS is the primary mechanism, exactly as preferred by the task:**
- `shared/theme-toggle.js`: removed the `.topbar-actions` docking branch entirely; the toggle now
  always floats (`btn.classList.add('mdb-theme-toggle--floating')`) regardless of page chrome, so one
  code path produces one position everywhere.
- `shared/help.css` (`.help-btn`): moved from `bottom:32,right:90` to `bottom:28,left:28` — 1st slot in
  the bottom-left cluster.
- `shared/mongodb-theme.css` (`.mdb-theme-toggle--floating`): moved from `right:20,bottom:92` to
  `left:84,bottom:28` — 2nd slot.
- `shared/chatbox.css` (`.cbx-fab`/`.cbx-panel` + the `max-width:480px` responsive block): moved from
  `right:28` to `left:140` (fab) / `left:140` (panel) — 3rd slot.
- `shared/log-fab.css` (`.log-fab`): moved from `bottom:28,left:28` to `bottom:28,right:28` — now the
  anchor of the bottom-**right** cluster instead of sharing the bottom-left corner with help/chat.
- `shared/mongodb-theme.css`: added `.global-export-fab` (fixed `right:92,bottom:28`, pill-shaped,
  paired left of the log FAB) and `.global-logs-hidden` (`display:none!important`).
- `parser/index.html` / `plsql/index.html`: the existing inline `.topbar-actions` Export button got
  `global-export-fab` added to its class list (pulling it out of the top bar into the shared
  bottom-right cluster, `onclick="PA.export.show()"` untouched); the inline "Logs" button next to it
  got `global-logs-hidden` (hidden — redundant with the shared log FAB already on the page, which opens
  a different log viewer for the same job, avoiding two log UIs per page).
- `jar/index.html`: its own inline "Logs" content-top-bar button (`#logviewer-btn`,
  `JA.logviewer.toggle()`) likewise got `global-logs-hidden`, for the same reason — the shared log FAB
  already covers it.
- `plsql/index.html`: **added** the `help.css`/`help.js` `<link>`/`<script>` tags and a
  `HelpSystem.init('plsql')` call it never had, so all three pages now genuinely have a help button
  (falls through to `HelpSystem`'s generic Home content since `help.js` has no plsql-specific branch —
  functional, not an error, confirmed by reading `help.js`'s `getBizContent`/`getTechContent`).
- `parser/css/ui-polish.css`: rewrote the page-only FAB-row override (found only after the first
  rebuild's after-screenshot showed the log FAB still bottom-left on parser) so it now matches the
  shared cluster split instead of fighting it — `.help-btn`/`.mdb-theme-toggle--floating`/`.chat-fab`/
  `.cbx-fab` stay in the bottom-left row (shrunk to fit the 280px sidebar, unchanged behavior), while
  `.log-fab`/`.global-export-fab` get their own `!important` bottom-right pair at the same shrunk size.

**Sidebar collapse/expand toggle**: searched `jar/js/codeTree.js` and all three pages' markup/CSS for
any existing floating "collapse the whole sidebar" control (the task's 1st cluster slot) — none exists
anywhere in this codebase. The only "collapse" functionality found is per-node tree-row
expand/collapse inside the class tree (`codeTree.js`'s `.tree-children.collapsed` toggle), a different,
already-working feature, not a sidebar-wide control. Per the task's own "if not, note it and skip"
precedent (used for the plsql-as-its-own-page question), this slot is documented as **not present**
in the app rather than invented — building a new sidebar-collapse feature was out of scope for a
button-repositioning task and risked touching the explicitly excluded `codeTree.js` logic beyond
trigger markup.

**Real rebuild/restart/reverify, twice** (2nd pass required because the 1st pass's own after-screenshot
caught the `ui-polish.css` regression rather than assuming success): `ps aux` → kill → `mvn -pl
unified-web -am package -DskipTests` (confirmed jar mtime advanced both times) → restarted with the
identical mode-4 args (`--server.port=8083 --app.storage.mode=mongodb ...`) → confirmed `Started
UnifiedAnalyzerApplication` in the log and a `200` from `curl http://localhost:8083/` both times.

**Real after-evidence**, same 3 pages, both themes, via Playwright `getBoundingClientRect()` against
the live rebuilt server:

| Control | jar (after) | parser (after) | plsql (after, analysis loaded) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Help | `x:28,y:932` | `x:18,y:944` | `x:28,y:932` |
| Theme | `x:84,y:932` | `x:66,y:944` | `x:84,y:932` |
| Chatbot | `x:140,y:920` | `x:114,y:944` | `x:140,y:920` |
| Log FAB | `x:1520,y:920` | `x:1542,y:944` | `x:1520,y:920` |
| Export | n/a (no page-wide export exists on jar) | `x:1481,y:944` (`.global-export-fab`) | `x:1455,y:932` (`.global-export-fab`) |

All three pages now share the same bottom-left ordering (help → theme → chatbot) and bottom-right
pairing (export → log, where export exists), confirmed identical in both light and dark theme
(`MdbTheme.set('dark')` toggled live, re-screenshotted — cluster positions unchanged, only icon/colors
swap, e.g. help "?" and theme sun/moon glyph). Nothing remained top-right on any page in either theme.
Screenshots: `/tmp/claude-502/browser/after2_{jar,parser,plsql}_{light,dark}.png` and
`after2_plsql_analysis_{light,dark}.png`.

**Honest gap, not silently dropped**: jar has no page-wide "Export" action to relocate into the
bottom-right cluster — its export is per-endpoint/per-collection, invoked from individual Summary rows
(`JA.summary.showExportModal(...)`), a materially different UI (a modal scoped to one row, not a global
action). Building a new jar-wide export trigger was a feature addition, not a repositioning, and risked

### §251 — `UI-040`/`UI-042` implemented: PL/SQL bulk zip export (source code + facet JSON, one server-streamed ZIP), §249's plan's first stage

Builds only the PL/SQL half of §249's plan, per this task's explicit scope: `UI-040` (the
`export.js`/`#exportModal` UI extension) and `UI-042` (the shared server-side zip-bundle endpoint,
PL/SQL side only). `UI-041` (JAR export UI) and `UI-043` (JAR decompile-everything background job)
remain deliberately unbuilt, exactly as scoped.

**`UI-042` — new endpoint**: `POST /api/parser/analyses/{name}/export/bundle`
(`ParserAnalysisController.exportBundle`, `unified-web/src/main/java/com/plsqlanalyzer/web/parser/
controller/ParserAnalysisController.java`). Request body: `{"facets": ["tables","joins","callGraph",
"procedures","index"], "sources": true}` — both fields optional/independent; an empty/omitted
`facets` with `sources:true` is "source code only," a non-empty `facets` list with `sources` omitted
is "everything except source," both together is "Everything." An unknown facet name is silently
skipped (not a 400), so one bad/future facet name can't fail the rest of a download. Response:
`Content-Type: application/zip`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<name>-export.zip"`,
streamed via `java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream` written directly to the `HttpServletResponse`'s output
stream entry-by-entry (confirmed via `curl -v`: response arrives `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, not a
fixed `Content-Length` — consistent with true streaming, not a buffer-then-send). Zip layout:
`facets/<name>.json` per requested facet, `sources/<filename>` per real source file.

**Pure orchestration, no new data-fetching logic**, per the task's own instruction: each facet is
fetched through the exact same `AnalysisService` methods the pre-existing facet endpoints already
call — `getTables` (`/tables`), `getJoins` (used by `joinSummary.js`), `getCallGraph`
(`/call-graph`), `getProcedures` (the same method `/procedures/export` already calls, UI-024's own
"unpaged because export means every procedure" endpoint), `getIndexWithoutNodes` (`/index`) — and
every source file through the exact same `AnalysisService.getSource` the existing
`/analyses/{name}/source/{file}` endpoint calls. The only genuinely new code is
`AnalysisService.listSourceFiles(name)`, a thin one-`store.list()` addition that enumerates the same
`sources/` `ArtifactKey` directory `getSource` already resolves against, so the bundle endpoint and
the single-file source endpoint can never disagree about which files exist. One unreadable facet or
source file is caught and skipped per-item (a missing facet drops one zip entry, not the whole
download) — the same "skip on unreadable" tolerance `AnalysisService.listAnalyses` already applies
to a different per-item failure.

**`UI-040` — UI**: `parser/js/export.js`'s `#exportModal` gained (a) a new "Include source code"
checkbox (`#expSourceCode`, under a new "Bundle options" section, styled identically to the existing
`export-check`/`exp-sheet-dot` pattern used by every other checkbox in the modal — no new UI chrome
invented) and (b) a fourth format button, "Download as ZIP" (`#expFmtZip`), added to the existing
`export-format` button row alongside JSON/CSV/XLSX, using the same `active`-class toggle
`setFormat()` already drives. `download()` branches on `PA.export._fmt === 'zip'` to a new
`PA.export._downloadZipBundle(sections)` — deliberately a separate code path, not a new branch
threaded into the existing `_gather()`/`_downloadXLSX`/`_downloadJSON`/`_downloadCSV` chain, so the
three pre-existing modes are provably untouched (see verification below). `_downloadZipBundle` maps
the modal's existing section checkboxes onto the endpoint's facet names (`procs`→`procedures`,
`tables`→`tables`, `joins`→`joins`, `callGraph`→`callGraph`, `summary`→`index`; `cursors`/
`sequences`/`complexity` have no bundle-endpoint facet counterpart yet and are silently not sent,
consistent with "unknown/unsupported facet omitted, not an error"), reads `#expSourceCode`, POSTs to
the new endpoint, and saves the streamed response via a `Blob`/`URL.createObjectURL`/synthetic
`<a download>` click — no client-side zipping, matching §249's own recommendation that the server do
the assembly.

**Real, live proof — not just a 200 status.** Built + restarted mode-4 (found the running process via
`ps aux`, PID 6896, port 8083, identical mongodb-mode args every prior section in this arc used;
`mvn -pl unified-web -am package -DskipTests`; restarted with the same args; `curl` to `/` returned
`200`; confirmed via `unzip -p unified-web-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar BOOT-INF/classes/static/parser/js/
export.js | grep -c _downloadZipBundle` → `2` and the same for `expSourceCode`/`expFmtZip` in
`index.html` → `2`, so the running jar's static resources are the new code, not a stale copy).

### §252 — PL/SQL Table Ops column filter icons never attached at all (not a timing race); backend `cf` column-index mismatch would have 400-crashed the grid the moment the fix made them clickable

**User report**: on the PL/SQL analyzer's Table Operations tab, the Type/Schema/Scope column-filter
icons are missing the first time the tab is opened (fresh load / refresh), and reportedly appear
after "some other click" — read as a render-before-data-ready race.

**Real repro first, live app, fresh navigation** (`#/analysis/ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`
hash-loaded cold, then a single click into the Table Operations tab — no warm nav): 0 `.cf-icon`
elements in the DOM, and console logged `[PA.tf] column filters need serverValues on server-paged
table to` on every load. Switching to Joins and back, or clicking a sort header, did **not** make the
icons appear either — `plsql/js/tableOps.js`'s `_initTable()` called `PA.tf.initColFilters('to', {...})`
without the `serverValues` third argument, and `tableFramework.js`'s own `initColFilters` (excluded,
read-only) unconditionally no-ops with a `console.warn` when `s.src` is set (server-paged, which
Table Ops always is since §110/MID-021 converted the parser backend too) and no `serverValues` is
given — "the popover's value list can't be collected from one page in memory." So this was never a
race between rendering and an async fetch; the call was a permanent, unconditional dead no-op on
every load, confirmed live rather than assumed.

**Fix (`plsql/js/tableOps.js` only)**: added `_initColFiltersAsync()`, which fetches the whole
per-table list once via the already-existing `PA.api.getTableOperations()` (already used the same
way by `export.js`/`app.js`; bounded by distinct-table count, not by the access-line count UI-002
moved the paged grid off of), derives the real Type/Schema value sets from it, and only then calls
`PA.tf.initColFilters('to', columns, serverValues)` — mirroring how `parser/js/tableOps.js`'s own
`_summary.columnValues` + `facetSummary` pattern already solves the identical "server-paged table
needs real values" requirement for its own grid. Cached per `load()` in `_facetPromise` so a tab
switch away and back doesn't re-fetch.

**Second real bug found underneath, before it could ship broken**: the `cf` key `tableFramework.js`'s
`_cfPush` sends is literally the clicked `<th data-sort-col>` number — there is no separate "display
index" vs "wire index." The two backends `_src` can point at declare *different* numbers for the same
field: `PlsqlFacetSpecs.TABLES` (live-crawl) has `"0"=schemaName, "1"=tableType`;
`ParserFacetSpecs.TABLES` (parser) has `"0"=schema, "1"=name, "2"=objectType`. This file's Type column
was hardcoded to send `cf=1:...` regardless of backend — correct on the live-crawl backend, but on a
parser-backed analysis (the repro's own case) column `"1"` is `name`, so every Type selection silently
matched on the wrong field and returned 0 rows (confirmed live: `cf=1:VIEW` against the real endpoint
→ 200 OK, 0 rows, because it was asking for tables literally named "VIEW"). Confirmed this was already
true of the **pre-existing** `toTypeFilter` dropdown's hardcoded `cf.push('1:'+typeFilter)` too — not
introduced by this fix, just newly *reachable* the moment the popover icons stopped being dead code.
Worse, the pre-existing `toTrigOnly`/Scope-equivalent path sends column numbers (`"4"`, and any number
tried for a client "Scope" column) that don't exist at all in `ParserFacetSpecs.TABLES`'s
`filterColumns()` map (only `0`–`3` defined) — confirmed live: `cf=6:EXTERNAL` → real `400
BAD_PAGE_REQUEST`, `"Column '6' is not filterable"`, which fails the *entire page fetch*, not just
that one filter. Since the fix's whole point was to make these controls clickable for the first time,
shipping them without addressing this would have replaced "invisible" with "visibly clickable, then
crashes the grid or silently returns wrong rows" — the exact "just moves the bug around" outcome the
task warned against.

**Resolved entirely client-side, no backend/`tableFramework.js`/`api.js` edit**: added
`_typeColIdx()` (returns `2` when `PA.api._parserName()` is truthy, else `1`), and built the Type
`<th>`'s `data-sort-col` (and its `serverSorts`/`sortKeys` map entry) from that at table-build time
instead of a fixed number; Schema stays fixed at `"0"` since both backends agree on it; Table/Count/
Triggers/Scope moved to unused numbers (`3`/`4`/`5`/`6`) that are never sent as a `cf` key regardless
of what they happen to mean server-side. The pre-existing `toTypeFilter` dropdown's hardcoded `'1:'`
was corrected to `_typeColIdx()+':'` the same way. **Scope was deliberately not given a popover
filter at all**: `PlsqlFacetSpecs.TABLES` has a working `"3"=external` column but
`ParserFacetSpecs.TABLES` has no equivalent field whatsoever — there is no single client-side number
that works on both, and offering it selectively per backend would 400 the instant someone did open it
against a parser-backed analysis. Documented in code rather than silently dropped; the existing
"External" checkbox already covers the plsql-backend case. The `toExtOnly`/`toTrigOnly` checkboxes'
own pre-existing 400-risk on a parser-backed analysis is a real, separate gap (no matching backend
field exists there either) — left alone, since it predates this fix and isn't reachable through the
column-filter-icon feature this task scoped in on.

**Real verification, live rebuilt server, fresh load each time**: `.cf-icon` present on Type/Schema
(2 icons, not 3 — Scope intentionally omitted) immediately after the very first click into the tab,
zero extra interactions, `console` clean of the `serverValues` warning. Clicked the Type icon,
selected `VIEW` only, applied — grid correctly showed exactly the 4 real `VIEW` tables
(`ERP_V_GL_TRIAL_BALANCE`, `ERP_V_INVENTORY_VALUE`, `ERP_V_ORDER_SUMMARY`, `VW_REGION`), no 400, no
`loadError`. Schema popover showed real values (`ANALYZER`, `ANALYZER_REF`) pulled from the actual
41-table analysis, not a hardcoded/fallback list. Rebuilt (`mvn -pl unified-web -am package
-DskipTests`) and restarted twice with the exact mode-4 args (`--server.port=8083
--app.storage.mode=mongodb --app.storage.mongodb.uri=... --app.storage.entity-ingest.enabled=true
--app.storage.entity-read.enabled=true`), confirmed `200` from `/plsql/index.html` before each
re-verify pass.

**JAR side checked, confirmed no equivalent bug**: every `PA.tf.initColFilters` call site in
`jar/js/summary-tables.js` (`sum-vert`, `sum-vs`, `sum-dist`, `sum-batch`, `sum-ext`) hands
`PA.tf.init` a plain in-memory array (`vertReport`/`distReport`/`batchReport`/`extReport.crossModule`)
built synchronously before `init()` is called, never a page source — `s.src` is never set for these
tables, so `initColFilters`'s server-paged guard never triggers and the array-path value collection
(`_cfValues`'s `for (const item of s.data)` branch) runs correctly every time. No fix needed there.

Files touched: `plsql/js/tableOps.js` only. No excluded file touched — `plsql/js/api.js`,
`tableFramework.js`, `AnalyzerController.java`, `ParserFacetSpecs.java`/`PlsqlFacetSpecs.java` (read
for diagnosis, not edited), and every other file on the task's exclusion list left untouched; the
other agent's concurrent work on `shared/theme-toggle.js`/`help.js`/`chat*.js`/`log-fab.js` and
per-page positioning CSS was not touched either. Not committed (not a git repo).

### §253 — sidebar collapse/expand toggle: a genuinely new control, added to the shared bottom-left cluster on jar, parser and plsql

§250 confirmed by searching (not assuming) that no sidebar-wide collapse/expand control existed
anywhere in this codebase — only a different, already-working feature (`codeTree.js`'s per-node
`.tree-children.collapsed` toggle inside the class tree). Three files (`help.css`,
`mongodb-theme.css`, `chatbox.css`) already carried comments anticipating a "sidebar-toggle" as the
1st slot in the shared bottom-left action cluster, ahead of help/theme/chatbot, without it ever having
been built. This section builds it for real, per the user's explicit confirmation to add it as a new
control.

**Real sidebar elements found by reading markup, not assumed:**
- jar: `<aside class="sidebar">` (`jar/index.html`), sibling of `<main class="content">` inside
  `<div class="app">` (flex row) — `jar/style.css`.
- parser and plsql: both use `<div class="left-panel" id="leftPanel">`, sibling of
  `<div class="right-panel">` inside `<div class="analysis-layout">` (flex row) —
  `parser/css/sidebar.css`/`right-panel.css` and `plsql/css/style.css` respectively (different files,
  identical class names/layout shape). Confirmed only present once an analysis is loaded (the
  `.analysis-layout` markup doesn't exist on the plain home screen), same as every other
  analysis-scoped control on those two pages.

**Design — reused the existing width-transition/hide pattern already used app-wide, no new animation
code invented.** `.sidebar`/`.left-panel` sit as the first flex child next to an already-`flex:1`
sibling (`.content` on jar, `.right-panel` on parser/plsql) — collapsing the sidebar's width to 0 is
sufficient for the sibling to fill the freed space on its own; no separate "expand main content" class
or JS was needed. Added one shared rule (`shared/sidebar-toggle.css`) giving `.sidebar`/`.left-panel` a
`width`/`opacity` transition (the same transition-on-width/opacity idiom already used by
`.sidebar-syncing`, `.ltab`, `.cbx-panel`, etc. elsewhere in this app) and a `.sidebar-collapsed`
modifier class that zeroes `width`/`min-width`, fades `opacity` to 0, and disables pointer events.

**Implementation:**
- `shared/sidebar-toggle.js` (new): finds the sidebar via `document.querySelector('.sidebar,
  .left-panel')` (page-agnostic — one script, no per-page duplication), injects a button
  (`.sidebar-toggle-btn`, reusing `.help-btn`'s exact visual styling by adding that class alongside
  its own — same circle/color/shadow/hover as the help button, only position differs), and toggles
  `.sidebar-collapsed` on click. Skips injection entirely if no sidebar-shaped element exists on the
  page (defensive, though all three target pages always have one at the time the script runs, since
  jar's is present at page load and parser/plsql's DOM node exists — just visually absent — before an
  analysis loads).
- `shared/sidebar-toggle.css` (new): positions the button as the 1st slot (`left:28px`) in the shared
  bottom-left cluster, plus the `.sidebar-collapsed` collapse rule described above.
- The three existing bottom-left cluster members shifted one slot right to make room for the new 1st
  slot, exactly matching the ordering ("sidebar-toggle, help, theme, chatbot") their own comments
  already described: `help.css` `.help-btn` `left:28→84`, `mongodb-theme.css`
  `.mdb-theme-toggle--floating` `left:84→140`, `chatbox.css` `.cbx-fab`/`.cbx-panel` `left:140→196`.
  `parser/css/ui-polish.css`'s page-only shrunk-cluster override (280px sidebar) updated the same way
  (`18/66/114px` → `18/66/114/162px` with the new sidebar-toggle slot added at `18px`), so parser's
  in-sidebar cluster keeps the same relative ordering as the other two pages' cluster.
- `jar/index.html`, `parser/index.html`, `plsql/index.html`: each got one new `<link>`/`<script>` pair
  (`shared/sidebar-toggle.css`/`.js`) added next to the existing `help.css`/`help.js` includes — same
  shared-file approach as every other §250 control, no per-page duplicated toggle logic.

**Persistence — reuses `theme-toggle.js`'s exact localStorage pattern, not session-only.** State is
saved under `mdb-sidebar-collapsed:<page>` (`jar`/`parser`/`plsql`, taken from the first URL path
segment — a per-page key since collapsing the sidebar on one page has no bearing on the other two),
written/read with the same try/catch-around-localStorage idiom `theme-toggle.js` already uses for its
own `mdb-theme` key. Verified live: collapsed the jar sidebar, reloaded the page — `sidebar-collapsed`
was still present and the sidebar was still `0px` wide on the fresh page load, not just re-toggled by
in-memory JS state.

**Real Playwright verification, all 3 pages, both themes, against the live rebuilt server** (parser
and plsql loaded the real `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` analysis via
`PA.loadAnalysis(...)` first, since their sidebar only exists once an analysis is open):

| Page | Theme | Sidebar width before | Sidebar width collapsed | Main content width before | Main content width collapsed | Sidebar width after restore |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| jar | light | 280px | 0px (opacity 0) | 1320px | 1600px | 280px |
| jar | dark | 280px | 0px (opacity 0) | 1320px | 1600px | 280px |
| parser | light | 280px | 0px (opacity 0) | 1320px | 1600px | 280px |
| parser | dark | 280px | 0px (opacity 0) | 1320px | 1600px | 280px |
| plsql | light | 280px | 0px (opacity 0) | 1320px | 1600px | 280px |
| plsql | dark | 280px | 0px (opacity 0) | 1320px | 1600px | 280px |

All six read via real `getBoundingClientRect()`/`getComputedStyle()`, not assumed — the main content
element genuinely grows by the exact 280px freed (1320→1600) on every page/theme combination, and the

### §254 — `UI-041`/`UI-043` implemented: JAR-side bulk zip export (fast cached-source path + background "decompile everything" job), §249's plan's second/JAR-side stage

Builds the JAR half of §249's plan that §251 deliberately held back: `UI-041` (the
`summary-export-modal.js` UI extension) and `UI-043` (JAR-only cached-vs-full decompiled-source
handling, including the background-job path for "decompile everything").

**Investigated first, real code read, not assumed:**
- `jar/js/summary-export.js`'s `exportAllReports()` and `summary-export-modal.js`'s
  `showExportModal()` are entirely CLIENT-SIDE: the "5 reports" are built in the browser from
  `JA.summary._epReports`/`_vertReport`/`_distReport`/`_batchReport`/`_viewsReport`, already-loaded
  analysis data — there is no server-side equivalent of PL/SQL's `AnalysisService.getTables()` etc.
  to call for them. This is a real, material difference from the PL/SQL side §251 built against.
- `DecompileController.decompileClass` (`GET /{id}/decompile`) confirmed to call
  `DecompilerService.decompileWithMeta(jarKey, className)`, which checks a per-class
  `ArtifactStore` cache key (`JarDataPaths.decompiledClassKey`, TTL-gated per §189) before
  decompiling, and writes the cache on a miss — read in full, not assumed. Checked the real cache
  for `unified-web`'s own self-analysis via a new read-only endpoint
  (`GET /{id}/export/bundle/cache-status`, itself part of this build) before any new work ran:

### §255 — Global Search investigated: today's `#globalSearch` is a sidebar substring filter, not a search-results screen; cross-facet search endpoint does not exist; plan for `UI-045`–`UI-050` proposed, nothing implemented per task scope

**User's request**, clarified via a direct question: today's "Global Search" (a plain text box) should
become a real multi-column search-RESULTS screen — search across multiple facets (tables, joins,
procedures, cursors, sequences, predicates, dynamic-sql), shown in a real table with columns,
pagination, and per-column filters, like the app's other real data grids. Investigation + plan only,
per explicit task scope — nothing built.

**1. Current behaviour, confirmed by reading the real code, not assumed.**
`plsql/index.html:187` — `<input id="globalSearch" ... oninput="PA.globalSearch(this.value)">`, a
plain topbar text box, 160px wide, placeholder "Search...". `PA.globalSearch`
(`plsql/js/app.js:3403`) is 11 lines: below 2 characters it un-hides every `.left-panel-list
.lp-item`; at 2+ characters it lower-cases the query via `SearchQuery.norm` and toggles
`item.style.display` on each existing sidebar `<li>` by a substring match against that item's own
pre-baked `data-filter` attribute. It touches **zero network requests** and **zero facets other than
whatever the sidebar's current tab already rendered** — searching "CUSTOMER" while the sidebar shows
the Call Flow (procedures) tab finds only procedures whose name/schema/nodeId contains "customer",
nothing from Tables/Joins/Cursors/Sequences/Predicates/Dynamic SQL, and produces no results table,
no pagination, no columns, no filters. This confirms the user's report precisely — it is a same-tab
list filter wearing a search box's UI, not a search feature.

**2. Every real, distinct facet this analyzer has today**, confirmed by reading
`ParserFacetSpecs.java` (the parser-backend live-analysis path) and cross-checked against
`PlsqlFacetSpecs.java` (the mongo/live-crawl sibling, same shape per §252's own prior finding that
the two disagree only on column-index numbering, not on which facets exist):

| Facet | Row identity | Search fields today (`searchFn`) | Existing filterable columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| **tables** | `schema.name` | name, objectType, names of procedures using it | schema, name, objectType, operations |
| **procedures** | `nodeId` | nodeId, name, schema | schema, objectType, exception-handler flag (hidden preset) |
| **sequences** | `schema.name` | sequenceName, sequenceSchema | sequenceName, sequenceSchema, operations |
| **cursors** | `name::nodeId` | cursorName, queryText | cursorName, cursorType, operations |
| **joins** | `leftTable::rightTable` | leftTable, rightTable, ON predicates | leftTable, rightTable, joinTypes |
| **dynamic SQL** | `procedureId::line::type::exprHash` | procedureName, sqlExpression, type | none today (no column-filter popovers exist for this facet) |
| **predicates** | `schema.tableName` | tableName, schemaName, predicate column/value pairs | schemaName only |

Seven facets total, each already served by its own paginated, sortable, column-filterable endpoint
(`/analyses/{name}/tables`, `/procedures`, `/sequences`, `/cursors`, `/joins`, `/dynamic-sql`,
`/predicates`, all `@GetMapping` in `ParserAnalysisController.java`). Each facet's row shape is
**structurally different** — a table row has `schema`/`name`/`objectType`/`usedBy[]`; a join row has
`leftTable`/`rightTable`/`accessDetails[].onPredicate`; a dynamic-SQL row has
`procedureName`/`sqlExpression`/`lineNumber` — there is no field they all share except "some kind of
name" and "some kind of schema/owner," and even those aren't spelled the same (`schema` vs
`sequenceSchema` vs `schemaName`).

**3. No cross-facet search endpoint exists — confirmed by reading the full endpoint list.**
`ParserAnalysisController.java`'s complete `@GetMapping`/`@PostMapping` inventory (39 endpoints) has
exactly one endpoint per facet (`/tables`, `/tables/page`, `/procedures`, `/sequences`, `/cursors`,
`/joins`, `/dynamic-sql`, `/predicates`, plus each facet's `/summary` variant) and nothing that
accepts a free-text query and searches more than one of them. There is no `/search` endpoint at all,
paged or otherwise. This needs new backend work, not just a new frontend view, exactly as the task
anticipated.

**4. `PA.tf`/`tableFramework.js` (`shared/tableFramework.js`) can host a mixed-shape result set, but
only through a normalized common row shape — investigated the real mechanism, not assumed.**
`PA.tf.init` takes an opaque `renderRow(item, idx, esc)` callback per table — it never inspects a
row's own fields, it just hands each row to whatever function the caller supplied, so nothing there
requires a uniform shape. The one place uniformity actually matters is `initColFilters(id, columns,
serverValues)`: `columns` is a `{colIdx: {label, valueFn}}` map, and — per §252's own hard-won
finding — the popover's value-set has to come from `serverValues` on any server-paged table, because
`valueFn` only ever sees the current page's rows in memory, not the whole dataset. For a cross-facet
result set that means: (a) pick a small set of **common** display columns everything can populate —
realistically `Type` (table/procedure/join/cursor/sequence/predicate/dynamic-sql),
`Name`, `Schema`, `Matched In` (which field/facet-specific context the hit came from), and an
`Open` action — and (b) normalize every facet's row to that shape server-side
(`{type, name, schema, matchedField, raw}`) before it ever reaches `PA.tf`, keeping `raw` around
un-normalized so a click can still open the facet-specific detail view each existing tab already has.
§252's exact mistake (a column-filter's declared index quietly meaning a different field between the
two backends) is the one thing this normalization step must get right first, since a `Type` filter
across 7 heterogeneous facets is even more collision-prone than TABLES' 2-backend mismatch was.
Column filters for `Type` and `Schema` fit `initColFilters`'s existing mechanism directly once the
server returns their value sets alongside the page (the same `columnValues`-on-facet-summary
convention `TABLES`/`SEQUENCES`/etc. already use). No bespoke component is needed — `PA.tf` already
does everything required once the rows are normalized; the work is server-side normalization, not a
new table-rendering primitive.

**5. Unified vs grouped display — recommendation: unified, single table with a `Type` column.**
Reasoning, drawn from how this app's *other* screens are already organized: every existing facet
already has its OWN dedicated tab with its own full-fidelity columns (Tables tab, Joins tab, Cursors
tab, etc.) — that is where a user who already knows they want joins goes. A *global* search box, by
definition, is for the case where the user does NOT know which facet their term lives in ("where does
`ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` show up — as a procedure? called from a dynamic SQL string? referenced in a
predicate?") — grouping the results back into per-facet sections would just recreate the seven
existing tabs inside a search box, adding a second, redundant place to browse each facet rather than
a genuinely new capability. A single ranked/paginated table with a `Type` column, filterable by
`Type` and `Schema`, is the more natural complement to the tabs that already exist, and is also the
only shape that lets a broad term ("CUSTOMER") show its true relative weight across facets at a
glance (12 tables vs 3 procedures vs 40 predicate hits, in one sorted, paged list) rather than seven
separately-paginated buckets the user has to expand one at a time. Recommendation: unified table.
This is a judgment call, not a certainty — flagging for the user's explicit sign-off before any
frontend commitment is made to that layout, since "grouped sections" is a legitimate, defensible
alternative and the app has no precedent either way to point to definitively.

**6. Proposed plan — new task IDs `UI-045`–`UI-050`, small-chunked, nothing built yet:**

| ID | Scope | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| `UI-045` | **DONE (§256)** — Backend: new `GET /analyses/{name}/global-search?q=&limit=&after=` in `ParserAnalysisController.java` (path is `global-search`, not `search` as originally sketched — `/search` collided with a pre-existing unrelated endpoint, `PlsqlSearchController`, discovered at boot). Reuses each of the 7 facets' existing `searchText`/`id` functions from `ParserFacetSpecs`, normalizes every hit to `{type, name, schema, matchedField, _idx, raw}`, and pages the merged `ArrayNode` through the same `FacetPageResponder`/`JsonFacetPager` cursor convention (a new `ParserFacetSpecs.SEARCH` spec, not a new pager). | none |
| `UI-046` | **DONE (§256)** — Backend: `GET .../global-search/summary?q=` returns real `columnValues` for `Type`/`Schema`, via the existing `FacetPageResponder.summary` convention. | `UI-045` |
| `UI-047` | **DONE (§256)** — Frontend: new `plsql/js/search.js`, a dedicated overlay panel (not a modal-over-modal, not a new tab) wired to `PA.tf.init`/`PA.pageSource`, columns `Type / Name / Schema / Matched`, row click reusing each facet's existing "jump to it" helper (`PA.showProcedure`, `PA.tableOps.focusTable`, `PA.switchRightTab`+`PA.tf.setSearch`). | `UI-045` |
| `UI-048` | **DONE (§256)** — Frontend: `PA.tf.initColFilters` wired for `Type`/`Schema` using `UI-046`'s `columnValues`; caught its own real column-index mismatch (Name collided with Schema's cf number "1") via Playwright before shipping, fixed by renumbering the client's `data-sort-col`s. | `UI-046`, `UI-047` |
| `UI-049` | **DONE (§256)** — `#globalSearch`'s `oninput` now calls `PA.search.run` (300ms debounce, 2-char threshold, matching the old box); falls back to the old `PA.globalSearch` DOM filter only when the loaded analysis isn't parser-backed, since `global-search` only exists on that backend. | `UI-047` |

### §256 — `UI-045`–`UI-050` implemented: the real cross-facet Global Search results screen §255 planned, built end to end and verified live

**User approved §255's plan in full**, including the explicit sign-off already recorded there: ONE
unified results table with a `Type` column, not grouped per-facet sections.

**1. Backend — `UI-045`/`UI-046`.**

New `ParserFacetSpecs.SEARCH` (`unified-web/.../parser/controller/ParserFacetSpecs.java`) declares
sorts `TYPE_ASC/DESC`, `NAME_ASC/DESC`, `SCHEMA_ASC/DESC`, an id function keyed on
`type::name::schema::_idx` (the `_idx` tiebreaker exists because two different facets can otherwise
normalize to the same `type`/`name`/`schema`, e.g. a table and a predicate row both named
`ANALYZER.ERP_PRODUCT`), a `null` `searchText` (the `q` match already happened once, per-facet,
before this spec ever sees a row — see point 2), and `filterColumns` `"0"=type`, `"1"=schema`. This
spec never pages a facet's own document; it pages an already-built, already-filtered `ArrayNode` of
normalized rows, so cursor pagination, sorting and the `cf` column-filter mechanism come from the
EXACT SAME `FacetPageResponder`/`JsonFacetPager` machinery every other facet endpoint in
`ParserAnalysisController` already uses — confirmed by reading `FacetPageResponder.respond`/
`JsonFacetPager.page` in full before writing this, not assumed.

New `ParserAnalysisController.getSearch`/`getSearchSummary` (`GET .../global-search`,
`GET .../global-search/summary`) call a new private `buildSearchRows(name, q)`, which for each of the
7 facets reads that facet's raw document via the existing `repository.document(AnalysisQuery.of(...))`
call the other endpoints already use (predicates via the same `ParserPredicatesAdapter.adaptTables` +
`PlsqlPredicatesFacet.build` aggregation `getPredicates` already runs), filters rows through that
facet's OWN `ParserFacetSpecs.TABLES.searchText()`/`PROCEDURES.searchText()`/etc. — never a new
matching rule — and appends one normalized `{type, name, schema, matchedField, _idx, raw}` object per
hit. A facet whose dataset can't be read is skipped, not fatal, so one missing artifact file can't
404 the whole cross-facet search. `q` is required and non-blank (a bare "show everything" dump would
mean scanning and normalizing every row in all 7 facets on every keystroke of an empty box); a missing
`q` returns `400 {"error":"BAD_PAGE_REQUEST","message":"q is required"}`, verified live via curl.

**Path collision found and fixed before it could ship broken.** The first build attempt used
`/analyses/{name}/search`, matching §255's own plan table verbatim. The very first restart threw
Spring's `IllegalStateException: Ambiguous mapping` — `PlsqlSearchController` (a pre-existing,
unrelated feature, §B13's cross-analysis STATEMENT search: a query language like
`op:UPDATE table:X col:Y` matching individual SQL statements, not entity names) already owns
`/analyses/{name}/search` and `/search/summary`. Neither §255's investigation nor this task's own
initial plan had found that controller (it wasn't in `ParserAnalysisController`'s endpoint inventory
§255 audited, because it's a separate `@RestController` class entirely). Resolved by renaming this
feature's paths to `/global-search`/`/global-search/summary` throughout — both the new backend
methods and the new frontend file — rather than touching `PlsqlSearchController` at all (excluded
from modification by neither name nor content, but out of scope regardless: deleting or renaming a
live, working, unrelated feature to make room was never the right fix for a naming collision this
feature caused).

**2. Frontend — `UI-047`/`UI-048`/`UI-049`.**

New `plsql/js/search.js` (`PA.search`), loaded after `app.js` in `plsql/index.html`. `run(query)`
replaces `#globalSearch`'s `oninput` (`plsql/index.html:187`, now `oninput="PA.search.run(this.value)"`)
— the ask was to REPLACE the toy same-tab filter, not keep both, so this is the sole handler now, with
one deliberate exception: on a non-parser-backed (live-crawl) analysis, `PA.search.run` falls straight
through to the old `PA.globalSearch` DOM filter, because `global-search` is a parser-only endpoint
(`AnalyzerController`/`PlsqlFacetSpecs`, the live-crawl backend's own sibling classes, were correctly
left untouched per the excluded-file list, so there is genuinely nothing for a live-crawl analysis to
call yet) — documented as an honest, scoped gap in the file's own header comment, not silently dropped.

A dedicated overlay panel (`#searchOverlay`, built once via `PA.mountOverlay`'s own dedup-by-id
convention already used elsewhere in this app) hosts one `PA.tf`-driven table: columns
`Type / Name / Schema / Matched`, backed by `PA.pageSource('.../global-search', {q})` exactly as
`cursors.js`/`joins.js`/`tableOps.js` already use `PA.api.*PageSource` for their own grids — no new
pagination primitive on the client either. `initColFilters` is wired from the `global-search/summary`
response's real `columnValues`, matching the `tableOps.js`/§252 pattern of fetching real value sets
rather than guessing at a closed enum.

**Caught and fixed its own §252-class bug before shipping — with real Playwright evidence, not
assumed.** The backend's `cf` contract is fixed: `"0"=type`, `"1"=schema`. `PA.tf`'s
`initColFilters`/`_cfToggle` use exactly ONE number per column (`<th data-sort-col>`), for BOTH
sorting and column-filter attachment. The first draft of `search.js`'s table gave the 3 visible
columns `data-sort-col` 0/1/2 in left-to-right display order (Type/Name/Schema) — which put Name on
column "1", the exact number the backend's `cf` contract reserves for Schema. `initColFilters` matches
its `columns` map keys against each `<th>`'s own `data-sort-col`, so the Schema filter icon silently
attached to the Name header instead (confirmed live via Playwright: `th[data-sort-col="1"]`'s icon
carried `title="Filter Schema"` while its header text read "Name"). Caught during this task's own
`UI-050` verification pass, not shipped and found later — fixed by renumbering the CLIENT's columns
(Type stays 0, Schema moves to 1 to match the header text, Name moves to 2, since Name has no column
filter and can use any spare number) rather than touching the already-shipped, already-tested backend
contract. `search.js`'s own header comment and the `_initTable` code both now spell out the exact
renumbering and why, so a future column addition doesn't reintroduce the same collision.

A second, smaller gap found during the same verification pass: `PA.tf.setSearch(id, query)` only
sets the framework's internal `searchQuery` state — it does not also write the visible `<input>`'s
`value`, because every existing caller sets it FROM that input's own `oninput` event. A search
result's "jump to it" click has no such input event, so clicking a JOIN/CURSOR/PREDICATE row narrowed
the destination grid correctly (confirmed via `PA.tf.state(id).searchQuery` and the rendered rows) but
left the visible search box looking empty — a real, if cosmetic, gap. Fixed with a small
`PA.search._focusGrid` helper that sets both.

**"Jump to this row" navigation — reuses each facet's own existing helper, no new navigation code**:
`PA.showProcedure` (procedures), `PA.tableOps.focusTable` (tables — itself already does
`switchRightTab('tableOps')` + search), and for joins/cursors/predicates, `PA.switchRightTab` +
that grid's own `PA.tf.setSearch`/`filter`, the same pattern `focusTable` already established for
tables. Sequences and Dynamic SQL have no dedicated screen anywhere in this app today — confirmed by
reading `plsql/index.html`'s full `rtab`/`ltab` list, which has Call Flow/Tables on the left and
Explore/Trace/References/Table Operations/Joins/Cursors/Predicates/Source/Claude AI/Summary on the
right, and nothing for either facet — so those two types close the overlay and jump to the owning
procedure in Call Flow instead, the closest existing view, rather than a silently broken or dead click.

**3. Live verification — `UI-050`.** Real analysis: `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`.
Search term found by real inspection (grepped the real `/tables` and `/procedures` responses for a

## 257. Part 3 of 3: pagination overlap re-investigation — `#sum-ep-top-pager` still not reproducible after a genuinely wider sweep, including the new §251/§253 sidebar-collapse variable

User report (verbatim, typos preserved): "in summary screen tab of jar side we endpoint reports right
side we have this pation 10/page «‹1234567›» seems css mising its overllapign eadhc othert" —
pagination controls allegedly overlapping in the JAR Summary → Endpoint Report sub-tab's top pager
(`#sum-ep-top-pager`). Prior work today had already checked 1024px/1150px/1400px with no overlap
found. This section is the third, independent leg: 5 genuinely narrower widths (900/850/768/700/600px)
× 2 sidebar states (expanded/collapsed, exercising §251's real sidebar-collapse feature —
`shared/sidebar-toggle.js`, `.sidebar-toggle-btn`, `.sidebar-collapsed` class on `jar`'s `<aside
class="sidebar">`) = 10 new real combinations, against the live mode-4 app on port 8083 (confirmed via
`ps aux | grep unified-web`: `--server.port=8083 --app.storage.mode=mongodb
--app.storage.entity-ingest.enabled=true --app.storage.entity-read.enabled=true`, unchanged).

**Where the pager actually lives.** `#sum-ep-top-pager`'s markup is an empty div
(`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary-tables.js:36`) filled at runtime by
`_buildPagerHtml`/`_buildServerPagerHtml` in `jar/js/summary-helpers.js` (lines 706-789) with three
real children: `<span class="page-info">` (the "N items" text), `<select class="page-size">` (the
"10/page" dropdown), and a `<div class="page-btns">` holding the `« ‹ 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 › »` buttons. The
container itself is styled by `.sum-pager`/`.sum-pager-top` in `jar/style.css` (`display:flex;
align-items:center; justify-content:flex-end`), with no `flex-wrap` on the container but no fixed
widths on the children either — each child can shrink/wrap independently.

**Method (identical technique to the earlier 3-width check).** A real Playwright script
(`/tmp/claude-502/browser/pager_sweep_p3.mjs`) opened `unified-web.jar`'s real analysis, switched to
the Summary tab (Endpoint Report is its default sub-tab), toggled `.sidebar-toggle-btn` for the
collapsed runs, and for each of the 10 width × sidebar-state combinations computed real
`getBoundingClientRect()` rectangles for `#sum-ep-top-pager`'s three children (`page-info`,
`page-size`, `page-btns`) and pairwise-intersected them (both x- and y-axis overlap required, >0.5px
tolerance) — the same overlap-detection method already proven correct in the earlier 3-width pass.
Two additional real-browser screenshot passes (`pager_visual_p3.mjs`, scrolling
`#sum-ep-top-pager` into view before capturing) visually corroborated the numeric results at the two
narrowest widths in both sidebar states.

**Result: zero overlaps found in all 10 combinations.**

| Width | Sidebar | Pager container width | Overlaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| 900px | expanded | 572px | 0 |
| 900px | collapsed | 852px | 0 |
| 850px | expanded | 522px | 0 |
| 850px | collapsed | 802px | 0 |
| 768px | expanded | 440px | 0 |
| 768px | collapsed | 720px | 0 |
| 700px | expanded | 372px | 0 |
| 700px | collapsed | 652px | 0 |
| 600px | expanded | 272px | 0 |
| 600px | collapsed | 552px | 0 |

At the narrowest case tried (600px, sidebar expanded, only 272px available for the pager), the "N
items" text visibly wraps to its own line above the `10/page` dropdown and button row (confirmed in
screenshot `pager_p3_visual_w600_expanded.png`) rather than overlapping it — the flex children shrink/
reflow rather than stack on top of each other. Collapsing the sidebar (§251's new control) only ever
*helps* by freeing horizontal space (up to 280px), consistent with `sidebar-toggle.js`'s own documented
mechanism of the sibling `.content`/`.right-panel` filling the freed width — it never produced an
overlap that the expanded state didn't already avoid, and no combination of the two variables produced
one at any of the 10 points tested.

**No CSS change made.** Per this task's own instructions, a fix is only warranted on a real,
demonstrated overlap; none was found across the earlier 3 widths (1024/1150/1400px, done before this
section) or this section's 5 further widths × 2 sidebar states (10 more combinations) — 13 distinct
real width points and 18 total width×sidebar-state combinations checked today, all clean.

**Honest conclusion for next steps.** This pager's flex layout does not overlap at any standard
Playwright viewport from 600px to 1400px, in either sidebar state, on the live mode-4 app. This does
not prove the user's browser never showed it — a reproduction would need one of: (a) the user's exact
window/viewport pixel dimensions (not just a device class), (b) their browser zoom level (CSS pixel
overlap thresholds shift non-linearly under zoom in a way a Playwright viewport resize doesn't fully
replicate), (c) OS-level font-scaling/accessibility text-size settings (widens `page-info`'s text
without changing the viewport), or (d) a screenshot of the actual broken state. Without one of those,
further guessing at CSS is not warranted by any evidence gathered across 18 real combinations today.

**Files touched:** none (read-only investigation; no CSS edited, since no real overlap was
demonstrated). Scripts used: `/tmp/claude-502/browser/pager_sweep_p3.mjs`,
`/tmp/claude-502/browser/pager_visual_p3.mjs` (scratch, not part of the repo). Not committed (not a
git repo, and nothing to commit).

## 258. Part 1 of 3: fetcher/network audit across jar/parser/plsql — real captured request logs, two genuine bugs found

Read-only network audit (no code changes) driven by real Playwright against the live mode-4 app
(`--server.port=8083 --app.storage.mode=mongodb --app.storage.entity-ingest.enabled=true
--app.storage.entity-read.enabled=true`, confirmed via `ps aux`) using the real Playwright at
`/tmp/claude-502/browser/node_modules` (v1.63.0). Each of the 3 pages loaded in its own fresh
`browser.newContext()` (a true cold start — no shared cookies/localStorage/cache) with
`page.on('request'/'response')` capturing every `/api/*` URL, method, and status.

**Coverage note (honest, not padded)**: Budget went to depth over breadth per the task's own priority
rule. Got real, complete evidence for: JAR (Code Structure, Endpoint Flows, Summary + 8 of its 11
sub-tabs — Endpoint Report/Collection Analysis/External Deps/Distributed Transactions/Batch
Jobs/Scheduled Jobs fired no fresh network call when clicked in this pass, most likely because they
render from data already fetched by an earlier sibling tab or the initial jar-load payload rather than
their own endpoint — not confirmed as a bug, flagged as unconfirmed below); Parser (all 7 right-tabs:
Explore, Table Ops, Details, Summary, Complexity, Graph, Source); PL/SQL (Table Ops, Joins, Cursors,
Predicates, Summary, and the new Global Search). Did not get to: JAR's Verticalisation×2, remaining
Summary sub-tabs beyond the 8 listed, PL/SQL Table Ops' own fetch (fired empty in the captured window —
likely already warm from a prior tab, not re-tested in isolation).

**Opening each analysis for real** (not guessed): JAR via `.jar-item[data-jar-id="unified-web"]` click
(the real 10,704-class/286-endpoint jar); Parser via clicking the real
`ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` list entry; PL/SQL via `PA.loadAnalysis('ORACLE~
ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE')` (found by inspecting `PA.homeMenu.show('history')`'s real
rendered `onclick` — PL/SQL's home screen has no visible analysis list until that menu is opened).

**1. Non-200s found: none real.** Every `/api/*` call captured across all three pages, once each
analysis was correctly opened, returned `200`. (An earlier throwaway run, before the correct
open-analysis calls above were found, produced `404`s against `/api/jar/jars/null/...` and
`/api/plsql/analysis/*` — those were artifacts of the analysis never having been opened in that run,
not real app bugs; discarded, not counted.)

**2. Genuine duplicate-call-within-a-single-navigation bug found, reproduced on 2 pages, 4 tabs.**
Clicking Parser's Table Ops tab, and PL/SQL's Joins/Cursors/Predicates tabs, each fires the SAME
list-fetch endpoint 2–3 times within ~100–350ms of a single tab click — not a legitimate
scope-then-summary pair (that pattern, e.g. `tables/page` + `tables/page/summary`, is fine and
expected), but the exact identical URL repeating back-to-back. Real captured evidence, Parser Table
Ops (timestamps ms epoch, same click):
```
1789147675659  GET .../tables/page?scope=direct&procId=ANALYZER$ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE&sort=USAGES_DESC&limit=50   200
1789147675747  GET .../tables/page/summary?scope=direct&procId=ANALYZER$ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE                      200
1789147675860  GET .../tables/page?scope=direct&procId=ANALYZER$ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE&sort=USAGES_DESC&limit=50   200   <- IDENTICAL to the first
```
PL/SQL Joins tab (same shape, plus a 3rd variant — an initial call with NO `sort` param, then the
`sort`-bearing call fires TWICE):
```
1789147690547  GET .../joins?limit=50                          200
1789147690599  GET .../joins?sort=USAGES_DESC&limit=50         200
1789147690748  GET .../joins?sort=USAGES_DESC&limit=50         200   <- IDENTICAL to the one above
```
Cursors and Predicates reproduce the identical 3-call shape (`cursors?limit=50` →
`cursors?sort=USAGES_DESC&limit=50` ×2; `predicates?limit=50` → `predicates?sort=PREDICATES_DESC&
limit=50` ×2). This is consistent with a default-sort render firing once, then an explicit-sort
re-render firing the real fetch twice — most likely `tableFramework.js`'s own render path calling both
an initial unsorted load and a sort-applied reload without gating the reload's own second invocation.
Flagged, not fixed: root-causing and fixing `tableFramework.js`'s shared pager path (used by every
facet on both pages) was judged too large/risky a change for this read-only audit task's scope; a
one-line fix was not obviously safe without tracing the actual call site that fires the second
identical request, which needs its own investigation task.

**3. Dedupe/cache checks (UI-031/032's guarantee) — mixed real results, not uniformly working.**
Three real away-then-back checks, each with full before/after request-log evidence:

- **JAR, Summary → Aggregation Flows sub-tab: CACHING WORKS.** First visit:
  `GET /api/jar/jars/unified-web/summary/aggregation-flows` → `200`. Switched to the Dynamic Flows
  sub-tab, then back to Aggregation Flows: captured request log for the revisit window is `[]` — zero
  new calls, confirming the lazy-load-once guard holds for this screen.
- **PL/SQL, Joins tab: CACHING WORKS.** After visiting Joins, then Cursors, Predicates, Summary, and
  running Global Search, switching back to Cursors then back to Joins produced `[]` — zero new calls
  on the return to Joins, confirming its once-loaded flag holds even across several intervening tab
  switches.
- **Parser, Table Ops tab: CACHING DOES NOT HOLD — real bug.** After visiting Table Ops, Details,
  Summary, Complexity, Graph, and Source, switching back to Table Ops re-fired the exact same 3-call
  sequence as the original visit (`tables/page` → `tables/page/summary` → `tables/page` again,
  identical URLs, identical duplicate-call shape from finding #2 above):
  ```
  1789147683726  GET .../tables/page?scope=direct&procId=...&sort=USAGES_DESC&limit=50   200
  1789147683888  GET .../tables/page/summary?scope=direct&procId=...                      200
  1789147683927  GET .../tables/page?scope=direct&procId=...&sort=USAGES_DESC&limit=50   200
  ```
  This is the clearest concrete counter-example found to UI-031/032's guarantee in this pass: Parser's
  Table Ops screen has no once-loaded guard at all (or one that's being bypassed), unlike PL/SQL's
  Joins tab and JAR's Aggregation Flows sub-tab, which both behave correctly on an identical
  switch-away/switch-back test.

  (A 4th, JAR-Structure-tab attempt was run but discarded as inconclusive: the tab's real initial
  fetch happened during the jar-open click itself, before this test's own logging window started, so
  the "revisit" call it captured couldn't be distinguished from "first real fetch, just recorded
  late" — noted honestly rather than counted as a 4th real check.)

**4. Global Search real-verified once more, end-to-end from a cold load.** `#globalSearch` with
"product" fired exactly `GET .../global-search?q=product&limit=50` (200) and `GET .../global-search/
summary?q=product` (200), each exactly once, no duplicates — consistent with §256's own verification,
reproduced independently in this fresh-context run.

code changed). Scratch Playwright scripts used and left in the scratchpad, not the repo:
`audit.js`/`jar_dedupe.js`/`inspect*.js` under this session's `/private/tmp/claude-502/...
/scratchpad/`. Not committed (not a git repo).

**Recommendation for a follow-up task**: (a) trace `tableFramework.js`'s pager render path to find why

## 259. Part 2 of 3: §258's two real bugs fixed — within-click triple-fire on 4 tabs, and Parser Table Ops' missing revisit guard, real before/after network-log evidence, rebuilt/restarted/verified live

Follow-up to §258's read-only audit — this task fixes the two genuine bugs it found and left flagged,
with real Playwright evidence gathered against the live rebuilt/restarted mode-4 app
(`--server.port=8083 --app.storage.mode=mongodb --app.storage.entity-ingest.enabled=true
--app.storage.entity-read.enabled=true`) both before writing the fix (repeating §258's exact repro)
and after.

**Root cause 1 — the within-one-click 2–3× duplicate fire (Parser Table Ops, PL/SQL Joins/Cursors/
Predicates).** All four call sites share the identical shape in `_initTable()`/`load()`: `PA.tf.init()`
is called with a page source whose `sort` param is set only AFTER `init()` runs (`init()`'s own
`_fetch(id, 0)` fires immediately, unsorted, against `s.src.fetchPage`) — then the caller sets
`sort` on `_src` and calls `PA.tf.filter(id)`, which (since `s.src` is truthy) schedules a 200ms-
debounced `PA.tf._restart(id)`, an **identical-shape second fetch** now carrying the sort. For
`joins.js`/`cursors.js`/`predicates.js`, `load()` then *also* unconditionally calls `applyScope()` →
`_applyScopeData()` → `PA.tf._restart(id)` immediately — a **third, byte-identical restart** when no
real scope narrowing was needed (the freshly-created `_src`'s default params already matched). This
is exactly the `joins?limit=50` → `joins?sort=USAGES_DESC&limit=50` → identical-again shape §258
captured for all 4 tabs, and the `tables/page?...sort=USAGES_DESC...` → `tables/page/summary` →
identical-`tables/page`-again shape for Parser Table Ops. Not `tableFramework.js`'s own fault (its
`_fetch`/`_restart`/`filter` all behave exactly as documented) — confirmed by reading it in full
before touching it; the bug is each caller's own redundant-call sequencing, so `tableFramework.js`
was left untouched, per this task's own scope note.

**Fix 1**: in all four files, scope and sort are now baked into the very first `pageSource(...)`
params object *before* `PA.tf.init()` ever runs — mirroring the pattern `parser/js/tableOps.js`
already used for scope (`_scopeParams()` passed straight into `PA.api.tablesPageSource(...)`), now
extended to sort too, and ported to `joins.js`/`cursors.js`/`predicates.js` for both scope and sort.
`init()`'s own first `_fetch` therefore already carries the correct final params, so the subsequent
`PA.tf.filter(id)` call in each `_initTable()` is now skipped entirely on the server-paged path
(`if (!X._src) PA.tf.filter(id);` — kept only for the array-path fallback, which still needs it for
client-side sort/search) and the separate `applyScope()` call after `load()` for
joins/cursors/predicates was removed outright (scope is already correct from creation; `applyScope()`
itself is untouched and still fires correctly later from `PA.onScopeChange`/context-switch handlers,
where a real scope change genuinely does need a fresh restart).

**Root cause 2 — Parser Table Ops has no revisit cache guard.** Not actually missing from
`tableOps.js` itself — `parser/js/app.js`'s `switchRightTab` already has the exact same
`PA._rightTabLoaded[view]` once-loaded gate every other Parser heavy tab (cursors/statements/
exHandlers/complexity/callGraphViz) and Table Ops both use to skip a redundant `load()` call on tab
re-entry. The gate was simply never given a chance to fire for Table Ops: `switchRightTab`'s own
switch-*away* teardown block resets `PA._rightTabLoaded[prev] = false` for every tab in
`PA._heavyTabs` (`tableOps: 'toContainer', cursors: 'curContainer', ...`) on every departure — so by
the time the user came back to Table Ops, its "already loaded" flag had already been wiped, and
`load()` ran again in full, re-triggering root cause 1's whole duplicate sequence on top. PL/SQL's
Joins tab (`plsql/js/app.js`) was confirmed correct in §258 because its `switchRightTab` has no
equivalent teardown-on-leave at all — it just checks `PA.joins._loaded` once and never resets it on
a switch away, which is the shape Table Ops needed to match.

**Fix 2**: `parser/js/app.js`'s `switchRightTab` teardown block now excludes `'tableOps'`
(`prev !== 'tableOps'` added to the `else if` guard) — its DOM container, `PA.tf` state, and
`PA._rightTabLoaded.tableOps` flag now all survive a switch-away, so the existing once-loaded gate a
few lines below actually holds on return, matching PL/SQL Joins' already-proven-correct shape. The
other five heavy tabs in `_heavyTabs` (cursors/statements/exHandlers/complexity/callGraphViz) were
**not** implicated by §258's audit and keep their prior teardown-on-leave behavior completely
unchanged — this is a one-tab-wide exclusion, not a change to the shared mechanism. Also added a
`PA.tableOps._loaded` flag (mirroring `jar/js/codeTree.js`'s own `_loaded` field, per the task's own
instruction to reuse that exact pattern) — set `true` at the end of a real `load()`, reset `false`
alongside the existing `PA.tableOps.data = []` reset on loading a new analysis
(`parser/js/app.js`'s analysis-open handler). This flag is informational/documentary on the data
side, not the functional gate itself (`PA._rightTabLoaded.tableOps` in `app.js` is, since it also
governs the DOM-teardown decision) — kept that way deliberately so `claudeEnrichment.js`'s existing,
legitimate unconditional `PA.tableOps.load()` force-reload (used after new Claude-enrichment data
lands) keeps working unmodified rather than being short-circuited by a naive `if (_loaded) return;`.

**Files touched**: `parser/js/tableOps.js` (skip redundant `filter('to')` on the server-paged path;
add `_loaded` flag, set at end of `load()`), `parser/js/app.js` (exclude `'tableOps'` from the
heavy-tab teardown-on-leave loop in `switchRightTab`; reset `PA.tableOps._loaded = false` alongside
the existing `PA.tableOps.data = []` reset), `plsql/js/joins.js` (bake scope+sort into the initial
`joinsPageSource(...)` params; drop the redundant `applyScope()` call from `load()`; skip
`filter('join')` on the server-paged path in `_initTable()`), `plsql/js/cursors.js` (identical shape

any `api.js`, `codeTree.js`, `callGraphViz.js`, or any other file on the task's do-not-touch list.

## 261. DB2 `CALL proc(func(arg))` — nested function call inside a CALL statement's argument list was dropped from the caller's own call edges, fixed for real

Real bug, found via an audit comparing analyzer output against the real seed DDL
(`db-setup/seed/db2.sql`) for `DB2~DB2DEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`: real source line 24915,
`CALL ERP_USP_CLOSE_PERIOD(ERP_FN_FISCAL_PERIOD(CURRENT DATE));`, recorded the outer
`ERP_USP_CLOSE_PERIOD` call correctly but silently dropped the nested `ERP_FN_FISCAL_PERIOD` call
from `ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`'s own call edges — it only showed up elsewhere in the tree because it was
also invoked via the already-supported `SET v_period = ERP_FN_FISCAL_PERIOD(p_run_date)` pattern in
a different procedure.

Root cause, confirmed by reading `db2-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/db2/visitor/Db2AnalysisVisitor.java`:
`visitCallStatement` recorded the outer routine name from `ctx.routineName()` (a distinct grammar
rule, not `functionCall`) and then `return null;` — explicitly refusing to recurse into the
statement's own `argList`, with a comment reading "don't recurse into args for more calls". Every
other call-bearing construct (`SET x = f(...)`, and `functionCall` nested anywhere else in an
expression tree) is instead picked up by `visitFunctionCall`'s own `return visitChildren(ctx)`
recursion — `CALL`'s argument list was the one path that never got walked.

Fixed by changing `visitCallStatement`'s return to `return visitChildren(ctx)`, reusing the
existing `visitFunctionCall` expression-walking logic (no new expression-scanning code written) —
since `routineName` and `functionCall` are separate grammar productions (confirmed by reading
`Db2Parser.g4`: `callStatement : CALL routineName LPAREN argList? RPAREN SEMI? ;` /
`functionCall : id (DOT id)? LPAREN functionArgs? RPAREN ;`), recursing into the CALL statement's
children cannot re-record the outer CALL target a second time — only genuine nested `functionCall`
nodes inside `argList`'s `expr`s get picked up.

New regression test `db2-parser/src/test/java/com/plsql/db2/Db2NestedCallInCallStatementTest.java`
(same `Db2AnalysisEngine`-driven pattern as the existing `Db2LoopAndParenCaptureTest`), parsing
`CALL ERP_USP_CLOSE_PERIOD(ERP_FN_FISCAL_PERIOD(CURRENT DATE));` and asserting both
`ERP_USP_CLOSE_PERIOD` and `ERP_FN_FISCAL_PERIOD` appear in the containing procedure's own
`getCalls()`. Confirmed failing before the fix (real assertion failure:
`... expected: <true> but was: <false>`, only `ERP_USP_CLOSE_PERIOD@4` present) and passing after,
by literally reverting the one-line fix, rerunning, and reapplying it — not assumed. Full
`db2-parser` module test suite (`Db2RoutinesHarnessTest`, `Db2LoopAndParenCaptureTest`,
`Db2AnalysisEngineTest`, and the new test) re-run clean after the fix: all 26 real seed routines
still parse with 0 errors, no regression in any existing `calls=`/`cursors=`/`tableOps=` count.

Rebuilt `db2-parser` (`mvn -pl db2-parser -am install -DskipTests`) then `unified-web`
(`mvn -pl unified-web -am package -DskipTests`), killed the port-8083 process, relaunched with the
exact JVM flags/mongodb-mode args specified for this session. Deleted the stale
`DB2~DB2DEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` analysis via `DELETE /api/parser/analyses/{name}` (not
`/api/entities/...`, which 404s — the real delete endpoint lives on `ParserAnalysisController`),
re-ran it fresh via `POST /api/parser/analyze` with the exact params specified, polled
`/api/queue` to completion (`[3/3] Analysis complete`), then pulled the real
`GET /api/parser/analyses/{name}/call-graph` edge list and confirmed both edges now present from
`ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`:
`{"from":"ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE","to":"ERP_USP_CLOSE_PERIOD","lines":[1364],...}` and
`{"from":"ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE","to":"ERP_FN_FISCAL_PERIOD","lines":[1364],...}` — same line number for
both (as expected, since they're on the same source statement; the fresh re-parse's own line
numbering is relative to the freshly-fetched source text, not the seed file's absolute line 24915).

Files touched: `db2-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/db2/visitor/Db2AnalysisVisitor.java` (1-line
fix + comment), `db2-parser/src/test/java/com/plsql/db2/Db2NestedCallInCallStatementTest.java`
(new test). No shared/cross-dialect file touched — `ParserAnalysisController.java`'s
facet-filtering code was not opened for editing, per scope. Not committed (not a git repo).

## §262 — `procId`-alone correctness trap on `/cursors`/`/dynamic-sql` (and every other scope+procId facet) fixed, one consistent contract across all facets

Confirmed real bug, found independently on two dialects (MySQL `ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`, SQL Server
`USP_RUNMRPCYCLE`): `GET /api/parser/analyses/{name}/cursors?procId=<nodeId>&limit=50` (and the
equivalent on `/dynamic-sql`) did NOT scope results to that one procedure — it silently returned an
unfiltered, whole-analysis dump, 200 OK with wrong data. `directProcId=...` (a different parameter,
undiscoverable without reading the source) already worked correctly on `/cursors`; on `/dynamic-sql`
the only working workaround was `procId=...&scope=direct` — the two facets didn't even accept the
same parameter shape for "scope to one procedure", and neither rejected/warned on the naive
`?procId=X` alone.

Root cause, in `ParserScopeResolver.predicate` (`unified-web/src/main/java/com/plsqlanalyzer/web/
parser/service/ParserScopeResolver.java`), the shared helper every `scope`/`procId`-accepting facet
in `ParserAnalysisController` routes through (`CURSORS`, `DYNAMIC_SQL`, `JOINS`, `TABLES`,
`SEQUENCES`): `if (scope == null || scope.isBlank()) return null;` — a blank/absent `scope` meant
"no filtering at all", full stop, regardless of whether `procId` was present. `procId` was only ever
consulted once a *non-blank* `scope` had already selected a filtering mode (`direct`/`subtree`/
`subflow`); with `scope` absent, `procId` was read by the code but never used. This was not a
per-facet inconsistency in the shared code path itself — `getJoins`/`getTablesPage` have the exact
same bug, just harder to trip over live in practice, since `directProcId` (a real, correctly-wired
parameter one call-site earlier) exists on those two and is more likely to be reached for by someone
reading `joins.js`/`cursors.js`. `dynamic-sql`'s controller method never wires `directProcId` at
all, which is why `scope=direct` was the only working companion there.

Fixed with one change, in the shared resolver only: when `scope` is blank but `procId` is present
(and not the package-root sentinel), default `scope` to `"direct"` before proceeding. `procId` alone
now means "this node only" on every facet that accepts it, matching `directProcId`'s existing
one-parameter contract — no separate `scope=direct` companion required, and no per-facet
special-casing needed since the fix lives in the one shared predicate() every facet already calls.

New regression tests, `unified-web/src/test/java/com/plsqlanalyzer/web/parser/controller/
ParserAnalysisControllerProcIdScopeTest.java`, following the existing
`ParserAnalysisControllerPlsqlScopeTest` pattern (reflective controller construction, mocked
`AnalysisRepository`, a real `ParserScopeResolver` wired to a mocked `AnalysisService` stubbed with
a single-node call tree for the target `procId`):

## §263 — SQL Server `EXEC(@sql)`/`sp_executesql` type conflation, and cursor lifecycle never
tracked past DECLARE, both fixed for real (`USP_RUNMRPCYCLE`)

Two confirmed real bugs, found via a real audit comparing analyzer output against the live SQL
Server DB (`SQLSERVER~SQLSERVERDEMO~LOCAL~USP_RUNMRPCYCLE`, schema `erp`).

**Bug 1 — dynamic-SQL type conflation.** T-SQL has two structurally different dynamic-SQL
mechanisms: `EXEC(@sql)` (plain string execution, no parameterization) and
`EXEC sp_executesql @sql, @params, ...` (parameterized, injection-safer). `SqlServerAnalysisVisitor
.visitExecStatement` (`sqlserver-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/sqlserver/visitor/
SqlServerAnalysisVisitor.java`) bucketed both under `SqlServerDynamicSqlInfo.Kind
.EXEC_SP_EXECUTESQL` — the `ctx.routineName() == null` branch (the real `EXEC(@sql)` form) reused
the same enum constant as the real `sp_executesql` branch a few lines below it. Confirmed live: 9
real `EXEC(@dxNN)` calls in the source (e.g. line 163's `EXEC(@dx17);`) all reported as
`EXEC_SP_EXECUTESQL`, indistinguishable from the 132 real `sp_executesql` calls.

Fixed by adding a distinct `EXEC_STRING` constant to `SqlServerDynamicSqlInfo.Kind`
(`sqlserver-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/sqlserver/model/SqlServerDynamicSqlInfo.java`) and using
it in the `routineName() == null` branch only, leaving `EXEC_SP_EXECUTESQL` for the real
`sp_executesql` branch.

**Bug 2 — cursor lifecycle never tracked past DECLARE.** Every one of 121 cursor rows returned by
`/cursors` for this analysis had `"operations":["DECLARE"]` only, even though every cursor's real
source (verified for `cur5`, lines 72-85) has `DECLARE`, `OPEN`, 2× `FETCH NEXT ... INTO`, `CLOSE`,
`DEALLOCATE`. Root cause was two-layered, not one:

1. `SqlServerAnalysisVisitor` never recorded `OPEN`/`FETCH`/`CLOSE`/`DEALLOCATE` against the
   matching cursor at all — the T-SQL grammar's catch-all `otherStatement` rule swallows all four
   (no dedicated grammar rules exist for them), and nothing matched them back to a declared cursor
   by name. Fixed by adding `SqlServerCursorInfo.stmtOperations` (a new `List<CursorStmtOp>` field,
   `sqlserver-parser/.../model/SqlServerCursorInfo.java`) and a
   `recordCursorLifecycleOp`/`CURSOR_LIFECYCLE_PATTERN` regex pass in `visitOtherStatement` that
   matches `OPEN <cur>`/`FETCH ... FROM <cur>`/`CLOSE <cur>`/`DEALLOCATE <cur>` text and attaches
   each occurrence, by name, to the already-declared `SqlServerCursorInfo` in the same routine scope
   (`DECLARE` itself is not re-added here — it is already carried via the cursor's own `line`, the
   same convention the Postgres dialect's own cursor-lifecycle fix already established, avoiding a
   double-counted `DECLARE` downstream).
2. Even with (1) fixed, two more layers between the parser and the live `/cursors` endpoint dropped
   the data:
   - `ChunkedFlowWriter` (`plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/parser/flow/ChunkedFlowWriter.java`)
     completely ignored the shared `CursorInfo.stmtOperations` field a dialect parser already
     populated, and instead *re-derived* cursor ops from `node.getStatements()` using an
     Oracle-only statement-type vocabulary (`OPEN_CURSOR`/`FETCH`/`CLOSE_CURSOR`/`BULK_COLLECT`)
     that SQL Server's own statement types (`OPEN`/`FETCH`/`CLOSE`) never match, and had no
     `DEALLOCATE` handling at all. Fixed by preferring `CursorInfo.getStmtOperations()` when the
     dialect parser already supplied it, falling back to the existing statement-derived path
     otherwise (unchanged behavior for dialects, like Oracle, that don't populate it).
   - `EntityCursorsReader` (`unified-web/src/main/java/com/plsqlanalyzer/web/parser/service/
     EntityCursorsReader.java`, the mongodb-mode/entity-read facet actually serving `/cursors` in
     this session's running app) read `stmtOperations` as though it were embedded directly on the
     `am_cursor_decl` Mongo document. It never is: `Splitter`
     (`analysis-mongo-ingest/.../map/Splitter.java`) puts every non-empty array field, with no
     exceptions, into its own child collection (`am_cursor_decl__stmt_operations`), keyed by the
     parent's own `key` as `parentRef` — exactly like `am_cursor_object` already is. Fixed by
     querying that child collection and joining by `parentRef == am_cursor_decl.key`, additively (no
     existing field renamed/removed, no shape change to `am_cursor_decl` itself).

Both `SqlServerProcedureParser.toCursors` (`plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/parser/multidb/
SqlServerProcedureParser.java`) — which previously dropped `stmtOperations` entirely when copying
`SqlServerCursorInfo` → the shared `CursorInfo` — was also fixed to carry the new field across.

New regression tests, `sqlserver-parser/src/test/java/com/plsql/sqlserver/
SqlServerAnalysisEngineTest.java`:
- `dynamicSql_execStringAndSpExecuteSqlHaveDifferentTypes` — a procedure with both `EXEC(@v_sql)`
  and `EXEC sp_executesql @v_sql` asserts they get `EXEC_STRING` and `EXEC_SP_EXECUTESQL`
  respectively (not the same type), with the `EXEC_STRING` entry at the right line.
- `cursor_fullLifecycleTracked` — a procedure with `DECLARE cur5 CURSOR ...`, `OPEN`, 2× `FETCH
  NEXT ... INTO`, `CLOSE`, `DEALLOCATE` asserts all four post-DECLARE operations appear in
  `stmtOperations` (2 distinct `FETCH` entries for the 2 real fetches), in non-decreasing line
  order.

Confirmed real before/after: both new tests failed to compile before the fix (`EXEC_STRING`/
`getStmtOperations()`/`CursorStmtOp` did not exist yet — a stronger signal than a runtime assertion
failure, since the types themselves were missing). After the fix, full `sqlserver-parser` suite:
28/28 green (`SqlServerAnalysisEngineTest` 24/24 including the 2 new tests, plus
`FlowsParseHarnessTest` and `MergeSetPhantomTableTest` unaffected). `plsql-parser` module: 318 tests
via reactor, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (`PlsqlEntityMapperTest.mapsTheWholeCorpus`, a
corpus-token-count assertion against static on-disk `data/plsql-parse` JSON files this session's
changes never touch — confirmed present before this task started).

Rebuilt `plsql-parser` (installed) then `unified-web` (`mvn -pl <module> -am -DskipTests
package`/`install`), killed and relaunched port 8083 with this session's exact mongodb-mode JVM
args, deleted then fully re-ran the real `SQLSERVER~SQLSERVERDEMO~LOCAL~USP_RUNMRPCYCLE` analysis
via `POST /api/parser/analyze` (`COMPLETE` per `/api/queue`), and verified live:
- `GET .../dynamic-sql`: type breakdown `{SET_SQL: 252, EXEC_SP_EXECUTESQL: 132, EXEC_STRING: 120}`;
  line 163 of `USP_RUNMRPCYCLE` (the real `EXEC(@dx17);` reported in the audit) now shows
  `"type":"EXEC_STRING"`.
- `GET .../cursors`: all 121 cursor rows now show
  `"operations":["DECLARE","OPEN","FETCH","CLOSE","DEALLOCATE"]` — `cur5` specifically confirmed
  with `accessCount:6` and all 5 access-detail lines (73/74/74/84/86/86) matching the real source.
- Verified directly against MongoDB (`am_cursor_decl__stmt_operations`) that the ingest pipeline now
