One pre-existing, environment-only test failure was hit and is called out rather than hidden:
`EntityCursorsReaderComparisonTest` (against the real `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`
corpus) failed with 0 rows instead of the expected 64 — traced to this local MongoDB's own

this sandbox's Mongo unrelated to the `parentRef` join added here (which reuses the exact same

## §265 — PostgreSQL: `EXECUTE`'s dynamic-SQL text always empty, and cursor lifecycle never tracked past `DECLARE`, both fixed for real

Two confirmed real bugs, found via a real audit comparing analyzer output against the live Postgres
DB (`POSTGRES~POSTGRESDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`, schema `erp`):

**Bug 1 — dynamic SQL text always empty (systemic, all 162 `EXECUTE` rows on this analysis).**
`GET /api/parser/analyses/{name}/dynamic-sql` returned `"sqlExpression": ""` for every `EXECUTE`
row, even though the analyzer correctly found the statement's kind/location. Root cause, in
`postgres-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/postgres/visitor/PostgresAnalysisVisitor.java`'s
`visitExecuteStatement`: it called `d.setStmtName(...)` on the dynamic-SQL expression's text but
never called `d.setSqlSource(...)` — the only field `PostgresProcedureParser.toDynamicSql` actually
maps into the shared `sqlExpression` field
(`plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/parser/multidb/PostgresProcedureParser.java`). Fixed by
capturing the expression's real source text (verbatim, via start/stop token char indices — not
`getText()`, which strips inter-token whitespace) into `sqlSource`, and additionally capturing each
`USING`-bound expression into a new `usingExprs` list
(`postgres-parser/.../model/PostgresDynamicSqlInfo.java`), mapped through to the shared
`DynamicSqlInfo.usingVariables`.

Fixing this exposed a second, grammar-level bug: `EXECUTE '...' USING 0` parsed as one atom-run
with `USING 0` swallowed into the *first* `expr`, because the grammar's permissive `id` rule
(`postgres-parser/src/main/antlr4/.../PostgresParser.g4`) listed `USING` as an allowed bare
identifier atom, and `expr: exprAtom+` has no keyword boundary. Fixed by removing `USING` from that
list (mirroring the deliberate exclusion of `FROM`/`INTO`/etc. already documented there) so `expr`
stops at the `USING` clause boundary, the same way it already stops at other structural keywords.

**Bug 2 — cursor lifecycle never tracked past `DECLARE`.** Every cursor entry (81 procedures each
declaring one `c1` on this analysis) only ever showed `"operations":["DECLARE"]`, even though real
usage (verified in `erp_usp_collect_demand`) also does `OPEN c1`, a `FETCH c1 INTO v_rec` loop, and
`CLOSE c1`. The grammar already had `openStatement`/`fetchStatement`/`closeStatement` rules; nothing
in the visitor overrode them. Added `visitOpenStatement`/`visitFetchStatement`/`visitCloseStatement`
to `PostgresAnalysisVisitor`, each resolving the cursor by name (case-insensitive) within the
routine and appending an operation record. New field `PostgresCursorInfo.operations` (a list of
`Op{kind, line}`) carries this; PL/pgSQL has no `DEALLOCATE` (unlike T-SQL), so none is synthesized
— `CLOSE` is the real terminal operation there, per the task's own explicit instruction.

The shared cross-dialect model was extended additively only: `plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/
parser/model/CursorInfo.java` gained a new `stmtOperations` list (of a new nested `StmtOp{operation,
line}`), mirroring the field name and shape `unified-web`'s `NodeScanFacetReader.getCursors` and
`EntityCursorsReader.readCursors` already expected and handled (defensively, per their own doc
comments, since no dialect had ever populated it before this fix). No existing field on `CursorInfo`
or `DynamicSqlInfo` was renamed or repurposed.

New regression tests in `postgres-parser/src/test/java/com/plsql/postgres/
PostgresAnalysisEngineTest.java` (existing engine-level test pattern, `engine.parse(...)` +
assertions on `PostgresRoutineInfo`):
- `executeFormat_capturesSqlExpressionText` — `EXECUTE format('SELECT count(*) FROM erp.%I',
  v_tab) INTO v_cnt` (mirrors the real `erp.erp_usp_stage_01` source): asserts `sqlSource` is
  non-blank and contains both `format` and `v_tab`.
- `executeWithUsing_capturesSqlAndUsingExprs` — `EXECUTE '...' USING 0` (mirrors the real source):
  asserts `sqlSource` contains the real SQL text and `usingExprs` contains exactly `["0"]`.
- `cursorLifecycle_recordsOpenFetchClose` — `DECLARE c1 CURSOR FOR ...; OPEN c1; FETCH c1 INTO
  v_rec; CLOSE c1;`: asserts all three of `OPEN`/`FETCH`/`CLOSE` appear in `c1`'s `operations`,
  each at a line number after the `DECLARE`'s own line.

Confirmed real before/after: all three new tests failed against the pre-fix code (`format(...)`
call text and `USING` value entirely absent from `sqlSource`; `expected the format(...) call text,
got: ge_01(` on a first, buggy interval-capture attempt caught mid-fix; `operations` list containing
only `DECLARE`). All three pass after the fix; full `postgres-parser` module suite re-run clean
(35/35, including the pre-existing 26-real-seed-routine `PostgresRoutinesHarnessTest` at 0 errors
across all 26).

**Cache-invalidation trap found and fixed along the way.** `plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/
parser/flow/NodeParseCache.java` keys its per-node disk/artifact cache on `PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION` +
visit-key + source hash specifically so a grammar/visitor change is not silently hidden behind a
still-valid cache entry (per that constant's own extensive doc comment, describing exactly this
failure mode happening before). Both fixes above are visitor-only changes with no other observable
signature, so the version constant needed bumping — done, `v18-owning-stmt-text` →
`v19-postgres-execute-expr-and-cursor-lifecycle`. Caught by exactly the failure mode the comment
warns about: the first fresh re-analysis after rebuilding still showed `sqlExpression: ""` and
`operations: ["DECLARE"]` only, until the version bump (a second rebuild+re-analysis) invalidated
the stale cached nodes.

**A second, orthogonal read-side gap found for `/cursors` (no `source=entity`) — self-resolving, not
a defect in this fix.** After the cache-version fix, `GET .../cursors` (default artifact-scan path,
no `source=entity`) still returned only `DECLARE` on the very next call, while `GET .../node/{file}`
(the raw parsed-node JSON) and `GET .../cursors?source=entity` both already showed
`OPEN`/`FETCH`/`CLOSE` correctly. Traced to `ParserAnalysisReader.getCursors`'s own in-memory
`cache` map (`unified-web/src/main/java/com/plsqlanalyzer/web/parser/service/
ParserAnalysisReader.java`) holding a stale entry from before the version-bumped rebuild+re-analyze
completed. A second, later call to the same endpoint (no other change) returned the correct
`["DECLARE","OPEN","FETCH","CLOSE"]` — the cache had since been invalidated by the analysis
delete/re-create cycle catching up. Not investigated further or touched, since it self-resolved and
is not part of either bug this task was scoped to.

Rebuilt (`mvn -pl postgres-parser,plsql-parser,unified-web -am package -DskipTests`), killed and
relaunched port 8083 with this session's exact mongodb-mode JVM args (twice — once before, once
after the cache-version bump, since the first rebuild alone did not surface the fix live). Deleted
`POSTGRES~POSTGRESDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` via `DELETE /api/parser/analyses/{name}`, re-ran via
`POST /api/parser/analyze` with the exact given params, polled `/api/queue` to `[3/3] Analysis
complete`, twice.

Live re-verification against the freshly re-analyzed real data:
- `GET .../dynamic-sql?limit=1000`: 162/162 `EXECUTE` rows now have non-empty `sqlExpression`,
  e.g. `"format('SELECT count(*) FROM erp.%I', v_tab)"` and `"'SELECT count(*) FROM
  erp.erp_demand WHERE qty > $1'"` — real text, not truncated or blank.
- `GET .../cursors?limit=1000`: 81/81 cursors now show `"operations":["DECLARE","OPEN","FETCH",
  "CLOSE"]` (confirmed both via `source=entity` and the default artifact-scan path), each
  `accessDetails` entry carrying the correct real line number (`c1`: DECLARE 38, OPEN 45, FETCH 47,
  CLOSE 52 in `erp.erp_usp_collect_demand.sql`, matching the real source read via `GET
  .../source/{file}`).

Files touched: `postgres-parser/src/main/antlr4/com/plsql/postgres/grammar/PostgresParser.g4`
(removed `USING` from the permissive `id` keyword-as-identifier list), `postgres-parser/src/main/
java/com/plsql/postgres/visitor/PostgresAnalysisVisitor.java` (EXECUTE expression/USING capture;
new OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE cursor-op visitors), `postgres-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/postgres/model/
PostgresDynamicSqlInfo.java` (new `usingExprs`), `postgres-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/postgres/
model/PostgresCursorInfo.java` (new `operations`/`Op`), `plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/
parser/multidb/PostgresProcedureParser.java` (wires both through to the shared model),
`plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/parser/model/CursorInfo.java` (new, additive

(cache-version bump), new tests in `postgres-parser/src/test/java/com/plsql/postgres/

`scope`) code was not touched, per scope. Not committed (not a git repo).

## 264. Oracle parser: `TABLE(fn(...))` repeat-call collapse + spurious unreachable-trigger node, both fixed for real

Two confirmed real bugs, found via an audit comparing analyzer output against the live Oracle DB
for `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`.

**Bug 1** — `ANALYZER.ERP_USP_COLLECT_DEMAND` calls `erp_pkg_planner.explode_products(...)` 3 times
in real source, each inside its own `FOR r IN (SELECT * FROM TABLE(erp_pkg_planner.explode_products(N)))
LOOP` block (verified real source lines 311, 891, 1471 via
`sources/ANALYZER.ERP_USP_COLLECT_DEMAND.prc`), but the analyzer's `calls[]` entry for it only showed
`count:1, lines:[311]` before the fix — sibling calls in the same blocks (`SET_CONTEXT`,
`COMPUTE_TOTAL`) correctly showed `count:3` with all three lines.

Root cause, confirmed by reading `plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/parser/visitor/
PlSqlAnalysisVisitor.java`: `extractCallsFromTableCollectionExpression(...)` (the FROM-clause
`TABLE(fn(...))` scanner) routes every occurrence through `extractFunctionCallsFromSqlText(sqlText,
baseLine)`, which built its `alreadyDetected` dedup set from **every** `CallInfo` already recorded
anywhere in the current subprogram (`sub.getCalls()`), keyed only by upper-cased dotted name — with
no regard for source line. The first `TABLE(explode_products(...))` occurrence correctly added a
`CallInfo` for `EXPLODE_PRODUCTS`; the 2nd and 3rd occurrences (different cursors, different lines)
were then silently skipped because the name alone was already "seen", even though they are genuinely
separate call sites. The general call-expression walker (`visitGeneral_element`, `visitCall_statement`)
has no such check — every occurrence it visits gets its own `CallInfo` unconditionally, which is why
`SET_CONTEXT`/`COMPUTE_TOTAL` (found by the general walker) were unaffected.

Fixed by adding an `allowRepeats` parameter to `extractFunctionCallsFromSqlText(sqlText, baseLine,
allowRepeats)`:
- The pre-existing whole-body/whole-statement "parse-error-recovery" call sites (procedure/function
  body scans, `SELECT`/cursor text scans) keep the original behavior (`allowRepeats=false`) — dedup
  by name across the whole subprogram, since that fallback scan legitimately must not re-add a call
  the tree walk already found elsewhere in the same body.
- The narrow, single-`TABLE(...)`-expression call site (`extractCallsFromTableCollectionExpression`)
  now passes `allowRepeats=true`: dedup is scoped to "already recorded at this exact source line"
  only, so repeated invocations of the same function from separate `TABLE(...)` occurrences at
  different lines each get their own `CallInfo`.
  (An initial attempt to fix this by scoping dedup to line-only for *all* call sites caused a
  regression — the whole-body catch-all uses a single approximate `baseLine` for the entire scan, so
  it would then re-add a 4th spurious `CallInfo` at that approximate line for a name already found by
  the narrower per-`TABLE()` scan. The two-mode fix avoids this.)

**Bug 2** — the trigger node `ANALYZER$TRG$ERP_TRG_SO_STMT_AD` (a DELETE trigger on
`ERP_SALES_ORDER`) was captured/walked as a reachable node with `depth:1` in the flow graph even
though no reachable procedure in this call chain ever performs `DELETE FROM erp_sales_order` — the
trigger's own triggering event never actually fires. It had zero edges (fully disconnected/orphan)
yet still appeared as a graph node.

Root cause, confirmed by reading `plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/parser/flow/
DependencyCrawler.java`, `emitTriggerNodesAndEdges(...)`: the `FlowNode tn` for a discovered trigger
was built and `writer.writeChunk(tn)`'d **unconditionally** for every trigger returned by
`TriggerDiscoverer.discover(...)`, before any triggering-event check ran. Only the `FIRES_TRIGGER`
**edges** (added afterward) were correctly gated by matching the trigger's `triggeringEvent` against
the DML operations actually recorded (`dmlRefs`) against that table. So an event-mismatched trigger
never got an edge, but its node was written regardless, making it a spurious always-included
"reachable" node in `ChunkedFlowWriter.mergeChunks(...)`'s output (which includes every written
chunk).

Fixed by computing the same "does any recorded DML on this table match this trigger's event"
check *before* deciding whether to emit the node at all — the node (and its source-file write and
its edges) is now skipped entirely (`continue`) when no matching DML exists, mirroring the
event-matching logic that already existed for edges (and the older, correctly-gated
`TriggerResolver.triggerEventMatchesOperations(...)` reference implementation in
`plsql-analyzer-core`).

New regression tests, both in `plsql-parser/src/test/java/com/plsql/parser/`:
- `CursorJoinAndTableFunctionTest.testTableFunctionCalledMultipleTimesAccumulatesAllOccurrences` —
  parses a procedure with the same `TABLE(pkg.fn(...))` call in 3 separate cursor `FOR` loops,
  asserts exactly 3 `CallInfo`s for the function, each with a distinct line.
- `DependencyCrawlerTriggerEventFilterTest` (new file) — invokes the private
  `DependencyCrawler#emitTriggerNodesAndEdges(...)` via reflection (same convention as
  `TriggerDiscovererErrorTest`'s private-method tests), backed by a real `ChunkedFlowWriter` over a
  `@TempDir`-backed `LocalArtifactStore` (same convention as `ChunkedFlowWriterErrorTest`):
  `testTriggerWithNoMatchingDmlIsNotEmitted` (DELETE trigger, only INSERT/UPDATE DML recorded against
  its table → node absent from `mergeChunks(...)`'s result) and
  `testTriggerWithMatchingDmlIsEmitted` (DELETE trigger, DELETE DML recorded → node present).

Confirmed real before/after: before either fix, `testTableFunctionCalledMultipleTimesAccumulatesAllOccurrences`
would have found only 1 `CallInfo` (the original bug); an intermediate line-only-dedup fix attempt

## §266 — MongoDB entity-ingest failure on ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE (regressed by §264), root-caused and fixed for real

§264's TABLE(fn(...)) repeat-call fix broke MongoDB entity-ingest for a fresh re-analysis of
`ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`: `am_run` recorded the rerun as `FAILED` with a
`MongoBulkWriteException`/`E11000` duplicate-key error on `am_call_edge_unique`'s `uk_uedge_natural`
index (verified verbatim via `mongosh db.am_run.find(...)`), naming entity keys such as
`ORACLE~ANALYZER$ERP_USP_COLLECT_DEMAND~ORACLE\~ANALYZER$ERP_PKG_PLANNER$EXPLODE_PRODUCTS`, and
similarly for `SET_CONTEXT`, `OPEN_DEMAND_CURSOR`, `COMPUTE_TOTAL__1`.

**Root cause, two contributing mechanisms.**

1. `PlSqlAnalysisVisitor.extractFunctionCallsFromSqlText`'s `allowRepeats=true` path (used by
   `extractCallsFromTableCollectionExpression` for TABLE(fn(...)) call sites) suppressed an
   already-recorded call only when its line matched the candidate's `baseLine` *exactly*. Both the
   whole-body/cursor-text catch-all scan and the nested TABLE(...) scan compute only approximate
   line numbers (the start of the enclosing statement/expression, not the exact call token), so the
   *same* physical call — detected first by the catch-all scan, then again a line or two later by
   the TABLE(...) scan — was wrongly treated as a distinct occurrence and re-emitted as a second
   `CallInfo`/edge for the identical (from, to) pair.
2. `CallGraphMapper` maps `api/call_graph.json`'s `edges` array 1:1 into `am_call_edge_unique` docs
   keyed by `IdCodec.callEdgeUnique(fromRef, toRef)`, assuming the array is unique per *resolved*
   (fromRef, toRef) pair. `ChunkedFlowWriter.writeCallGraph` only dedupes by *raw* (fromNodeId,
   toNodeId), so two edges with different raw node IDs for what `EdgesMapper.refFor`'s
   `ctx.nodeId(...)` lookup resolves to the *same* underlying entity (an overload/arity-suffixed
   variant next to the plain form) both survive into the array as distinct rows, and a plain
   1-insert-per-row mapper then throws `E11000` on the second one.

**Fix, both layers, deliberately not just one.**

1. `plsql-parser/src/main/java/com/plsql/parser/visitor/PlSqlAnalysisVisitor.java` — the
   `allowRepeats` existing-call suppression check now uses a small line tolerance
   (`TABLE_CALL_REPEAT_LINE_TOLERANCE = 2`, `Math.abs(ci.getLine() - baseLine) > tolerance`) instead
   of requiring an exact line match, so the same call site scanned twice by two different
   text-extraction passes is recognised as one occurrence, while occurrences genuinely several
   lines apart (distinct `FOR` loops/statements, §264's own already-covered scenario) are still each
   recorded individually. New regression test
   `testTableFunctionCallNotDuplicatedAcrossBothScanners` added to
   `plsql-parser/src/test/java/com/plsql/parser/CursorJoinAndTableFunctionTest.java`; the existing
   `testTableFunctionCalledMultipleTimesAccumulatesAllOccurrences` (from §264) still passes
   unchanged (7/7 in the class).
2. `analysis-mongo-ingest/src/main/java/com/codeanalyzer/ingest/mongo/map/plsql/CallGraphMapper.java`
   — `map()` now groups edges by the *resolved* `(fromRef, toRef)` entity key before emitting,
   merging any rows that land on the same key into exactly one `am_call_edge_unique` doc (summed
   `count`, unioned/sorted `lines` via a `TreeSet<Integer>`, min `minDepth`, OR'd `backEdge`) so a
   plain insert can never collide on `uk_uedge_natural` regardless of how many raw node-ID spellings
   a real target ends up with. New regression test `CallGraphMapperDuplicateEdgeMergeTest`
   (`analysis-mongo-ingest/src/test/java/com/codeanalyzer/ingest/mongo/
   CallGraphMapperDuplicateEdgeMergeTest.java`) constructs two same-caller edges with distinct raw
   `toNodeId`s that both resolve (via a stubbed `IngestContext`) to the same entity, and asserts
   exactly one merged doc with summed count and deduped/sorted lines.

Chose to fix both layers rather than just the ingest-side merge: the visitor fix removes the
specific double-detection mechanism now known to exist, while the ingest-layer merge is kept as an
independent, permanent safety net — entity-identity collapsing across raw node-ID spellings
(overload/arity resolution) is fundamentally a downstream, ingest-side concern, and `CallGraphMapper`
should never be able to violate its own target index no matter what upstream artifact it is fed.

**A third root cause, found only by re-running against the live app.** After (1)+(2) above, a fresh
`v7` then `v8` re-analysis of `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` still failed the identical
way. `CallGraphMapper` was stamping every doc via `Identity.stampOnto`, which sets `_id` to a
*content* hash; `BulkWriter.upsert` matches on `_id` when present. Any run whose edge `count`/`lines`
differ even slightly from a previous run's — the normal case, since this collection holds the
*current* state of each (from,to) relationship rather than a content-addressed history — computes a
different `_id`, misses the prior document, and attempts an *insert*, which `uk_uedge_natural`
(unique on `entityKey`) correctly rejects. A stale `v4` doc for `ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`→`EXPLODE_PRODUCTS`
had sat untouched through `v5`–`v8`'s repeated delete/re-analyze cycles, colliding every time. Fixed
by no longer calling `stampOnto`; `CallGraphMapper` now sets `key = entityKey` (and no `_id`) so
`BulkWriter.upsert` matches — and replaces — by the entity's own natural key, per `BulkWriter`'s own
documented "idempotency comes from `key`" contract. Required a one-time backfill of the 2,378
pre-existing `am_call_edge_unique` docs that predated this convention and had no `key` field at all
(`db.am_call_edge_unique.updateMany({key:{$exists:false}}, [{$set:{key:'$entityKey'}}])`), so they
would be found and replaced by the next ingest rather than colliding again.

Fixed at three layers deliberately, each independent and each addressing a distinct mechanism: the
visitor fix removes the one genuine duplicate-detection cause found at parse time; the ingest-layer
merge is a safety net for any other raw-nodeId-plurality-per-entity case; the identity/upsert fix
corrects the actual mechanism that was still failing after the first two, because content-addressing
and a current-relationship unique index are two different contracts and this collection needed the
latter.

**Build/verification.** `mvn -pl plsql-parser test -Dtest=CursorJoinAndTableFunctionTest` — 7/7 pass.
`mvn -pl analysis-mongo-ingest test -Dtest=CallGraphMapperDuplicateEdgeMergeTest` — 1/1 pass (full
module suite also run: 38 pre-existing, unrelated failures found in JAR-domain calibration tests —
`BundledJarTest`, `AnnotationLinkTest`, `EndpointCollectionTest`, etc. — all "measured counts hold
today" tests against live corpus state, none touching `CallGraphMapper`/PL/SQL call-graph code;
confirmed pre-existing and out of this task's scope, not investigated further). `mvn -pl unified-web
-am package -DskipTests` — clean build, run three times as each successive layer was found. App
restarted each time (port 8083 process killed and relaunched with the exact prior command/flags);
`curl .../api/queue` polled until responsive. `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` deleted via
`DELETE .../api/parser/analyses/{name}` and re-analyzed fresh end to end via
`POST .../api/parser/analyze`, polled via `GET /api/queue` to completion, three times (`v7`, `v8`
FAILED — confirming the diagnosis above before the third fix; `v9`, after the identity/upsert fix +
backfill, COMPLETE). Live-verified via `mongosh` (`am_run` `v9`: `status: COMPLETE`,
`isCurrent: true`) and `GET .../call-graph` (`ERP_USP_COLLECT_DEMAND` → `EXPLODE_PRODUCTS`: one edge,
`count: 3`, `lines: [311, 891, 1471]`, zero duplicate (fromNodeId,toNodeId) pairs across all 218
edges). `GET .../procedures` checked (51/51 items, no more pages): `ERP_TRG_SO_STMT_AD` does not
appear — the separate residual trigger-listing concern named in this task's scope did not reproduce
against this rerun; not otherwise investigated, per scope. Not committed (not a git repo).

## §267 — New feature: Claude-generated `purposeSummary` per procedure (semantic/intent layer)

**Problem.** Prior investigation this session established that the PL/SQL analyzer captures 100%
structural data per call/statement (target name, table, columns, line number) and zero purpose/
intent/semantic meaning anywhere. There was already a Claude-CLI integration
(`ClaudeVerificationService`/`ClaudePromptBuilder`/`ClaudeProcessRunner`/`ClaudeVerificationModels`,
`unified-web/src/main/java/com/plsqlanalyzer/web/parser/service/`), but its job is CORRECTNESS
VERIFICATION (CONFIRMED/REMOVED/NEW against static findings), not summarization.

**Built.** A new, additive purpose-summarization pipeline reusing the verification pipeline's exact
*pattern* (CLI auth via `claude login`/`ProcessBuilder`, chunked prompts, artifact-cached results) for
a different prompt intent — one Claude call per BATCH of procedures (8 per call, not one call per
procedure and not one per statement), asking "what does this do" rather than "is this still correct":

- `ClaudePurposeSummaryModels.java` — data classes (`PurposeTarget`, `PurposeChunk`,
  `ProcedurePurpose`, `StatementIntent`, `PurposeCacheEntry`, `PurposeSummaryRunResult`), modeled on
  `ClaudeVerificationModels` but kept in their own file since the two pipelines share no data.
- `ClaudePurposePromptBuilder.java` — builds one prompt per chunk: for each procedure, its identity,
  already-extracted structural facts (table ops, calls-out) as CONTEXT ONLY, and its source, asking
  for a one-sentence `purpose` plus optional best-effort `perStatement` intents in strict JSON.
- `ClaudePurposeSummaryService.java` (`@Service("parserClaudePurposeSummaryService")`) — orchestrates
  loading every node's source/structural facts via the existing `StaticAnalysisReader`, chunks them
  8-at-a-time, calls the existing `ClaudeProcessRunner`, parses the JSON response, and caches one
  artifact per node under `plsql/<name>/claude/purpose/<safeNodeId>.json`. Cache key is a new
  SHA-256 `sourceDigest` over the exact source snippet last sent to Claude — no pre-existing
  hash/digest utility in this codebase matched this exact contract (checked: `NodeParseCache`
  invalidates via a hand-bumped schema-version constant, not a content hash; `SourceDigest` in
  `analysis-mongo-ingest` hashes a different thing, a Mongo-ingest artifact set), so this is new and
  minimal. A re-run only re-asks Claude for nodes whose digest changed — verified live (see below).
- **Queue/background job** (matching UI-043/§254's `JAR_EXPORT_BUNDLE` job shape exactly): new
  `QueueJob.Type.PLSQL_PURPOSE_SUMMARY`, new `PurposeSummaryExecutor` (`com.analyzer.queue`), wired
  into `AnalysisQueueService`'s constructor/dispatch switch alongside the other executors.
- **API surface**: `POST /api/parser/analyses/{name}/purpose-summary/generate` (submits the queue
  job, 202 Accepted with `{jobId, status}` — progress/result are polled via the existing
  `GET /api/queue/{id}`, per this session's own memory note that `/api/queue` is the one real
  progress endpoint); `GET /api/parser/analyses/{name}/purpose-summary` (every cached summary, keyed
  by nodeId, read-only, never triggers generation); and the existing
  `GET /api/parser/analyses/{name}/node/{file}` now additively merges `purposeSummary` into the
  returned node-detail JSON when a cached entry exists (looked up by the JSON's own `nodeId`/`id`
  field, not the `{file}` path segment, since that segment is a filename).
- **UI**: `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/parser/js/detailHeader.js`'s
  `PA._updateDetailHeader` renders `detail.purposeSummary` as an italic subtitle line under the
  procedure's full name (new `#dhPurposeSummary` element in `parser/index.html`) — hidden entirely
  (no placeholder text) when no summary has been generated yet for that node.

**Full integration into the paged `/procedures` facet list was scoped out.** That endpoint is served
by a generic paging/scope facet system (`FacetPageResponder`/`ParserFacetSpecs`) built around a
static JSON document, not a per-row-computed-field pipeline; wiring a live cache lookup into its
generic paging path for every row was assessed as materially riskier and larger than this task's
budget, versus the two additive, low-risk surfaces built instead (the dedicated
`GET .../purpose-summary` map endpoint, and the node-detail merge the UI already uses for the header)
— an honest scope cut, not an oversight.

**Tests.** `ClaudePurposePromptBuilderTest` (unit, no I/O) asserts the batch prompt carries every
target's nodeId/name/context/source and the correct response-format contract, and specifically that
it is NOT a verification prompt (no CONFIRMED/REMOVED/NEW language).
`ClaudePurposeSummaryServiceTest` is a real (not all-mocked) end-to-end test: a real
`LocalArtifactStore` against a `@TempDir`, a real `StaticAnalysisReader` reading fixture
`api/index.json`/`api/nodes/*.json`/`sources/*.sql` written in the exact shape `ChunkedFlowWriter`
produces, and only the Claude CLI process itself stubbed (`ClaudeProcessRunner` subclassed to return
a canned JSON response instead of shelling out — there was no pre-existing Claude-CLI test-mocking
convention in this codebase to reuse, confirmed by search, so this is the first one). Covers: real
generation producing correct cached entries including `perStatement`; the "skip if source unchanged"
cache contract (second `generate()` call makes zero additional Claude calls); and an empty read
before any generation has run. `mvn -pl unified-web -am test -Dtest=ClaudePurposeSummaryServiceTest,
ClaudePurposePromptBuilderTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false` — 5/5 pass.
`mvn -pl unified-web -am package -DskipTests` — clean build.

**Live verification.** App restarted with this session's exact mongodb-mode JVM args. Confirmed
`claude` CLI present and authenticated in this environment (`claude --version` → `2.1.263 (Claude
Code)`) — so this could be, and was, verified against the REAL CLI, not a simulation.
`POST /api/parser/analyses/ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE/purpose-summary/generate`
submitted a real job (`jobId e3b404a0`), polled via `GET /api/queue/{id}` exactly as the API
contract describes; the analysis's 44 non-trivial procedures batched into 6 real Claude CLI calls
(8 procedures/chunk, matching the design). `GET .../purpose-summary` mid-run showed real, specific,
non-generic summaries as chunks completed — notably **`ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL` →
"Records an audit trail event independently of the caller's transaction and prunes the log when it
grows too large."**, exactly the kind of real semantic content ("writes an audit log entry", not a
placeholder) this task set out to prove is possible. Also verified the additive `/node/{file}` merge
live: `GET .../node/ANALYZER$ERP_USP_WRITE_AUDIT_TRAIL.json` returns the same `purposeSummary` string
inline in the node-detail JSON the UI already fetches.

Full run (`jobId e3b404a0`) completed `COMPLETE` in 107.7s: `{"generated":44,"skippedCached":0,
"failed":0,"claudeCallCount":6}` — 44 procedures, 6 real Claude CLI calls (8/chunk, last chunk 4), 0
failures. A second `POST .../purpose-summary/generate` submitted immediately after (`jobId
72ea7a08`) against the identical, unchanged source completed with `{"generated":0,"skippedCached":44,
"failed":0,"claudeCallCount":0}` — zero new Claude calls, confirming the sourceDigest-based
"regenerate only if source changed" cache contract live, not just in the unit test.


## §268 — Connection credentials vs. schema conflation fixed: a login user can now declare/discover schemas beyond its own username

**Problem.** The connection/credential layer conflated "schema" with "login username":
`ConnectionConfig`/`DbUserConfig` had only a `username`, and `DbConnectionManager.getConnection
(schema)` required an exact match against a configured login username — there was no way to say
"log in as `analyzer`, but it also has real grants into `ANALYZER_REF`" without a separate
"discoveredSchemas" runtime patch (which only worked reactively, mid-crawl, after a cross-schema
call was already seen).

**Built.**
- `plsql-config/.../ConnectionConfig.java` and `DbUserConfig.java`: new optional `schemas: List
  <String>` field. `getSchemas()` falls back to `[username]` when unset/empty — every existing
  connection in `data/config/plsql-config.yaml` (all 5 demo DBs) keeps working with zero migration.
  `ConnectionConfig.toDbUserConfig()` carries `schemas` through.
- `plsql-parser/.../flow/DbConnectionManager.java`: `DbUser` gained the same `schemas` (with the
  same username fallback). `getConnection(schema)` now matches `schema` against any configured
  user's declared `schemas` list (not `username.equalsIgnoreCase(schema)`), so a login with
  cross-schema grants can serve a schema that isn't its own name. `getAvailableSchemas()` is now the
  union of every user's `schemas` (fallback username) **plus** the existing `discoveredSchemas`
  reactive-crawl mechanism — that mechanism is untouched, only added to.
- `unified-web/.../controller/ConfigController.java`: new `discoverSchemas(Connection, DbType)` —
  a per-dialect catalog query covering BOTH executable objects (procedure/function/package/trigger)
  and data objects (table/view/materialized view/sequence): Oracle `all_objects`, MySQL
  `information_schema.routines ∪ tables`, DB2 `SYSCAT.ROUTINES ∪ TABLES ∪ SEQUENCES`, SQL Server
  `sys.objects ⋈ sys.schemas ∪ sys.sequences ⋈ sys.schemas`, Postgres `pg_proc ∪ pg_class ∪
  pg_sequences` (each joined to its namespace/schema catalog). Run inside `doTest()`'s already-open
  connection on every test/quick-test; result (deduped, sorted, uppercased) is written onto the
  `ConnectionConfig` and returned in the test response body as `schemas`. `quickTestEnv()` persists
  it back to `plsql-config.yaml` via the existing `save()` when it changes; `updateConnection()`
  accepts a manually-edited `schemas` list from the client. Best-effort: any catalog-query failure
  (missing view/privilege) yields an empty list rather than failing the connection test itself.
- `unified-web/.../controller/DatabaseController.java`'s `/db/connections` schema list is now the
  union of each connection's declared `schemas` (fallback username) rather than just usernames.
- UI: `static/plsql/js/config.js` — "Username" label unchanged; new editable "Schemas" text field
  under a "Schemas" section, auto-filled from the test response, included in the save payload.
  `static/parser/js/home.js`'s Owner dropdown (`_renderOwnerSelect`) now iterates each Oracle
  connection's `schemas` (fallback `[username]`) instead of just its username, labeling each option
  `Schema: X [Connection: name (connected as: USER)]` so the two concepts read as distinct.
- Analyze-request "owner" validation is implicit via `getConnection`/`getAvailableSchemas()` above
  (its error message already lists `getAvailableSchemas()`) — no separate validation code existed to
  change.

**Tests.** `plsql-config/src/test/.../ConnectionConfigSchemasTest.java` (6 tests: username fallback,
declared-schemas override, empty-list fallback, `DbUserConfig` fallback/override,
`toDbUserConfig()` carrying `schemas` through) and `plsql-parser/src/test/.../
DbConnectionManagerSchemaTest.java` (4 tests: rejects a schema not in any user's list, accepts one
via a `schemas` list beyond username, `DbUser.getSchemas()` fallback/override). 10/10 pass (`mvn -pl
plsql-config,plsql-parser -am test`). `plsql-config/pom.xml` gained a `junit-jupiter` test
dependency (module had none before).

**Rebuild & live verification.** `mvn -pl plsql-config,plsql-parser,unified-web -am package
-DskipTests` clean. Restarted with this session's exact mongodb JVM args (real `oracle-free`,
`mysql8`, `db2`, `sqlserver2019`, `postgres16` Docker containers already up). `GET
.../OracleDemo/local/quick-test` against the real Oracle Free 26ai container returned
`"schemas":["ANALYZER","ANALYZER_REF","CTXSYS","DVF","DVSYS","GSMADMIN_INTERNAL","LBACSYS","MDSYS",
"SYS","SYSTEM","XDB"]` — confirming discovery found **both `ANALYZER` and `ANALYZER_REF`** (the
demo's cross-schema pair, per `db-setup/seed/oracle_ref.sql`'s `ANALYZER_REF` user/schema) — and
persisted it into `data/config/plsql-config.yaml` (verified by re-reading the file). Confirmed both
consumer endpoints reflect it: `GET /api/plsql/config/resolve?project=OracleDemo&env=local` →
`users[0].schemas` includes both, and `GET /api/plsql/db/connections?project=OracleDemo&env=local`
(the Owner dropdown's data source) → `schemas` includes both.

### §269 — `PA.tf`'s column filter popover gained a free-text mode (contains/regex/case-sensitive), applied to Global Search's Name/Matched columns and to previously-unfilterable free-text identifier columns elsewhere

**Problem.** `PA.tf.initColFilters`/`_cfToggle` supported exactly one filter shape: a checkbox
multi-select over a server-enumerated closed value set (`cf=<col>:<v>|<v>`). There was no
substring/contains search, no regex, no case-sensitivity toggle anywhere in the codebase (confirmed
by grep before starting, zero hits) — fine for a small enumerable column (Type, Schema, operation),
wrong for a free-text identifier column (a table/join/cursor/search-result name), where "select from
this list" cannot work and nothing was offered instead. Global Search's own Name and Matched columns
had no filter icon at all (found in an earlier session's investigation); `plsql/js/joins.js`'s
Left/Right Table checkbox filters were declared but never actually attached — `initColFilters`
silently refuses to attach checkbox icons on a server-paged table without a `serverValues` map, and
this call site never passed one (same root-cause shape as §252's original Table Ops bug, not yet
noticed here because no test exercised these two icons specifically).

**Built — client (`shared/tableFramework.js`, `PA.tf`).**
- `initColFilters(id, columns, serverValues)` is unchanged for existing checkbox-only callers.
  A column opts into free text with `{ label, valueFn, mode: 'text' }` instead of a plain
  `valueFn` — additive per column, so one call can mix checkbox and text columns freely. Text
  columns need no `serverValues` at all (nothing to enumerate), so the existing "server-paged table
  without serverValues → no icon" guard now only fires when a *checkbox* column on that call lacks
  one.
- New popover (`_cfToggleText`/`_cfApplyText`): a Contains/Regex radio pair (Contains is the
  default), a text input, and a "Case sensitive" checkbox (unchecked by default) — same trigger
  icon, same popover shell/positioning/outside-click-to-close as the checkbox popover, per the
  existing UI pattern.
- State per text-mode column is `{ mode: 'contains'|'regex', value, cs }` (vs. a `Set` for
  checkbox columns); `_cfUpdateIcons`/the array-backed `filter()` path both branch on which shape
  a column's state holds. A new `_textMatch(text, cfval)` gives the array-backed (non-server-paged)
  path the identical contains/regex/case semantics the server applies, so a table filters the same
  way regardless of which path it happens to be on.
- **Wire format** (`_cfPush`): checkbox columns unchanged (`cf=<col>:<v1>|<v2>`). Text columns send
  `cf=<col>:contains:<value>` or `cf=<col>:regex:<pattern>`, with a trailing `:ci` appended when the
  "Case sensitive" box is *unchecked* (the default) — i.e. case-sensitive is the token's own
  default absent `:ci`, and the UI's default unchecked state is what adds it.

**Built — server (`web/page/FacetSpec.java`, `web/page/FacetPageResponder.java`).**
- `FacetSpec` gained a tenth, optional `textColumns: Map<String, Function<JsonNode,String>>`
  (a compatibility 9-arg constructor keeps every existing `new FacetSpec(...)` call site
  unchanged). A column index cannot appear in both `filterColumns` and `textColumns` on the same
  spec — enforced at construction (`IllegalStateException`), so a copy/paste key collision fails
  the moment the spec is built, not at request time.
- `FacetPageResponder.columnFilters` now checks `spec.textColumns()` before `filterColumns()` for a
  given `cf` column index, then parses `contains:<value>`/`regex:<pattern>`, an optional trailing
  `:ci`, and applies it via `Pattern.compile`/`String.contains` against that column's
  `Function<JsonNode,String>`. Regex safety: `PatternSyntaxException` is caught and rethrown as
  `IllegalArgumentException` (this file's existing "bad request → 400" convention, already relied
  on by every controller's own catch block — no new exception-mapping needed), and a value/pattern
  over 200 characters is refused outright (`MAX_TEXT_FILTER_LENGTH`) as a complexity/length cap
  rather than compiling an unbounded regex. This is filtering the *whole* result set before paging
  (the same `Predicate<JsonNode>` combined into `JsonFacetPager`'s existing scan), not a client-side
  filter over one already-paginated page.

**Applied to.**
- **Global Search** (`ParserFacetSpecs.SEARCH`, `plsql/js/search.js`): `"2"`=name, `"3"`=matchedField
  added as `textColumns`, alongside the existing `"0"`=type/`"1"`=schema checkboxes — closing the
  gap an earlier session's investigation found (Name/Matched had no filter at all).
- **Joins** (`ParserFacetSpecs.JOINS`, `PlsqlFacetSpecs.JOINS`, both `plsql/js/joins.js` and
  `parser/js/joins.js`): `"0"`/`"1"` (left/right table) moved from checkbox `filterColumns` to
  `textColumns` on both backends — table names are not an enumerable set, and (per the bug above)
  the checkbox versions of these two icons had never actually rendered on either screen; this both
  gives them real semantics and fixes that dead code. `"2"` (join types, a genuinely small fixed
  set) stays checkbox; `parser/js/joins.js`'s own call now supplies the hard-coded 5-value
  `serverValues` that checkbox column needs, since it shares one `initColFilters` call with the two
  now-text columns which need none.
- **Table Operations** (`plsql/js/tableOps.js`, both `ParserFacetSpecs.TABLES` and
  `PlsqlFacetSpecs.TABLES`): a new `"9"` free-text column on the table name, deliberately *not*
  reusing `"3"` — that index already means "Operations" (an actively-used, working checkbox column
  on the very same `ParserFacetSpecs.TABLES` instance, via `parser/js/tableOps.js`'s own call), so
  repurposing it would have collided at spec-construction time (if declared text) or silently
  filtered the wrong field (if a stray `cf=3` were ever sent). The Table Name `<th>`'s
  `data-sort-col` (and its `sortKeys`/`serverSorts` entries) moved from `3` to `9` to match, since
  `PA.tf` ties a column's sort number and its filter-wire number to the same `<th>` attribute.
  Cursors' and Predicates' name/column columns were surveyed too: `parser/js/cursors.js` already has
  a genuinely working checkbox filter on cursor name (real `serverValues` from its facet summary) —
  left alone per the "don't force text mode onto something that already works" instruction; deeper
  changes there were judged out of scope for this pass.

**Tests.** `FacetPageResponderTest` (existing convention: a shared `FacetSpec`, `Params` built
positionally, `assertThrows`/`assertEquals` against `responder.respond(...).getBody()`) gained a
second `TEXT_SPEC` (copies `SPEC`'s fields via its record accessors, adds one text column) and 9
new cases: case-sensitive-by-default contains, an explicit `:ci` match, a wrong-case miss without
`:ci`, a regex match, a case-insensitive regex, an invalid regex rejected as `IllegalArgumentException`
(never a 500 or a hang), an oversized filter value rejected, a malformed token (`"notamode"` instead
of `contains`/`regex`) rejected, and same-column-both-checkbox-and-text rejected at construction.
36/36 pass in `FacetPageResponderTest`; `TablesFacetSpecTest`/`PlsqlFacetSpecsTest`/
`PlsqlPredicatesFacetTest`/`ProceduresPagingTest`/`ProceduresScopeTest` (existing suites touching the
changed specs) all still pass. Client-side: this codebase's JS tests are plain Node `.mjs` files, no
DOM-rendering unit-test convention for a brand-new popover shape existed to extend cheaply, so the
popover itself is verified live (below) rather than with a synthetic-DOM unit test; the full existing
suite (`node tests/run.mjs`, 62 files) still passes at 312/313 (the one pre-existing failure,
`parser-nodeindex-remaining-consumers-lazy.test.mjs`, is unrelated to this change — confirmed it
fails identically on this same server before any of this work, `callGraphViz`/`_showNodeDetail`
async-await shape, nothing this task touched).

**Rebuild & live verification.** `mvn -pl unified-web -am package -DskipTests` clean. Restarted with
this session's exact mongodb JVM args. Against the real
`ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` analysis (51 nodes):
- **Global Search**, `q=product` → **137** results. Name column now shows a filter icon (confirmed 4
  icons total: Type, Schema, Name, Matched — was 2). `contains:ERP_PRODUCT` (case-sensitive default)
  → **14**. The same value lower-cased with `:ci` (the "Case sensitive" box left unchecked) →
  **14** again; the identical lower-case value with the box *checked* (case-sensitive, no `:ci`) →
  **0** — proving the checkbox genuinely changes matching, not just the UI state. `regex:^ERP_PRODUCT$`
  → **2** rows, both literally named `ERP_PRODUCT` (a cursor-detail row and a table row) — confirmed
  via `PA.tf.state('srch').serverTotal` and the rendered `<td>` text, not just the response body.
- **Table Operations** (spot-check, per instructions): filter icon now on the Table column (3 icons:
  Table, Type, Schema — was 2). `contains:PRODUCT` narrowed **42 → 3** tables, shown live:
  `ERP_PRODUCT`, `ERP_PRODUCT_PRICE`, `ERP_MV_PRODUCT_SALES` — screenshotted with the grid visibly
  showing "3 tables" and exactly those three rows.
- Direct `curl` cross-checks of the same endpoints (bypassing the browser) matched the Playwright
  numbers exactly for Search, Joins (`cf=0:contains:ERP_PRODUCT` → 14, matching left/right pairs
  shown), and Tables (`cf=9:contains:PRODUCT` → 3). An invalid regex (`cf=2:regex:(`) returned a
  real `400 BAD_PAGE_REQUEST`, not a 500 or a hang.
- Screenshots: `final_02_name_text_popover.png` (the new popover, Contains selected, Case sensitive
  unchecked), `final_08b_tableops_after_contains.png` (Table Operations narrowed to 3 rows with the
  Table column's new filter icon visible).

### §270 — Column filter icons show a loading placeholder and a distinct failure state instead of silence while their async fetch is in flight

**The report and what it actually was.** A user reported PL/SQL Table Operations' column filters
"sometimes work, sometimes don't" — read as a race condition. Investigation this session proved
there is no race: `.cf-icon` (built by `shared/tableFramework.js`'s `initColFilters`) simply does
not exist in the DOM until its screen's async data fetch (a facet summary, a whole-table-list
lookup) resolves. There was no "built early with stale data" bug — the header just shows nothing at
all for however long that fetch takes. On a slow network/DB that silence reads exactly like "the
filter isn't there", which is what got reported.

**Built (`shared/tableFramework.js`).** Two additive methods alongside the existing
`initColFilters(id, columns, serverValues)`, using the same trigger position/SVG/hover language so
this reads as "the same icon, not ready yet" rather than a different UI element:
- `pendingColFilters(id, columns)` — takes only `{ colIdx: { label } }` (no `valueFn`/`serverValues`
  needed yet) and renders a non-interactive placeholder icon (`.cf-icon.cf-pending`, a slow CSS
  opacity pulse, title "Filter X — loading…") into every matching `<th>` the moment a table renders
  — before its fetch even starts. Safe to call before `PA.tf.init`'s own render and safe to call
  again; no-ops if a real or pending icon already occupies that header.
- `colFiltersFailed(id, columns, reason)` — replaces a pending placeholder with a distinct muted
  `.cf-icon.cf-error` state (title "Filter X unavailable: <reason>") instead of leaving it pulsing
  forever. Leaves an already-real icon alone.
- `initColFilters` itself now calls a new `_cfRemovePlaceholders` first, so the real, interactive
  icon cleanly replaces whichever placeholder was there. Existing synchronous callers that never
  call `pendingColFilters` are unaffected — there is nothing to remove.
- Shared helpers factored out for all three (`_cfEachHeader`, `_cfMakeIcon`, `_cfIconSvg`) so the
  header-walk and icon markup can't drift between the three entry points.
- CSS: `.cf-icon.cf-pending`/`.cf-icon.cf-error` plus a `cf-pulse` keyframe added to all three
  stylesheets that already declare `.cf-icon` (`jar/style.css`, `parser/css/column-filter.css`,
  `plsql/css/style.css`) — kept in the same three places as the existing rule rather than
  centralized, matching how `.cf-icon` itself is already duplicated per page.

**Applied to every screen with a real async gap** (the six named in the investigation, confirmed via
`grep -rl initColFilters`):
- `plsql/js/tableOps.js` — `pendingColFilters` right after the table renders; the existing
  `_initColFiltersAsync`'s try/catch already degrades gracefully (partial `serverValues`) rather
  than failing outright, so no `colFiltersFailed` call was needed there.
- `plsql/js/joins.js`, `parser/js/joins.js` — `pendingColFilters` before their `setTimeout(0)` call
  (a genuine, if short, async gap: the real call still waits a macrotask).
- `plsql/js/search.js` — `pendingColFilters` before the `fetch(.../global-search/summary)` call;
  both a non-ok response and a network failure now route through `colFiltersFailed` instead of the
  old bare `.catch(() => {})` that left nothing in the header at all.
- `parser/js/tableOps.js` — extracted the inline column-def object into `_colDefs()` (removing a
  `setTimeout(0)` race against `_loadSummary`'s own `await`) so `pendingColFilters` runs
  synchronously after render and the real attach or `colFiltersFailed` happens directly from
  `_loadSummary`'s success/catch. Also fixed a real bug found while wiring this up:
  `PA.api.facetSummary` reports a failed request by resolving to `null` (it already calls
  `PA.apiFail` itself), not by throwing — the first pass here handed that `null` straight to
  `initColFilters` as if it were merely "no values yet", which on a server-paged table's checkbox
  columns silently no-ops and would have left the pending placeholder pulsing forever. Fixed by
  checking for a falsy summary explicitly and routing it to `colFiltersFailed`.
- `parser/js/cursors.js` — same `_colDefs()` extraction; `_loadSummary` and `_initColFilters` both
  now call `colFiltersFailed` on a thrown error or a summary with no `columnValues` respectively.

**Tests.** `tests/colfilter-loading-state.test.mjs` — loads the real `shared/tableFramework.js`
(same technique as `tests/lib/tf-golden.mjs`) against a small hand-built DOM (a `matches`/`findAll`
pair supporting `table`/`th`/compound class selectors and `closest`, since the shared `tests/lib/
dom.mjs` stub's `querySelector(All)` always returns empty and can't run `initColFilters`'s header
walk). Four cases: placeholder appears synchronously before any data resolves; the real icon
replaces it once `initColFilters` runs; a failed fetch shows the distinct `cf-error` state (not
silence, not perpetual pulsing); an ordinary synchronous caller that never touches
`pendingColFilters` is unaffected. Updated `tests/tableops-paged.test.mjs`'s
`test_column_filter_values_come_from_the_summary` assertion (`}, cv);` → `_colDefs(), cv);`) to match
the `_colDefs()` extraction in `parser/js/tableOps.js` — a source-shape assertion, not a behavior
change. Full suite (`node tests/run.mjs`, 63 files): 316/317 — the one failure
(`parser-nodeindex-remaining-consumers-lazy.test.mjs`) is the same pre-existing, unrelated
`callGraphViz`/`_showNodeDetail` failure noted in §269, confirmed untouched by this change.

**Rebuild & live verification.** `mvn -pl unified-web -am package -DskipTests` clean; restarted with
this session's exact mongodb JVM args. Against the real `ORACLE~ORACLEDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`
analysis, real Playwright with `page.route()` delaying/failing the relevant summary fetch:
- **Table Operations**, `**/tables/page/summary*` delayed 2.5s: 8 pending (`cf-pending`) icons
  present across all filterable headers the instant the grid rendered (screenshotted); all 8 became
  real, interactive icons once the delayed response landed, 0 pending remaining. Clicked the real
  Schema icon — popover opened with the real value `ANALYZER` (screenshotted), proving it's not just
  visually swapped but genuinely wired to real data.
- **Table Operations**, same endpoint returning a real `500`: all 8 headers showed the `cf-error`
  state instead of reverting to silence or staying stuck pending; icon title read "Filter Schema
  unavailable: request failed" (screenshotted, icons visibly red/muted vs. the grey pending state
  and the normal active state).
- **Global Search** (`plsql/js/search.js`, plsql page, `#globalSearch` input, query "ERP"),
  `**/global-search/summary*` delayed 2.5s: pending icons visible in the results-overlay header
  while "Loading…" rows are still showing (screenshotted); replaced by real icons once 546 real
  results arrived (screenshotted).
- **Global Search**, same endpoint returning `500`: all 4 header columns (Type/Name/Schema/Matched)
  showed the `cf-error` state with title "Filter Type unavailable: no filter values returned"
  (screenshotted, zoomed crop confirms all four are the red error glyph, not the default or pending
  colour).

Not committed (not a git repo).

## §271 — New feature: JAR-side Global Search, mirroring PL/SQL's (§256/§269)

PL/SQL has had a real, server-side, cross-facet Global Search since §256 (further hardened in §269
with per-column `contains`/`regex` filters): `ParserAnalysisController.getSearch`/`getSearchSummary`
normalizing 7 facets into one `{type, name, schema, matchedField, _idx, raw}` row set, paged via the
shared `FacetSpec`/`FacetPageResponder` machinery, rendered by `plsql/js/search.js`. JAR had no
equivalent — `#search-classes` on the Code Structure tab is a same-tab substring filter scoped to
one screen, not a cross-facet search.

**Facets picked, and why.** Read every `@GetMapping`/`@PostMapping` on `AnalyzerController` and its
siblings first, rather than guessing. JAR already reuses PL/SQL's `FacetSpec`/`FacetPageResponder`
directly for two real facets (`JarFacetSpecs.CLASS_TREE`, `.BUNDLED_JARS`) plus a bespoke
`streamSummaryEndpointPage` scan for the endpoint list — those three are the ones with an actual
name/identifier a user would type into a search box, so all three went in:
- **CLASS** — from `AnalysisQuery.Dataset.JAR_CLASS_TREE`; matches fully-qualified name, simple
  name (→ `matchedField:"name"`) or package name (→ `"content"`).
- **DEPENDENCY** — from `AnalysisQuery.Dataset.JAR_BUNDLED_JARS`; matches the JAR file name.
- **ENDPOINT** — via the existing `AbstractAnalysisDataProvider.streamSummaryEndpointPage`, called
  with the search query itself so the (already-written) `fullPath`/`httpMethod`/
  `controllerSimpleName`/`controllerClass`/`methodName` matching happens once, not reimplemented.

Methods were **not** added as a separate facet: `JAR_CLASS_TREE`'s own projection (`classRow`)
deliberately drops `methodSummaries` (93.8% of the tree's payload, §118/§134) specifically because
nothing reads it server-side either — adding a method facet here would mean re-fetching exactly the
field the class tree was paged to stop sending.

**Backend.** `JarFacetSpecs.SEARCH` (new `FacetSpec`, `unified-web/.../jaranalyzer/controller/
JarFacetSpecs.java`) is a deliberate line-for-line port of `ParserFacetSpecs.SEARCH` — same `cf`
column contract (`"0"`=type, `"1"`=schema, both checkbox; `"2"`=name, `"3"`=matchedField, both
text/contains/regex), same normalized-row-only `searchText:null`. Two new endpoints on
`AnalyzerController`:
- `GET /api/jar/jars/{id}/global-search?q=&limit=&after=&sort=&cf=` → the standard page envelope.
- `GET /api/jar/jars/{id}/global-search/summary?q=` → `{columnValues: {"0":[...types],
  "1":[...schemas]}}` for the checkbox columns' popovers.

Both build their row set via a new private `buildSearchRows(id, version, q)`, which scans the three
facets above and merges them — any one facet failing (e.g. an older analysis with no
`bundled-jars.json`) is swallowed so the other two still answer, mirroring
`ParserAnalysisController.buildSearchRows`'s own per-facet "skip, don't fail". The merged
`ArrayNode` is hand to `facets.respond`/`facets.summary` with `JarFacetSpecs.SEARCH` exactly the way
`getClassTree`/`getCollectionCallPaths` already hand their own rows to `respondStreaming` — no new
pagination code, `cf`'s contains/regex/case-sensitive modes come for free from the same
`FacetPageResponder` §269 already hardened.

**Frontend.** `jar/js/search.js` — a namespace-only port of `plsql/js/search.js` (`JA.search` instead
of `PA.search`, `JA.app.currentJarId` instead of `PA.api._parserName()`), reusing the same shared
`PA.tf`/`PA.pageSource` framework (`shared/tableFramework.js`) JAR's own `endpointList.js` and
`codeTree.js` already call `.init()` on — confirmed by reading those files, not assumed compatible.
Same overlay panel, same Type/Name/Schema/Matched columns, same column-index-vs-`cf`-index mismatch
guard the PL/SQL file's own doc comment warns about. `openRow` jumps CLASS results into the Code
Structure search box (`#search-classes`/`filterTree()`) and ENDPOINT results into the endpoint
list's own filter; DEPENDENCY has no dedicated screen today, so it just closes the overlay (its own
row already showed everything Global Search has for it). Wired into `jar/index.html` as
`#globalSearch`, placed in the sidebar directly under the Upload/Targeted buttons (this app has no
top-bar-actions strip the way `plsql/index.html` does — the sidebar is the natural, and only,
persistent chrome on every screen).

**A real, pre-existing bug found and fixed along the way.** `jar/style.css`'s `.cf-popover` had
`z-index: 1000` — fine for every other screen, where the popover only has to sit above the plain
page, but Global Search's own overlay (`#searchOverlay`, `z-index: 9000`, same value PL/SQL's uses)
sits far above it. Every popover opened for a Global Search column filter rendered *behind* the
overlay's own table, so a click that visually looked like it landed on a radio button or "Apply"
actually landed on the table underneath and closed the popover instead — caught by real Playwright
interaction (a `.click()` that silently did nothing, then a `regex` filter that produced 0 rows
where 1 was expected), not by inspection. Fixed by raising `.cf-popover` to `z-index: 9999`,
matching `plsql/css/style.css`'s own value for the identical reason. This bug pre-dates this task —
it was latent in every other screen that opens a `.cf-popover` inside a `z-index:1000+` layer — but
was undiscovered until Global Search's own overlay (the first `z-index:9000` layer on this page to
host a column filter) exposed it live.

**Tests.** `AnalyzerControllerGlobalSearchTest` (`unified-web/src/test/java/com/jaranalyzer/
controller/`), same reflection-over-constructor pattern as `AnalyzerControllerClassPackagesTest`
(mock every dependency except `ObjectMapper`/`AnalysisRepository`, real `FacetPageResponder`): merges
CLASS + DEPENDENCY rows from a stubbed `repository.rows(...)` into one normalized set, rejects a
blank `q` with 400, and confirms `global-search/summary`'s `columnValues["0"]` includes `"CLASS"`.
Endpoints are not exercised in this unit test — they need a real backing document via
`AnalysisDataProvider`, not a repository stub, and the endpoint scan's own try/catch (confirmed by
these same tests returning 200 with only CLASS/DEPENDENCY rows against a bare-mock
`providerFactory`) is what makes that safe to omit here. 3/3 pass.

**Rebuild & live verification.** `mvn -pl unified-web -am package -DskipTests`; restarted with this
session's exact mongodb JVM args. No JAR analysis existed yet (`GET /api/jar/jars` → `[]`) — analyzed
this very repo's own build artifact, `unified-web/target/unified-web-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` (86.5 MB),
via `POST /api/jar/jars`; completed in the background to `unified-web-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT` — 1,691
classes, 359 endpoints, real data, not a fixture.

`curl` against the real analysis: `q=Controller` → 425 total matches spanning CLASS and ENDPOINT
rows; page 2 (via the real `nextCursor`) showed genuinely different rows than page 1; `cf=0:ENDPOINT`
→ 357 (ENDPOINT-only); `cf=2:contains:Chat` → 2 (`ChatController`, `ChatboxController`);
`cf=2:regex:^com\.analyzer\.chat\..*` (case-sensitive) → 1 (`ChatController`) — column filters
confirmed working before touching the browser at all.

Real Playwright against the live UI (`jar/index.html`, `#globalSearch` input, query "Controller"):
results overlay opened with 425 items across CLASS/ENDPOINT rows (screenshotted); `PA.tf.goPage`
to page 2 showed different rows than page 1 (confirmed by content diff, not just a page-number
change); the Type column's checkbox popover, clicked live, narrowed the grid to ENDPOINT-only rows;
the Name column's popover, in `contains` mode with value "Chat", narrowed to 15 rows; in `regex`
mode with `^com\.analyzer\.chat\..*` and case-sensitive checked, narrowed to exactly 1 row
(`com.analyzer.chat.ChatController`) — this last one is what caught the `.cf-popover` z-index bug
above: it failed (0 rows, radio click silently doing nothing) until that CSS fix, then passed.
Screenshots captured at every stage (multi-type results, page 2, the Type popover, the
ENDPOINT-only filtered grid, the contains filter, the regex filter).

Not committed (not a git repo).

## §272 — Four live UI fixes: Summary-tab pager, Global Search overlay theming (JAR + PL/SQL), search title JAR scope, JAR Export FAB

Four concrete UI problems reported against the live app, fixed and Playwright-verified against the
real `unified-web-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT` JAR analysis (1,691 classes, 359 endpoints) — no new analysis
created.

**Problem 1 — Summary tab pagers rendered with zero visible styling.** Every Summary sub-table
(Endpoint Report, Collection Analysis, External Dependencies, Distributed Transactions, Batch Jobs,
Scheduled Jobs, Aggregation Flows, Dynamic Flows, Verticalisation, Claude Insights, Claude
Corrections — all ~11 built on `shared/tableFramework.js`'s `PA.tf._renderPager`) showed page-number
buttons crammed together with no border/background/hover/active state. Root cause, found by
inspecting the live DOM rather than guessing from the CSS: `jar/style.css` already had a fully
fleshed-out `.sum-pager-btn` rule (border, hover, `.active` fill), but `PA.tf._renderPager`'s actual
markup never uses that class — it renders plain `<button>` tags inside a `.page-btns` wrapper, and
the container itself carries class `sum-pager` (set by each summary table's own HTML), not
`.sum-pager-btn` on the buttons. A second, unrelated `.pagination-bar .page-btns button` rule (added
in an earlier session for `endpointList.js`'s pager) also didn't match, because that pager's
container is `.pagination-bar`, not `.sum-pager` — so neither existing rule ever reached these ~11
tables' buttons; they rendered as bare unstyled `<button>`s.

Fix: added `.sum-pager .page-btns button` (and `.page-info`/`.page-size select`) rules to
`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/style.css`, reusing the exact same treatment as
`.pagination-bar`'s (border/radius/background from `--border`/`--radius-sm`/`--bg`, hover and
`.active` fill from `--accent`/`--text-inverse`) rather than inventing new colors — since the
container class is shared by all ~11 sub-tables, one rule fixes all of them at once. The old
`.sum-pager-btn` rules are left in place (harmless, unused) rather than deleted, since removing dead
CSS was out of scope for this fix.

**Problem 2 — JAR Global Search overlay unstyled (and, on closer look, PL/SQL's own overlay too).**
The task's original framing treated `plsql/js/search.js`'s overlay as "the reference for done
right" — live testing during this session disproved that: PL/SQL's own overlay had the identical
gap. Root cause, same shape as Problem 1: both `jar/js/search.js` and `plsql/js/search.js` build
their results grid with `<table class="to-table">` and Type-column badges with
`<span class="lp-type-badge">`, and their pager container is `<div id="srch-pager" class="pager">`
— a THIRD pager class distinct from both `.sum-pager` and `.pagination-bar`. `jar/style.css` never
defined `.to-table` at all (only `plsql/css/style.css` had it, for its own unrelated tables), so the
JAR overlay's grid had no header background, no row borders, no zebra/hover. Neither stylesheet
defined `.pager`, so both overlays' pagers were unstyled regardless of Problem 1's fix. And neither
`_renderRow` ever added a type-specific modifier class to `.lp-type-badge` (e.g. `CLASS`/`TABLE`),
so even where `.lp-type-badge`'s base rule existed (plsql only) it had no background/color — the
Type column rendered as plain text either way.

Fix, in both stylesheets, all reusing existing shared theme variables (`--border`, `--bg-hover`,
`--accent`, `--radius*`, `--badge-*-bg`/`--badge-*`) — no new colors invented:
- `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/style.css` — added `.to-table` (ported from
  `plsql/css/style.css`, which already had it), `.lp-type-badge` base rule plus
  `CLASS`/`ENDPOINT`/`DEPENDENCY` color variants, `.pager`/`.page-btns button` pagination rules
  (same treatment as `.sum-pager`/`.pagination-bar`), and `#srchContainer tr.lp-item` row-hover
  rules.
- `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/plsql/css/style.css` — added the same `.pager`/
  `.page-btns button` pagination rules, `TABLE`/`PROCEDURE`/`SEQUENCE`/`CURSOR`/`JOIN`/
  `DYNAMIC_SQL`/`PREDICATE` color variants for `.lp-type-badge` (its existing base rule already
  covered size/padding, it was missing these facet colors), and scoped `#srchContainer tr.lp-item`
  back to `display: table-row` — the sidebar's own `.lp-item` rule (a flex row, for a different,
  pre-existing use) would otherwise break the search grid's `<tr>` layout by giving it
  `display: flex`.
- `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/search.js` and
  `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/plsql/js/search.js` — `_renderRow` now emits
  `class="lp-type-badge ${type}"` instead of the bare class, so the new color variants actually
  apply.

Column-filter popovers (`.cf-*`, the contains/regex/case-sensitive UI) needed no new CSS in either
file — both stylesheets already had a complete, correctly-themed `.cf-popover`/`.cf-header`/
`.cf-item`/`.cf-apply`/`.cf-cancel` set from earlier sessions (§256/§271); confirmed live rather than
assumed.

**Problem 3 — Global Search overlay title missing JAR scope.** `jar/js/search.js`'s overlay title

the raw id), appending `.jar` if the resolved name doesn't already end in it, and writes it into a

## §273 — History "Load" false 404 error banner, root-caused and fixed for real

Followed up on the bug flagged (not fixed) at the end of §272: clicking "Load" on a PL/SQL History
entry could show a red "A request returned 404 (nothing loaded)" banner
(`/api/parser/analyses/{name}/node/{id}`) at the top of the page while the rest of the screen —
including a subsequently-opened Global Search overlay — showed real, correct data. Reproduced live
first, with real Playwright network/console capture, before touching any code.

**Root cause — not stale cross-session state.** The bug reproduces on the *very first* History
"Load" of a session, on any of the five dialect demo analyses tried (Postgres, SQL Server, Db2,
MySQL, Oracle) — ruling out the "stale node id left over from a previously-loaded analysis"
hypothesis from the task brief. The real cause: `PA.autoSelectEntryProc`
(`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/plsql/js/app.js`) and `loadSidebarData`'s own equivalent
loop deliberately probe several *candidate* node ids in sequence — `SCHEMA.OBJ.PROC`, `SCHEMA.OBJ`,
`OBJ` — since the analysis metadata alone doesn't say which of those the parser actually used as the
node id. Each candidate is a `GET .../node/{candidate}` through `PA.api.getProcDetail`, wrapped in
its own `try/catch`; a 404 for a wrong candidate is expected, silently-handled control flow — the
loop just moves on to the next one. But `getProcDetail` (`plsql/js/api.js`) called the *shared*
`PA.apiFail(res)` helper unconditionally on any non-OK response. `apiFail` (`shared/page-envelope.js`)
exists specifically to make otherwise-silent failures visible by raising a throttled, page-wide
banner — appropriate for a call site that has no other way to signal failure, wrong for a call site
that already handles the failure itself one line later. Every wrong candidate in the probe loop
therefore raised the global banner, even on an analysis that went on to auto-select correctly a
moment afterward — explaining the "error banner sitting next to a screen full of real data"
symptom exactly.

**Fix.** Threaded a `{ silentOn404: true }` option through `PA.api.getProcDetail(procName, opts)`:
on a 404 with that flag set, it skips `PA.apiFail` (any other status, or any call site that omits
the flag, still raises the banner as before — this is not a blanket suppression). Set the flag at
all three genuinely-probing call sites: `autoSelectEntryProc`'s `rootId` probe and its
`schema.obj.proc`/`schema.obj`/`obj` candidate loop, and `loadSidebarData`'s identical candidate
loop. Non-probing callers (`showProcedure`, the summary tabs' single definite-id lookups) were left
untouched and still surface a real 404 as a banner.

**Tests.** No existing test in `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/tests/run.mjs` covered this
flow, so added `plsql-autoselect-silent-404.test.mjs` (static-source assertions, matching this
codebase's own established pattern for app.js/api.js call-site checks, e.g.
`parser-resolve-detail-file.test.mjs`): `getProcDetail` accepts and honors the option; every
`getProcDetail(...)` call inside `autoSelectEntryProc`'s body carries `silentOn404: true`;
`loadSidebarData`'s own candidate-loop call does too. 3/3 pass; full suite otherwise unchanged
(319 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure in `parser-nodeindex-remaining-consumers-lazy.test.mjs`,
about `callGraphViz`'s click handler — untouched by this change, confirmed pre-existing).

**Rebuild & live verification.** `mvn -pl unified-web -am package -DskipTests`; killed port 8083,
restarted with this session's exact mongodb JVM args. Real Playwright, before and after:
- Before (unmodified server, captured for the record): loading
  `POSTGRES~POSTGRESDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` fired `console.warn('[api] request failed', 404, …
  /node/ERP.ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE)` and `.../node/ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`, and the `#api-fail-banner` element
  appeared (banner count 1) — confirmed the exact failing URL from the task brief.
- After the fix: loaded all five dialect demo History entries individually
  (Postgres/SQL Server/Db2/MySQL/Oracle `…ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`/`USP_RUNMRPCYCLE`) — `#api-fail-banner`
  never appeared for any of them (banner visible: false ×5), even though the same underlying 404s
  still occur (expected, and now silent — confirmed via network capture, same URLs, same 404
  statuses, no console warning). Then bounced directly from the Postgres entry to the SQL Server
  entry with no "Home" step in between, the way a real user flips between History rows — no banner,
  screenshotted (`after-fix-bounce.png`): topbar correctly shows `ERP.USP_RUNMRPCYCLE`, 55 procs,
  84 tables, real procedure list in the left panel.
- Honesty note: the auto-select still doesn't land on a specific procedure for these five demo
  analyses (the Explore panel shows "Select a procedure from the left panel" rather than a
  pre-selected one) — none of the three candidate ids it tries match these particular demo
  analyses' real node id format. That is a separate, lower-severity cosmetic gap (probably the
  parser's actual node ids don't follow the assumed `schema.obj.proc` shape for these connectors);
  it was true before this fix too, is not what the task described, and was left alone rather than
  silently gold-plated in scope creep. The reported bug — the false top-of-page error banner — is
  fixed and verified.

Not committed (not a git repo).

## §275 — Top-right Export+Log FAB cluster: hardcoded per-page `top` pixel guesses (§274) replaced with a runtime-measured `--fab-top-offset`

§274 pinned `.global-export-fab`/`.log-fab` to a static `top` pixel value per page (parser
`ui-polish.css`: 54px, `jar/style.css`: 120px, `plsql/css/style.css`: 40px), each tuned against
whatever procedure happened to be loaded during that session's live-testing. Both the `.topbar`
action row and, on parser/plsql, the `.detail-header` badge row (built by
`parser/js/detailHeader.js` / plsql's equivalent) are full-width with zero free space at the right
edge (confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect()` — there is no just-move-it-sideways fix), and their
height varies with the loaded procedure's name/schema/file-path/line-range length. A static guess is
therefore wrong for any procedure whose header wraps to more lines than the one it was tuned on.

**Fix — measure the real DOM at runtime instead of guessing.** New
`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/shared/floating-fab-position.js`:
- On `DOMContentLoaded`, debounced `window resize`, and a `MutationObserver` on `document.body`
  (`childList`/`subtree`/`attributes` on `style`/`class`) — the observer is the mechanism that
  reacts to procedure switches, since none of the three SPAs (parser/jar/plsql) fire a dedicated
  route-change custom event; `jar/js/app.js`'s only navigation hook is a plain `popstate` listener
  plus direct DOM mutation from render calls, so observing the DOM directly is the one hook that
  works uniformly across all three without inventing a new lifecycle event.
- Measures `getBoundingClientRect().bottom` of whichever of `.topbar` / `.content-top-bar` (JAR's
  own topbar class) / `.detail-header` (parser/plsql) / `.analysis-header` (JAR) / `.sum-topbar`
  (JAR's Summary-tab inline export bar) actually exist and are visible on the current page, takes
  the max, and sets `document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--fab-top-offset', Math.max(bottom
  + 8, 48) + 'px')`.
- Defensive: wrapped in try/catch; if no candidate element is found (home screen, before an
  analysis loads) the property is left unset and the CSS fallback value applies — never throws,
  never forces a wrong value.

**CSS changed to consume the variable** (fallback = each file's previous hardcoded value, so
behavior before the script's first paint, or on a screen with no header, is unchanged from §274):
- `shared/mongodb-theme.css` — `.global-export-fab`: `top: 60px` → `top: var(--fab-top-offset,
  60px)`.
- `shared/log-fab.css` — `.log-fab`: `top: 60px` → `top: var(--fab-top-offset, 60px)`.
- `parser/css/ui-polish.css` — `.log-fab`/`.global-export-fab`: `top: 54px !important` → `top:
  var(--fab-top-offset, 54px) !important`.
- `jar/style.css` — `.log-fab`/`.global-export-fab`: `top: 120px !important` → `top:
  var(--fab-top-offset, 120px) !important`.
- `plsql/css/style.css` — `.log-fab`/`.global-export-fab`: `top: 40px !important` → `top:
  var(--fab-top-offset, 40px) !important`.

**Wired in** via a new `<script src="../shared/floating-fab-position.js">` tag (immediately after
each page's existing `../shared/log-fab.js` include) on `parser/index.html`, `jar/index.html`, and
`plsql/index.html`.

**Rebuild & live verification.** `mvn -pl unified-web -am package -DskipTests`; killed port 8083,
restarted with this session's exact mongodb JVM args. Real Playwright (from
`/tmp/claude-502/browser/node_modules`, no mocks) against the live app, hash-routing directly to
`parser/index.html#/analysis/POSTGRES~POSTGRESDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE/proc/{nodeId}` for three
procedures of deliberately different name/line-range length — `ERP.erp_usp_ping` (short, L1-13),
`ERP.ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` (the entry point, L1-264), `ERP.erp_usp_compute_net_requirements` (long,
L1-257) — at viewport widths 1280, 1600, and 1999. For every one of the 9 combinations: computed
`getBoundingClientRect()` for `.topbar`, `.detail-header`, `.global-export-fab`, `.log-fab` and a
real rectangle-intersection test (not eyeballing) between the FAB rects and both header rects —
**zero overlap in all 9 cases**. Confirmed the procedures actually differed (`dhFullName`/`dhMeta`
text and line ranges checked per case, e.g. `L1-13` vs `L1-264` vs `L1-257`) rather than the route
silently no-op'ing. Logged `--fab-top-offset` per case: 239.59375px at 1280w, 238.59375px at 1600w,
206.59375px at 1999w (identical across the three procedures at a given width in this run — the
`.detail-header`'s badge row wraps to the same number of lines for all three names at these
widths, so its height, and therefore the offset, doesn't change; the mechanism is still driven by
the live measurement each time, not a hardcoded value — a name long enough to wrap an extra line
would produce a different offset, which the debounced resize/MutationObserver path re-measures for).
Screenshots saved under the session scratchpad
(`parser_{short,entry-medium,long}_w{1280,1600,1999}.png`) confirm the Export pill and Log FAB
sitting cleanly below the topbar/badge rows at every width. Spot-checked JAR (loaded the existing
`unified-web-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT` JAR analysis) — `--fab-top-offset` computed as 241px, zero overlap
with `.content-top-bar`/`.analysis-header`. Spot-checked PL/SQL's home screen (no PL/SQL analysis
was present in this MongoDB instance's history to load a procedure from — `/api/plsql/analysis/history`
returned `[]`) — no header container present, so the script left the property unset and the
existing 40px CSS fallback applied correctly, with no overlap since no content is present that low
on that screen; the mechanism itself was already exercised on parser using the identical
`.detail-header` markup PL/SQL shares.

**Known edge case not covered by live data in this pass:** a procedure name long enough to wrap
`.detail-header`'s badge row (`.dh-meta`) onto an extra line was not naturally present in the
`ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` demo dataset at the tested widths, so the "taller header → larger measured
offset" branch of the fix was exercised by the code path (the script re-measures on every DOM
mutation, and did produce different offsets across the three tested viewport widths, confirming the
measurement is live rather than cached) but not by a single procedure whose own name pushed the
header height higher than another procedure's at the same width. The mechanism itself has no such
gap — `getBoundingClientRect().bottom` is taken fresh on every MutationObserver callback — but it
is flagged here rather than silently claimed as fully exercised.

**Files changed:**
- New: `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/shared/floating-fab-position.js`
- `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/shared/mongodb-theme.css`
