## §276 — Summary "External Dependencies" always empty despite a real, nonzero "95 Cross-Module" stat — root-caused (a front-end identity-join bug, not the server field-stripping first suspected) and fixed

**Symptom.** JAR Summary tab's External Dependencies sub-tab always rendered "No cross-module
dependencies detected", even though the stat card directly above it correctly showed "95
Cross-Module" (`unified-web-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT`, real analysis, 359 endpoints).

**Initial hypothesis, investigated and ruled out.** The task brief this session started from
suspected `AbstractAnalysisDataProvider.HEADERS_SKIP_FIELDS` stripping `externalCalls` from
`/summary/endpoints`'s lightweight payload as the root cause. Live curl against the running server
disproved this: `/summary/reports` already returns a fully-populated, real `extReport.crossModule`
(3 modules, 95 endpoints total, real class/method/breadcrumb data) computed server-side by
`EndpointCrossReportBuilder`, and a dedicated `/summary/external-calls` slice endpoint already
returns every endpoint's real `externalCalls` array. Both of these were already wired into
`jar/js/summary.js`'s `_render`/`_ensureSliceLoaded`/`_mergeSliceData` — the server-side aggregate
endpoint the brief proposed building already existed and already worked.

**Actual root cause, found by executing the client code under Playwright, not by reading it.**
`JA.summary._mergeSliceData` (`jar/js/summary.js`), on the `externalCalls` slice arriving, correctly
joins the slice onto `this._analysis.endpoints` by identity key (`JA.utils.endpointKey`) and sets
real `externalCalls`/`httpCalls` there — but it then tried to copy that data onto `_epReports` (the
rows `/summary/reports` returns, used to build `_extReport`) by reading `r.endpoint.externalCalls`,
assuming `r.endpoint` was the *same object* as the just-mutated `analysis.endpoints[i]`. It never
was: `_epReports` and `analysis.endpoints` are two independently JSON-parsed object graphs from two
separate fetches, so `r.endpoint` is always a distinct, never-mutated copy — and a stripped-down one
at that (only `controllerClass`/`methodName`; no `httpMethod`/`fullPath`/`endpointId`), so even a
correct-looking key built from it alone would still be wrong. Confirmed live in the browser:
`JA.summary._epReports[0].endpoint === JA.summary._analysis.endpoints[0]` is `false`, and
`_epReports[0].externalScopeCalls` stayed `0` even after `_loadedSlices.externalCalls` was `true`
and the real slice fetch had completed successfully.

**Fix** (`unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary.js`, `_mergeSliceData`): for each
report row `r`, reconstruct the same composite key `JA.utils.endpointKey` falls back to
(`httpMethod + ' ' + fullPath + ' ' + controllerClass + '#' + methodName`, since this analysis has
no `endpointId` field) from `r`'s own top-level `httpMethod`/`fullPath` plus `r.endpoint`'s
`controllerClass`/`methodName`, and look the real, already-mutated `ep` up in `byKey` — the exact
map the slice-merge loop just above already built. No server-side change was needed or made; the
brief's proposed new endpoint was not built because the data it would have served already existed
and was already reaching the client correctly — only the client-side join was broken.

**Tests.** New `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/tests/mergeslicedata-externalcalls.test.mjs`
(2 cases), following this codebase's existing convention (`revive-sets.test.mjs`) of loading and
executing the real `jar/js/utils.js` + `jar/js/summary.js` via `new Function(...)`, not a source-text
check. Builds two genuinely separate object graphs for `_epReports` vs `_analysis.endpoints` (same
shape as the real two-fetch case) and asserts the join finds the right row by identity even though
no object reference is shared, and that an endpoint absent from the slice is left untouched. Both
pass; full suite otherwise unchanged (321 passed / 1 pre-existing, unrelated failure in
`parser-nodeindex-remaining-consumers-lazy.test.mjs`, not touched this session).

**Rebuild & live verification.** JS-only change: `python3 scripts/stamp-assets.py` (asset already
current — `summary.js?v=1789226308`), then `mvn -pl unified-web -am package -DskipTests` (no
`jar-analyzer-core` change was needed — this bug was never in
`AbstractAnalysisDataProvider`). Killed port 8083, restarted with this session's exact MongoDB JVM
args. Real Playwright (from `/tmp/claude-502/browser/node_modules`, no mocks) against the live
`unified-web-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT` analysis:
- **Before** (`/tmp/claude-502/browser/verify_extdeps_tab.png`): "95 Cross-Module" stat visible,
  External Dependencies tab body reads "No cross-module dependencies detected".
- **After** (`/tmp/claude-502/browser/s278_after_extdeps.png`): same "95 Cross-Module" stat, tab now
  renders "CROSS-MODULE (3 MODULES)" with a real, sortable/filterable table — Plsql Parser (9
  classes, 32 endpoints, 1681 calls), Plsql Config (13 classes, 54 endpoints, 1233 calls), Plsql
  Analyzer Core (4 classes, 68 endpoints, 510 calls), each with real method names
  (`OracleDictionaryService.getRecursiveDependencies`, `PlsqlConfig.resolveEnvironment`, etc.).
- In-page state dump confirmed the mechanism directly:
  `JA.summary._extReport.crossModule.length === 3` (was effectively empty before, since
  `_buildExternalDeps`/the server `extReport` was being fed all-zero `externalScopeCalls` rows on
  the stale join path) and the "95 Cross-Module" chip unchanged at 95 across both runs.

**Files changed:**
- `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/js/summary.js` (`_mergeSliceData`'s `externalCalls`
  branch — identity join fixed)
- New: `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/tests/mergeslicedata-externalcalls.test.mjs`
- `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/jar/index.html` (asset stamp, already current — no visible
  diff since the mtime-derived version was unchanged across the edit+stamp sequence in this run)

Not committed (not a git repo).

## §278 — Color audit: Parser Export modal painting its entire body with a saturated `var(--blue)` gradient, plus an unscoped `.src-modal-header` override leaking that same wash into the real Source View modal's header

**Symptom.** `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/parser/css/export.css` filled the whole Export
modal body with `linear-gradient(160deg, var(--blue) 0%, var(--blue) 60%, var(--sidebar-bg) 100%)`
— a big saturated-surface fill, directly against `shared/mongodb-theme.css`'s rule that
`--blue`/`--accent`/status colors are for small elements (badges, buttons, icons) only, never a
background wash. Worse, the same file's `.src-modal-header` rule was unscoped (no parent selector),
so it also silently overrode the real Source View modal's own calm `var(--bg)` header
(`source-view.css`) with a solid `--accent-hover` bar — confirmed live in both cases (Export modal
open, and separately Source View modal open) before touching anything.

**Fix.** Flattened `.export-modal` to the same `var(--bg-card)` + `1px solid var(--border)` card
surface every other modal in this app uses; re-scoped the header/title/close rules to
`.export-modal .src-modal-header` / `.export-modal .src-modal-title` / `.export-modal
.src-modal-close` so they can never again apply outside this one modal. Source View's own header
rule in `source-view.css` was left untouched and now renders correctly again. Also flattened
`.export-format .btn.active`'s one-off gradient to the same flat `var(--accent)` fill
`.btn-primary` already uses elsewhere (`plsql/css/style.css:1371` uses no gradient either, so this
was purely a leftover one-off).

**Live verification.** Rebuilt, restarted on 8083, opened both modals in both themes on the Parser
app (`POSTGRES~POSTGRESDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE`): Export modal now shows a plain card, no
saturated fill; Source View modal's header is back to its own calm `var(--bg)` style, unaffected by
Export modal's CSS. Not committed (not a git repo).

## §279 — Color audit: shared chat panel header (`.cbx-header`, `shared/chatbox.css`) painting its full width with a saturated `--accent`→`--accent-hover` gradient bar

**Symptom.** The chat/chatbox panel — which opens from every page in all three apps (JAR, PL/SQL,
Parser all load `../shared/chatbox.css`) — had a full-width solid gradient header, the same
"big saturated surface" pattern flagged in §278, just with `--accent` instead of `--blue`.

**Fix.** Flattened `.cbx-header` to the same calm `var(--bg-card)` + `1px solid var(--border)`
bottom-border header every other modal in this app uses, keeping `--accent` only on the small
`.cbx-header-icon`. Title/icon-button colors switched from `--text-inverse` (needed when sitting on
a solid saturated fill) to normal `--text`/`--text-muted` tones now that there's no fill underneath.

**Live verification.** Rebuilt, restarted on 8083, opened the chat panel from JAR, PL/SQL, and
Parser (shared CSS — checked on all three per the design-system rule, not assumed from one app),
both light and dark theme: header is now a plain card in all six combinations, no gradient bar.
Not committed (not a git repo).

## §281 — New feature: draggable resize handle for every real split-panel layout (JAR, Parser, PL/SQL), one shared mechanism, `localStorage`-persisted, interoperating with the existing sidebar-collapse feature

**Scope found.** Grepped every `.css`/`.html` under `static/**` for fixed-width-next-to-flex-sibling
patterns rather than assuming the two "obvious" splits were the only ones. Four real split-panel
layouts exist:
  - `jar/index.html`: `<aside class="sidebar">` (280px fixed) next to `<main class="content">`
    (flex:1), inside `.app`.
  - `parser/index.html` and `plsql/index.html` (identical markup): `<div class="left-panel"
    id="leftPanel">` (280px fixed) next to `<div class="right-panel">` (flex:1), both inside
    `.analysis-layout`.
  - `jar/index.html`'s Code Structure tab: `<div class="code-split-left">` (40%, min 280px) next to
    `<div class="code-split-right" id="code-panel">` (flex:1, min 200px), inside
    `.code-split-container`.
  - Also found but **not wired**: `jar/js/cross-ref.js`'s `.cr-split-left`/`.cr-split-right` (Cross
    Reference modal's two-pane browse view). These panels are built via template-string `innerHTML`
    and re-rendered on every open, which the static `install()` calls below don't reach without
    re-invoking per render — left as a known gap rather than rushed in; see "Not done" below.

**Mechanism.** One new pair of files, not three one-off implementations:
  - `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/shared/resizable-panel.js` — exposes
    `window.MdbResizablePanel = { clamp, keyFor, install }` (same public-API pattern as
    `MdbTheme`/`MdbInlineFab`). `install({panelSelector, panelId, page, min, max})` finds the panel,
    restores any saved width, inserts a `.mdb-resize-handle` sibling right after it, and wires
    mousedown/mousemove/mouseup to resize the panel live and persist on mouseup. `autoInit()` calls
    `install()` once per known selector; missing selectors (e.g. `.code-split-left` when that tab
    isn't the current page) are silently skipped via a `querySelector` null-check.
  - `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/shared/resizable-panel.css` — the handle itself: 5px
    wide, `cursor: col-resize`, transparent at rest, a `var(--bg-hover)` tint on hover/active (no new
    color introduced, per the design-system's calm-palette rule), plus a
    `.mdb-resize-dragging { transition: none !important; }` class toggled only during an active drag
    (see bug below).
  - Wired into `jar/index.html`, `parser/index.html`, `plsql/index.html` immediately after the
    existing `shared/sidebar-toggle.css`/`.js` `<link>`/`<script>` pair.

**Persistence.** `mdb-panel-width:<page>:<panelId>` in `localStorage` — `<page>` defaults to the
first URL path segment (`jar`/`parser`/`plsql`), exactly mirroring `sidebar-toggle.js`'s own
`mdb-sidebar-collapsed:<page>` key shape and its try/catch-around-storage-calls pattern (private
mode / storage disabled degrades to "just don't persist", not a crash). Written once, on mouseup,
not on every mousemove.

**Bounds.** `min: 180`, `max: 50% of viewport width` for both sidebar-type panels (`.sidebar`,
`.left-panel`); the code-structure split uses `min: 220`, `max: 60% of viewport width` since its
right pane needs more headroom. A stale/tampered saved value outside current bounds is clamped on
restore, not applied verbatim (covered by a test — see below).

**Interaction with the existing sidebar-collapse feature (`shared/sidebar-toggle.js`, built
earlier this session).** Read that file first, as instructed, before adding anything on top of it.
Its collapse mechanic is a CSS class (`.sidebar-collapsed`) forcing `width:0 !important` — it
doesn't touch inline styles, so this feature's inline `style.width`/`style.minWidth` survive a
collapse/expand cycle untouched and the panel reappears at the user's last dragged size, not the
CSS default, when re-expanded. Conversely, a handle stays present and visible even while its panel
is collapsed (it's a sibling, not a child); mousedown on it while collapsed does **not** start a
drag (dragging a 0-width panel has no sensible meaning) — it instead clicks the existing
`.sidebar-toggle-btn` to re-expand, reusing that button's own logic rather than duplicating it.

**Real bug found and fixed during live verification.** The panel elements already carry
`transition: width 0.25s ease` (from `sidebar-toggle.css`, for the collapse animation), and that
transition also fires on *any* inline `style.width` change — including ours. First live drag test
showed `getBoundingClientRect().width` reporting `290` moments after setting `style.width = '380px'`
mid-drag: the rect read landed mid-transition, not at the just-applied target, so mouseup was
persisting a stale in-between value instead of the real drop position. Fixed two ways: (1) track the
last-applied clamped width in a JS variable (`lastWidth`) and use *that* for both `startWidth` on
mousedown and the persisted value on mouseup, instead of ever reading the animated rect; (2) added
`.mdb-resize-dragging { transition: none !important; }`, toggled on the panel only while a drag is
in progress, so the drag itself tracks the cursor 1:1 instead of visibly lagging behind it.

**Tests.** `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/tests/resizable-panel.test.mjs` — 8 cases, all
passing: `clamp` bounds, the `mdb-panel-width:<page>:<panelId>` key format, handle insertion,
drag-by-exact-mouse-delta (including clamping past both the min and the 50%-viewport max),
mouseup-persists-final-width-to-localStorage, saved-width-restored-on-load,
out-of-range-saved-width-clamped-on-restore, and mousedown-on-a-collapsed-panel-does-not-start-a-
drag. Since the shared `tests/lib/dom.mjs` stub's `querySelector` always returns `null` (fine for
the render-only modules it was built for, not enough for a module whose whole surface is
"find-by-selector then track document-level mouse events"), this test file brings its own small
fake DOM rather than stretching the shared one to fit a shape it wasn't designed for — loads the
real source via the same `new Function(source)()` pattern `tests/node-index.test.mjs` already uses.
`node tests/run.mjs`: 329 passed, 1 failed (`parser-nodeindex-remaining-consumers-lazy.test.mjs` —
confirmed pre-existing, file untouched by this change, last modified before this session's work).

**Live verification.** `python3 scripts/stamp-assets.py`, `mvn -pl unified-web -am package
-DskipTests`, killed port 8083, restarted with this session's exact MongoDB JVM args, confirmed
`curl http://localhost:8083/jar/index.html` → `200`. Real Playwright drag (mousedown + 5 stepped
mousemoves totalling +100px + mouseup, not a CSS/attribute check) on all three apps, both themes,
using the real analysis `POSTGRES~POSTGRESDEMO~LOCAL~ERP_USP_RUN_CYCLE` for Parser/PL-SQL (navigated
via `#/analysis/<name>` so the `.analysis-layout` split — hidden behind the home screen until an
analysis is open — is actually present to drag), plus JAR's `unified-web-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT`:

| app | theme | before | after drag (+100px) | after reload | collapse→expand |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| jar | light | 280.0px | 380.0px | 380.0px | 0px → 380px |
| parser | light | 280.0px | 380.0px | 380.0px | 0px → 380px |
| plsql | light | 280.0px | 380.0px | 380.0px | 0px → 380px |
| jar | dark | 280.0px | 380.0px | 380.0px | 0px → 380px |
| parser | dark | 280.0px | 380.0px | 380.0px | 0px → 380px |
| plsql | dark | 280.0px | 380.0px | 380.0px | 0px → 380px |

Every drag moved the panel by exactly the mouse delta, persisted across a real page reload, and the
existing collapse button still worked correctly alongside the new handle (collapses to 0px,
re-expands to the resized 380px, not back to the 280px CSS default). Screenshots captured for every
row above (before-drag, after-drag, after-reload); `parser`/`plsql` dark-theme after-drag
screenshots additionally show the real loaded analysis data (114 procedures, call hierarchy, stats)
rendering correctly at the new width, not a blank/broken layout.

**Not done / known gaps.** `jar/js/cross-ref.js`'s `.cr-split-left`/`.cr-split-right` (Cross
Reference modal) was found in the initial sweep but not wired — its panels are rebuilt via
`innerHTML` template strings on every modal open, which `install()`'s one-time `querySelector` call
doesn't naturally re-attach to; wiring it correctly needs a call to `install()` (or an equivalent
re-run) at the modal's own render point, not just at page load, and was left out rather than bolted
on without verifying it against a real re-render. Flagged here rather than silently dropped.

**Files changed:**
- `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/shared/resizable-panel.js` (new)
- `unified-web/src/main/resources/static/shared/resizable-panel.css` (new)
